info.title: Cloud World Model — Agent API
info.description: Agent-facing discovery API for Cloud World Model: 54 operations across 50 paths, including 48 metered operations with x402 prices and six operations without a per-call x402 price (wallet challenge and verification, scenario listing, x402 configuration, analysis-job lookup, and AI-job cancellation). Some read and status operations are metered; do not assume all reads are free. Check each operation's x402 price or GET /billing/x402/config for current prices. Anonymous callers can pay for metered requests with USDC on Base via `X-PAYMENT`, or optional Solana USDC via `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` when advertised by the config endpoint — no account or API key is required for x402 payment.

post.summary: Generate an EIP-191 sign-in challenge
post.description:
Issues a one-time nonce for the given EVM wallet address. The caller must
sign the returned `message` string with `personal_sign` (EIP-191) and
submit the hex signature to `POST /wallet-auth/verify` within 5 minutes.

Rate-limited to 10 requests per IP per minute to prevent nonce-farming.
No authentication required.

walletAddress.description: The EVM wallet address requesting a sign-in challenge

nonce.description: The random hex nonce (32 hex chars)

message.description: The full message string to sign with personal_sign
message.example:
Sign in to Cloud World Model
Nonce: a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6
Expires: 2026-01-01T00:05:00.000Z

expiresAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the nonce expires (5 minutes)

429.description: Rate limit exceeded — 10 challenges per IP per minute

post.summary: Generate a session token from an EIP-191 signature
post.description:
Verifies the EIP-191 personal_sign signature for the challenge previously
issued by `POST /wallet-auth/challenge`. On success, returns a 24-hour
JWT session token.

Use the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on `GET /simulations`
and `GET /simulations/{simulationId}` to list and retrieve simulations
claimed by this wallet address without a traditional API key.

The nonce is single-use and consumed on successful verification.
No authentication required.

walletAddress.description: The EVM wallet address that signed the challenge

signature.description: Hex-encoded EIP-191 signature from personal_sign (0x-prefixed, 65 bytes)

post.summary: Generate a wallet session JWT via x402 micro-payment
post.description:
Issues a 24-hour wallet session JWT in exchange for a small USDC
micro-payment on Base (x402 protocol).  Designed for managed/MPC
wallets that cannot sign EIP-191 challenges directly.

**Flow:**
1. Call this endpoint with no `X-PAYMENT` header — the server returns
   `402 Payment Required` with the USDC amount and payment details.
2. Submit the x402 payment and resend the request with the
   `X-PAYMENT` header populated.
3. On success the response body includes both a `settlement` block
   (confirmed transaction hash) and a `walletSession` block
   containing the JWT token and its expiry.

The issuance is idempotent per transaction hash — replaying the same
transaction hash returns the same session: the returned token carries
the same `jti` (session nonce) as the original issuance. No new
session record is created. The token's `iat`/`exp` timestamps differ
between calls (each JWT is freshly signed), but the session identity
bound by `jti` is stable across all replays of the same hash.

**Token lifetime and persistence:** Tokens are valid for 24 hours and
reusable across requests until they expire. Token validity **survives
server restarts only when the `WALLET_AUTH_JWT_SECRET` environment
variable is set to a stable, persistent value**. Without it, an
ephemeral per-process secret is used and all sessions are invalidated
on every redeploy. The server logs a startup warning when this variable
is absent.

**Authentication:** x402 micro-payment only (no API key required).

200.description: Session JWT issued alongside x402 settlement

walletSession.description:
Issued wallet session JWT (24-hour TTL). Tokens are reusable
across requests until expiry. Token validity survives server
restarts only when the `WALLET_AUTH_JWT_SECRET` environment
variable is set to a stable, persistent value — without it
sessions are invalidated on every redeploy.

token.description: JWT session token (HS256, 24-hour TTL, reusable until expiry)

get.summary: Search available simulation templates
get.description:
Returns the list of pre-built infrastructure scenario templates. Scenarios
define a complete simulation configuration (resources, traffic, connections)
that can be loaded directly into a new simulation via the browser UI or the
API.

Optional filters narrow the catalog by provider, category, and difficulty.
Omit all filters to receive the complete, unfiltered scenario catalog.
Category matching is case-insensitive.

**No authentication required.**

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Return scenarios containing resources from this cloud provider.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description:
Return scenarios in this category. Matching is case-insensitive.
Supported catalog categories are cost, failure, networking, reliability,
and scaling.

parameters.name: difficulty
parameters.description: Return scenarios at this difficulty level.

get.summary: Fetch x402 pricing and payment configuration
get.description:
Returns the x402 payment configuration for this server, including canonical
`paymentOptions`, the legacy Base-primary fields, facilitator URL, and per-call-type
price table. Base USDC is the primary option. Solana USDC-SPL is an additional option
only when it appears in `paymentOptions`; it does not replace the Base option.

AI agents can use this endpoint to discover whether x402 anonymous pay-per-request is
enabled, choose an advertised network, and obtain the exact USDC amounts required before
sending the option's required payment header (`X-PAYMENT` for Base or
`PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` for optional Solana) to a metered endpoint.

This endpoint requires no authentication and is always public.

enabled.description: Whether x402 pay-per-request is active on this server.

network.description: Blockchain network where payments are accepted.

asset.description: USDC contract address on the configured network.

payTo.description: EVM wallet address that receives payments (null when disabled).

paymentOptions.description:
Canonical list of payment methods that can satisfy a live 402 challenge.
Base is listed first when x402 is enabled. Solana is listed only when its
recipient wallet is configured, as an additional option rather than a
replacement for Base.

network.description: CAIP-2 network identifier, matching a 402 `accepts[].network` value.

asset.description: USDC token contract or mint address on `network`.

payTo.description: Recipient wallet address on `network`, matching a 402 `accepts[].payTo` value.

header.description: Required request header containing the signed x402 payment payload.

feePayer.description: Solana-only PayAI wallet that sponsors the transaction fee; absent for Base.

solana.description: Legacy optional Solana payment details. Prefer `paymentOptions` for new integrations.

facilitatorUrl.description: Base URL of the x402 facilitator used to verify payments.

creditsPerUsdc.description: How many platform credits equal 1 USDC (determines price per credit).

credits.description: Number of platform credits consumed per call.

usdcAtomicUnits.description: Payment amount in USDC atomic units (6-decimal integer string).

simulationRetentionDays.description:
Number of days an x402-wallet-owned simulation is retained after its
last activity (step, update). Every `/step-hybrid` call on a simulation
resets this rolling window. After the window expires, the simulation and
all its metrics are permanently deleted by the server's cleanup sweep.

autoClaimOnFirstStep.description:
When `true`, an unclaimed (demo) simulation is automatically assigned to
the paying wallet's ownership on its first x402-authenticated
`/step-hybrid` call. No explicit claim endpoint is required.

post.summary: Create a cloud simulation
post.description:
Creates a simulation with cloud resources (compute, network, database, storage).
The simulation serves as the environment for RL training.

**Ownership:** If an `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header is provided, the
new simulation is immediately assigned to that API key and is fully write-accessible
without any additional steps. Without authentication the simulation is created
as a "demo" simulation (`apiKeyId: null`), subject to a 20-step limit; use
`POST /simulations/{simulationId}/claim` to adopt it once you have a key.

scenarioId.description: Live scenario identifier from the scenario catalog; mutually exclusive with resources and connections

scenarioOverrides.description:
Scenario-only customization. Requires scenarioId and must not
be combined with resources or connections. Select exactly one
override supported by the selected catalog scenario.

startupSeconds.description: Catalog EKS Spot startup duration in seconds

includeTrafficRecovery.description: Include the catalog Web App Autoscaling Traffic Recovery phase in the replay input before the first step.

description.example: Multi-tier web application with load balancer and database

resources.description: Cloud resources in the simulation; mutually exclusive with scenarioId

maxInstances.description:
Optional ceiling on the autoscaled compute fleet size, stored as
`autoscalingConfig.maxInstances` and enforced by the engine's
autoscale cap logic. If omitted, the provider default applies
(AWS 50, GCP 15, Azure/OCI/DigitalOcean 10) — which may be much
larger than your intended fleet size.

minInstances.description:
Optional floor on the autoscaled compute fleet size, stored as
`autoscalingConfig.minInstances`.

autoscalingTargetCpu.description: Canonical CPU HPA scale-out target. This targeted override wins over the provider default while CWM synthesizes all unrelated autoscaling defaults. If more than one supported target name is sent, every value must agree. Simulation-wide by default: sent at this top level, the engine applies one CPU threshold identically to every resource's scale decision. To override the threshold for ONE resource only, nest the same canonical name (or one of its three aliases) under that resource's `characteristics` as `scaleOutCpuThreshold` instead — every other resource keeps using the simulation-wide default. A misplaced or misnamed CPU-target field name (e.g. `autoscalingTargetCpuPercent`, `targetCPUUtilizationPercentage`) is rejected with 400 at either level, never silently dropped and defaulted.

ecsCpuTargetTracking.description: Opt in to ECS Fargate CPU-only target tracking. Requires an AWS Fargate compute resource. Uses autoscalingTargetCpu as the target; latency and throughput do not trigger ECS scaling. The effective policy is persisted on resource.characteristics.applicationAutoscalingPolicy.

scaleOutCooldownSeconds.description: ECS CPU target-tracking scale-out cooldown in simulated seconds; requires ecsCpuTargetTracking.

scaleInCooldownSeconds.description: ECS CPU target-tracking scale-in cooldown in simulated seconds; requires ecsCpuTargetTracking.

simulationSecondsPerStep.description: Simulated seconds per step for ECS cooldowns (default 1); requires ecsCpuTargetTracking.

resilienceConfig.description:
Optional retry/cascade resilience model. When present, the step engine
models retry amplification, circuit-breaker state, rate limiting, and
cascading-failure depth across declared `dependencies`. Set an edge's
timeout and retry count at
`resilienceConfig.dependencies[].retryPolicy.timeoutMs` and
`resilienceConfig.dependencies[].retryPolicy.maxRetries`. The same
policy accepts backoffMs, backoffMultiplier, jitterRatio,
retryBudgetRatio, retryBudgetRps, and retryActorId. Omitted values
retain defaults (timeoutMs 2000, maxRetries 2). Omit resilienceConfig
to leave the resilience model disabled (byte-identical to existing behavior).

value.name: AWS Production Web App
value.description: Multi-tier web application on AWS with load balancer and RDS

value.name: DO Production Web App
value.description: Multi-tier web application on DigitalOcean with Droplets, Managed PostgreSQL, Spaces, and Load Balancer

digitalOceanTrafficSpike.summary: DigitalOcean traffic spike — triggers DOKS HPA Droplet scale-out

value.name: DO Traffic Spike Autoscaling
value.description:
Demonstrates DigitalOcean DOKS Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) scaling
Droplets during a sudden traffic surge. Starting traffic (80 000 RPS) is
deliberately above the capacity of a single s-2vcpu-4gb Droplet to
guarantee that CPU breaches the 75 % HPA threshold and triggers automatic
Droplet provisioning within one simulation step (150 s cooldown window).
Run the simulation and observe DOKS HPA scale-out events in the event log.

effectiveMaxInstances.description:
The autoscaled fleet-size ceiling the engine will enforce —
`autoscalingConfig.maxInstances` when set, otherwise the
primary provider's default (AWS 50, GCP 15,
Azure/OCI/DigitalOcean 10).

effectiveMinInstances.description:
The autoscaled fleet-size floor the engine will enforce —
`autoscalingConfig.minInstances` when set, otherwise the
primary provider's default.

get.summary: List simulations for the authenticated caller
get.description:
Returns simulations owned by the authenticated caller.

**API key callers:** Returns all simulations assigned to the API key.
Admin-scoped keys receive all simulations across all keys.

**Wallet session callers:** Returns simulations claimed by the wallet
address (where `ownerWallet` matches), paginated via `limit` and `offset`
query parameters and sorted by `updatedAt` descending. The response shape
differs — it is an object `{ simulations, total, limit, offset }` rather
than a plain array.

Requires `read` scope or a valid wallet session JWT.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of simulations to return (wallet session only)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of simulations to skip (wallet session only)

total.description: Total simulations matching the wallet address

get.summary: Fetch a simulation by ID
get.description:
Returns the full state of a simulation including its resources,
current time step, traffic load, and autoscaling history.
Requires `read` scope and ownership.

403.description: Access denied — caller does not own this simulation

get.summary: Fetch the latest per-resource cost breakdown
get.description:
Returns the per-resource hourly cost array from the simulation's most
recent metrics record, joined with each resource's current status and
serving state. `status` is raw health severity/cooldown; use
`availabilityState`, `isRoutable`, and `routedRps` to determine whether
the resource is currently serving. A critical resource may therefore be
`availabilityState: degraded` with `isRoutable: true` after it rejoins
routing. Use this after a failure or traffic surge to identify resources
that continue billing while genuinely unavailable ("residual" spend).

`totalCostPerHour` is the exact sum of all `resources[].costPerHour`
values. The response is always a flat array (no paging, no metrics
history), making it cheap to call between scenario steps.

Aurora Serverless v2 rows identify writer/reader role, reader scaling
mode, billable ACU and the per-ACU-hour rate. An unavailable quick-failure
writer retains its pre-failure allocated ACU in this model; this is a
modeling assumption, not a claim that AWS bills a failed instance like
a stopped cluster. AWS distinguishes stopped clusters from running
instances: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-cluster-stop-start.html
(reviewed 2026-09-25). Aurora capacity/reader behavior:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html
(reviewed 2026-09-25).

OpenShift rows retain their billing metadata. For ARO, compare like-for-like
units: `publishedUnitRatePerHour` is the official `$0.171/hour` rate per
4-vCPU billing unit, while `derivedPlatformFeePerHour` and `costPerHour`
are the topology-derived total. For example, three 2-vCPU workers produce
`effectiveWorkerVcpu: 6` and a `$0.2565/hour` platform total
(`publishedUnitRatePerHour × effectiveWorkerVcpu ÷ billingUnitVcpu`).
Platform, control-plane, and worker rows are separate additive entries;
the estimated control-plane charge must not be folded into the platform
unit comparison or added a second time.

Returns 404 when the simulation has not been stepped yet (no metrics
record exists). Requires `read` scope and ownership, or an x402
micro-payment (`simulation_cost_breakdown`, $0.0030).

stepIndex.description: Simulation step (metrics timestamp) the breakdown was computed at

totalCostPerHour.description: Exact sum of all resources[].costPerHour values (USD/hr)

residualCostPerHour.description: Exact subtotal of costPerHour for resources that are currently unavailable/parked or stopped. Healthy/degraded idle resources, including ALBs, are excluded.

residualCostDefinition.description: Explains which billed resources are included in residualCostPerHour; totalCostPerHour includes all billed resources.
residualCostDefinition.example: Unavailable, parked, or stopped resource costs only. Healthy or degraded idle resources, including ALBs, are excluded; totalCostPerHour remains the complete billed total.

scalingMode.description: Reader promotion tier 0/1 mirror or tier 2–15 independent mode.

billableAcu.description: Allocated ACU billed for this instance; frozen pre-failure ACU on modeled quick writer park.

ratePerAcuHour.description: Aurora per-instance ACU-hour rate derived from the authoritative AWS rate.

storageCostPerHour.description: RDS SQL Server allocated-storage component expressed as USD/hr.

storageGb.description: Normalized allocated RDS SQL Server storage in GiB.

status.description: Current resource status ("stopped" when billingState is stopped; "billed" for synthetic egress/data-transfer charges; "removed" when a real resource no longer exists)

availabilityState.description: Current serving classification for compute, Kubernetes, and database rows. `available` means healthy and serving; `degraded` means warning or critical severity while still serving; `unavailable` means a failed or parked resource is not serving. `scaled_to_zero` means an ECS Fargate service has no running tasks; `cold_start` means its tasks are starting and not yet routable. These Fargate lifecycle states are distinct from generic `unavailable`. Do not infer unavailability from status: critical alone.

isRoutable.description: Whether this resource is currently receiving routed traffic. True for available/degraded rows and false for unavailable, scaled_to_zero, or cold_start rows.

routedRps.description: Current routed requests per second for tracked compute, Kubernetes, and database rows when available.

offering.description: OpenShift offering associated with this row, when the resource is an OpenShift overlay.

chargeType.description: OpenShift accounting component; platform, control-plane, and worker rows are additive.

pricingStatus.description: Provenance status for the pricing represented by this row.

pricingSource.description: Pricing source associated with this row.

effectiveDate.description: ISO date of the pricing evidence represented by this row.

referenceRegion.description: Region represented by the published pricing evidence.

pricingArithmetic.description: Published amount and conversion used for an OpenShift platform/license row.

billingUnit.description: Published OpenShift platform billing unit used before topology proration.

billingUnitVcpu.description: Number of worker vCPUs in one published billing unit; 4 for ARO.

publishedUnitRatePerHour.description: Published platform rate for one billing unit, before topology proration. For ARO this is $0.171/hour per 4 vCPU in the published East US reference.

effectiveWorkerCount.description: Total worker count represented by the derived OpenShift platform charge.

effectiveWorkerVcpu.description: Total worker vCPU-equivalents used to prorate the published platform unit.

derivedPlatformFeePerHour.description: Topology-derived platform charge; equals publishedUnitRatePerHour × effectiveWorkerVcpu ÷ billingUnitVcpu for ARO. For three 2-vCPU workers this is $0.2565/hour, not a second published rate.

workerTopology.description: Per-pool worker quantities used to derive the OpenShift platform charge.

403.description: Access denied — caller does not own this simulation

404.description: Simulation not found, or no metrics record exists yet (simulation not stepped)

post.summary: Simulate provider quotas, throttling, retries, and concurrency
post.description:
Use this operation for provider quotas, API throttling, retries,
backoff, queueing, worker/concurrency limits, and other control-plane
operations. It runs a bounded, synchronous workload through Cloud World
Model's deterministic provider-limit scheduler and models throttling,
queueing, throughput, completion, retries, timeouts, failures,
dependency blocking, and optional concurrency comparisons.

This is simulated provider-control-plane data, not a provider SDK or a
live quota lookup. It never calls AWS, Azure, GCP, DigitalOcean, OCI,
or any other provider API, discovers negotiated quotas, creates
resources, persists the workload, or changes the simulation's resource
graph or /step state. Provider throttling in the result is distinct
from CWM's own HTTP 429/rate-limit middleware. Use resource `/step` for
cloud workload behavior and use `/simulations/stateless` for the
separate stateless resource simulation; neither substitutes for this
provider-limit operation.

Supply one service per request: the top-level `service` applies to
every operation group in the DAG. To compare services, submit separate
requests. Supported exact provider/service/operation/category tuples
resolve with `result.policyResolutions[].policySource` set to
`catalog_default`; unsupported tuples return `unsupported_policy`
without a scoped caller override.

Execution is protected by a 2-second wall-clock deadline and a
process-local admission limit of two concurrent runs. Identical active
or recently interrupted workloads, and workloads submitted while
execution capacity is full, are rejected with HTTP 409 and must not be
automatically retried. Deadline expiry is an HTTP 422 non-retryable
failure.

Catalog defaults cover `aws.ec2.mutating-api` (`service: ec2`,
`operation: mutating`, `category: compute`), AWS Elastic Load Balancing
v1 and v2 (`service: elbv1` or `elbv2`, `category: network`), and Azure
Resource Manager read/write buckets. For each ELB service the exact
supported operations are `resource-intensive`, `registration`,
`non-mutating`, and `mutating`, yielding `aws.elbv1.resource-intensive`,
`aws.elbv1.registration`, `aws.elbv1.non-mutating`,
`aws.elbv1.mutating`, `aws.elbv2.resource-intensive`,
`aws.elbv2.registration`, `aws.elbv2.non-mutating`, and
`aws.elbv2.mutating`. These are documented API action categories,
not arbitrary AWS action names. Do not infer an ELB category for an
uncategorized action or interchange ELBv1 and ELBv2 buckets.
Aurora Serverless v1 Data API has two **independent** catalog models
(`service: rds-data-api-aurora-serverless-v1`, `category: database`):
`operation: requests-per-second` resolves
`aws.rds-data-api-aurora-serverless-v1.requests-per-second` (1,000
requests/second per account in the current Region);
`operation: concurrent-requests` resolves
`aws.rds-data-api-aurora-serverless-v1.concurrent-requests` (500
concurrent requests to ONE cluster using the SAME secret, with excess
requests queued). Do not interpret them as joint enforcement of one
workload. A request mixing these two selectors is rejected; send
separate requests and do not treat results as simultaneous enforcement.
Both require `quotaScope.account`; concurrency additionally
requires `quotaScope.resource`, an opaque cluster-secret-pair label,
never an actual secret. The rate model has no documented burst; its
fixed 1-second scheduler window approximates the AWS rate limit, not
AWS's documented timing. Source:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/CHAP_Limits.html
Generic RDS control-plane, Aurora Serverless v2 Data API, and
provisioned Aurora Data API are not covered by these selectors.
AWS IAM, generic RDS control-plane, EC2 Auto Scaling, Application Auto Scaling,
and S3 control-plane requests have no numeric scheduler-compatible
public baseline in this catalog. S3 object per-prefix throughput is
data-plane guidance, not a control-plane quota. Such tuples, as well
as GCP, DigitalOcean, and OCI tuples without a caller-supplied quota
override, return `unsupported_policy` rather than HTTP 429. Overrides must use a
concrete account, subscription, or project scope and include
caller-supplied provenance. The catalog policy source, documentation
reference, confidence, and as-of date are returned in `provenance`
and `result.policyResolutions`.

EC2 Auto Scaling (`service: ec2-auto-scaling`, `category: compute`) initially
models `DescribeAutoScalingGroups`, `DescribeScheduledActions`,
`CreateAutoScalingGroup`, `UpdateAutoScalingGroup`, `SetDesiredCapacity`,
and `DeleteAutoScalingGroup`. AWS documents one shared account API token
bucket, `RateExceeded` on throttle, and no public numeric capacity/refill
pair. Use one account/Region-scoped caller `operation: all` token-bucket
override with caller-verified burst capacity and refill for these six
operation groups. Put `operation: all` on the override policy and its
policy `scope`, not on the request's `quotaScope`; the latter can omit
`operation` for a mixed workload. They contend for the same bucket.
Other operations do not inherit this six-action override. Mark `throttled` retryable and
configure exponential backoff to model client retry behavior. This is
not an Auto Scaling resource/configuration quota or an EC2 API bucket.
AWS advises `IncludeInstances=false` for `DescribeAutoScalingGroups`
to omit instance details; this advice does not change modeled token
consumption, latency, or quota. See
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/APIReference/Welcome.html
and docs/aws-api-limit-evidence.md for the evidence gap.

`latency` is required because it is a Cloud World Model client-side
model input: provide measured client values when available. If no
measurements are available, use the canonical baseline
`meanMs: 40`, `p95Ms: 80`, and `timeoutMs: 5000` shown below. These
values are simulation guidance, not AWS service defaults and not a
live AWS latency claim. The same applies to every latency and retry
value in this operation.

For mixed workloads, each `result.policyResolutions` entry is keyed by
operation category, operation, and resource group (resource is omitted
when absent). Multiple operation IDs with the same three values share
one resolution. Its `accounting` counts that group's planned units,
attempts, retries, throttles, and completions; summing these fields
across resolutions gives the corresponding `result.accounting` totals.
Attempts count initial and retry attempts, while retries and throttles
can count the same work, so do not sum different fields together.
For the `mixedAwsEc2Groups` request example below, the modeled result
contains this fragment (other result fields are omitted):

```json
{
  "policyResolutions": [
    {"operationCategory":"compute","operation":"mutating","resource":"fleet-a","policySource":"catalog_default","accounting":{"plannedOperations":3,"attemptedOperations":3,"retryOperations":0,"throttledOperations":0,"completedOperations":3,"denominator":"planned_operations"}},
    {"operationCategory":"compute","operation":"mutating","resource":"fleet-b","policySource":"catalog_default","accounting":{"plannedOperations":2,"attemptedOperations":2,"retryOperations":0,"throttledOperations":0,"completedOperations":2,"denominator":"planned_operations"}}
  ],
  "accounting": {"plannedOperations":5,"attemptedOperations":5,"retryOperations":0,"throttledOperations":0,"completedOperations":5,"failedOperations":0,"timedOutOperations":0,"dependencyBlockedOperations":0,"unsupportedOperations":0,"pendingOperations":0,"terminalOperations":5,"denominator":"planned_operations"}
}
```

Omitting `retry` selects the one-attempt, no-backoff baseline:
`maxAttempts: 1`, `baseBackoffMs: 0`, `maxBackoffMs: 0`,
`backoffMultiplier: 2`, `jitterRatio: 0`, and no retryable outcomes.
The retry object models caller/client behavior; it does not describe
AWS retry defaults or an AWS SDK configuration.

Bounds: up to 256 operation groups, 100,000 aggregate planned units
across all distinct concurrency-sweep runs, 500,000 estimated attempts
(aggregate planned units multiplied by `retry.maxAttempts`), 1,000
workers, 1,000 concurrency, 16 concurrency sweep values, 10 retry
attempts, and 1,000,000 scheduler events. Aggregate work-budget checks
run before authentication billing or demo-quota consumption and return
HTTP 413 when exceeded. Results with more than 1,000 planned operations
omit per-unit detail: `result.operations` is empty and
`result.outputDetail` is `summary_only`. This endpoint is a modeled
simulation, not a provider SDK or drop-in provider API.

parameters.name: simulationId
parameters.description: Owned simulation UUID used for access control and result context; workload state is not persisted.

contractVersion.description: Version of the provider API-limit simulation input contract.

provider.description: Cloud provider whose modeled API quota policy will be applied.

region.description: Provider region used to resolve regional quota policies.

service.description: Provider service whose API operations will be simulated.

operations.description:
DAG operation groups. Each item has id, operation, category,
plannedCount (1..100,000), optional resource, and
dependsOn IDs. The aggregate planned count is bounded at
100,000.

id.description: Unique identifier for this operation group and its dependencies.

operation.description: Provider operation class or operation name used to select applicable quota policies.

category.description: Service category used to resolve provider API-limit policies.

plannedCount.description: Number of operations in this group to schedule.

items.description: ID of a prerequisite operation group.

resource.description: Optional opaque resource label used to match resource-scoped quota policies.

workerCount.description: Number of simulated workers issuing the planned operations.

maxConcurrency.description: Maximum simultaneous in-flight operations scheduled across workers.

values.description: Concurrency levels at which to repeat the modeled workload.

items.description: A distinct number of simultaneous in-flight operations to evaluate.

latency.description: Required caller-supplied latency assumptions used by the scheduler.

meanMs.description: Caller-supplied mean operation latency in milliseconds.

p95Ms.description: Caller-supplied P95 operation latency in milliseconds.

jitterMs.description: Maximum modeled latency variation in milliseconds.

quotaScope.description: Scope dimensions; region and service must match the request. Aurora Serverless v1 Data API requires account for both selectors; concurrent-requests additionally requires resource as an opaque cluster-secret-pair label, never an actual secret.

quotaOverrides.description: Caller-supplied policy overrides with concrete account, subscription, or project scope. Optional concurrencyOverflow queue/reject applies to concurrency ceilings; absent retains reject behavior.

concurrencyOverflow.description: Optional concurrency-ceiling overflow behavior; absent retains reject behavior.

post.summary: Create an RL training environment
post.description:
Creates a reinforcement learning environment for training agents.
Links to an existing simulation and configures episode parameters.

This endpoint works with simulations built on **any supported provider**,
including AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and **DigitalOcean**. Training an agent against
a DigitalOcean simulation lets you learn optimal autoscaling strategies for
Droplet-based workloads, Managed Database failover handling, and
multi-datacenter traffic routing — all without incurring real cloud costs.
The observation space, action space, and reward function are identical
regardless of provider.

**Idle TTL:** Authenticated RL environments expire after **2 hours of inactivity**
(no `step` or `reset` call received). Expired environments and their linked
simulations are removed automatically; subsequent requests return `404`. Reset the
idle timer by calling `POST /rl/environments/{environmentId}/step` or
`POST /rl/environments/{environmentId}/reset` at least once every 2 hours during
long training runs.

**Note:** In-memory deployments (the default) do not persist RL environments
across server restarts. Reconnect or recreate the environment after a restart.

**UI Status Viewer:** Once an environment is running you can monitor its episodes,
cumulative rewards, and health without writing code — open the
[RL Environment Status viewer](/admin/rl-environments) in the platform UI and enter
your API key to see all active environments at a glance.

    "simulationId": "a638caad-7423-40a3-bb09-f91235d9392d",

      "maxSteps": 200,
      "targetTrafficPattern": "wave",
      "initialTraffic": 1500,

      "costBudgetPerHour": 3.50,

  }'

post.summary: Run a stateless synchronous cloud simulation
post.description:
Executes a tightly bounded cloud scenario entirely in memory through the
production hybrid, pricing, failure, and autoscaling engine paths. No
simulation, metric, event, result, ownership, or job record is created.
The same seed and input produce the same result. This REST-only operation
requires write scope via a bearer key or one x402 payment; MCP transport
is intentionally omitted because it cannot preserve payment challenge,
settlement, and replay semantics end to end.

seed.description: Deterministic seed for reproducible execution with identical input.

steps.description: Number of simulation steps to execute synchronously.

resources.description: Required resource graph to model; each resource needs an ID, name, type, and provider.

id.description: Unique caller-supplied identifier used to connect and target this resource.

name.description: Human-readable resource name shown in simulation results.

provider.description: Cloud provider whose resource and pricing model to use.

characteristics.description: Optional provider-specific sizing and behavior settings for this resource.

instanceType.description: Compatibility alias for size. If size is omitted, this value is canonicalized into size; if both are supplied they must match, with size remaining canonical.

size.description: Provider size or SKU used to resolve modeled capacity and hourly price.

serviceFamily.description: Provider service family used to select resource-specific behavior and rates.

maxThroughput.description: Optional modeled maximum request throughput for the resource.

baseLatency.description: Optional baseline request latency in milliseconds.

costMultiplier.description: Optional multiplier applied to the resource's modeled hourly cost.

maxConnections.description: Maximum concurrent database connections used for pool-capacity modeling.

connectionDemand.description: Optional database connection-demand model. Declared counts are ASSUMPTION / plan-time budgets, not live connection observations. Omission preserves the load-derived behavior. Over-budget declared demand adds a bounded rule-based pool-saturation error signal; it is not a provider-calibrated rate. The optional saturationErrorThreshold suppresses the load-derived pool error below the configured utilization without changing connection capacity.

mode.description: load-derived uses the existing RPS-derived estimate; declared ignores instantaneous RPS; max uses the greatest of load-derived and declared/floor demand.

saturationErrorThreshold.description: Optional threshold for the load-derived pool error curve. Below it, connection-pool saturation adds no errors; above it, the curve rises with utilization beyond the threshold. When multiple databases exist, set the same value on all of them for this override to apply. Does not change connection capacity.

declaredConnections.description: ASSUMPTION / plan-time peak pool budget, e.g. replicas × per-pod pool size; not observed live DB connections.

idlePoolFloor.description: ASSUMPTION / plan-time minimum idle pool footprint; not observed live DB connections.

minNodes.description: Minimum Kubernetes worker-node count when autoscaling is enabled.

maxNodes.description: Maximum Kubernetes worker-node count when autoscaling is enabled.

autoscaling.description: Whether the resource may scale within its configured bounds.

connections.description: Optional directed resource links; each connection identifies a source and target resource.

autoscaling.description: Optional compute fleet autoscaling bounds and CPU target.

post.summary: Run one hybrid ML and rules simulation step
post.description:
Steps the simulation using the Hybrid Prediction Engine, which blends a
deterministic rule-based simulation with a simulated ML-based prediction.
The engine uses a confidence threshold to decide how much weight to give
each path, and falls back to pure rules when ML confidence is low.

Returns the updated simulation state, step metrics, events, the hybrid
decision record (including ML confidence and blending rationale), and the
updated cumulative hybrid result object.

Requires `write` scope and ownership.

steps.description:
Number of time steps to advance in a single call (1–500, default 1).
Each sub-step evaluates traffic patterns at the correct elapsed time,
so a ramp or wave pattern reaches the same final value whether driven
as N×1 individual calls or a single batch call of N.

mlWeight.description: Weight given to ML prediction vs rule-based (0 = pure rules, 1 = pure ML)

confidenceThreshold.description: Minimum ML confidence to apply blending; below this threshold pure rules are used

scenarioHash.description: Canonical SHA-256 of the persisted scenario graph and attached traffic-pattern order.

effectiveConfigHash.description: Versioned prediction SHA-256 over the replay startup-input hash, engine version, and calibration identity. The original replay-only hash remains at replayIdentity.effectiveConfigHash.

predictionEffectiveConfigHash.description: Engine-versioned prediction identity, separate from the replay-input identity.

engineVersion.description: Simulation engine version used to produce the prediction.

metrics.description: Metrics snapshot for this step. `throughput` is successful throughput (goodput). The normal simulation engine emits `offeredRps` on the final top-level step result as the aggregate original-client offered load for the same step/window. Legacy persisted histories may omit it; it is never derived from retry/path/per-resource figures.

timestamp.description: Simulation timestamp for this metric snapshot (seconds)

latencyP50.description: Median latency (ms), or null when no serving-tier latency distribution is modeled.

latencyP95.description: P95 latency (ms), or null when no serving-tier latency distribution is modeled.

latencyP99.description: Modeled 99th-percentile latency in milliseconds, or null when no serving-tier latency distribution is modeled. Interpret with latencyP99Basis and predictionEvidence.latencyP99 for the P99-specific basis and evidence level / assumption range.

latencyPercentileStatus.description: Whether P50/P95/P99 are supported by a modeled serving-tier latency distribution.

latencyP99Basis.description: Percentile-specific P99 basis: owned in-VPC internal-ALB fit, scaled from that fit (not directly measured), or uncalibrated generic model. Historical metric rows may omit this field.

latencyBasis.description: General modeled latency path/boundary (for example, in-VPC load-balancer or end-to-end model). Use latencyP99Basis for percentile-specific P99 provenance.

engineVersion.description: Simulation engine version used to produce this metric.

predictionEffectiveConfigHash.description: Engine-versioned prediction identity, separate from replay identity.

throughput.description: Completed request rate in RPS; may exceed offeredRps during backlog drain, with queued completions identified in applicationQueue.

backlogDrainRps.description: Completed request rate above this interval's offeredRps, explicitly attributed to backlog drain.

offeredRps.description: Aggregate original-client request rate offered to the simulation for this step/window (RPS). The normal simulation engine emits this on the final top-level step result and persists it with current metric history; legacy histories may omit it. Never infer from retry/path/per-resource figures.

modeledShedRps.description: Aggregate request rate shed by modeled capacity limits for this step/window (RPS). Optional: emitted only when complete aggregate capacity evidence exists, never fabricated from goodput or error rate, and distinct from application errors.

type.description: Stable event discriminator for this step event.

coverageSummary.description:
Resource/behavior and base-rate coverage summary for this hybrid step —
what CWM could model deterministically, what it estimated, and what it
could not see at all. `level` never means complete economic or invoice
coverage; inspect `billingPolicyCoverage` separately. Shares are of
SIMULATED cost, never a real bill; known
gaps are listed by name with a zero share. Also persisted on each
decision in the cumulative hybrid result.

**Share distribution:** `shareOfSimulatedCost` values do NOT necessarily
sum to 1.0. When an unrecognized SKU is present its share is deliberately
forced to 0. Use `modeledCostShareOfTotal` as the authoritative denominator.

level.description:
Resource/behavior fidelity only. Deterministic rules — "full": every resource is modeled and no
not-observable category applies; "limited": at least one
not-observable category applies to this resource mix; "partial":
anything estimated or a known gap, but nothing not-observable.

modeledCostShareOfTotal.description: Sum of shareOfSimulatedCost ONLY for rows with costFidelity "modeled" (deterministically simulated resources). Rows with estimated or known_gap fidelity are excluded because their cost is an approximation. Always present (0 for zero-resource or all-estimated topologies). Authoritative Trust Layer denominator: values in (0, 1] indicate the fraction of simulated cost backed by fully-modeled resources. A value well below 1.0 (e.g. 0.0166) signals that most simulated cost is in unsupported or estimated resources. Consistent across all decision objects in a session for topologies with the same resource mix. Measures rule-coverage completeness, not billing accuracy. A value near 1.0 means nearly all simulated cost is backed by deterministic rules; it is not evidence that the cost figures match a real billing statement or that discounts, support charges, and marketplace fees are included.

notObservableCategories.description: Topology-specific dimensions CWM cannot observe about THIS simulation's environment. Distinct from structuralLimitations. An empty array is valid and intentional — it means no not-observable predicates fired for this topology (not a defect).

structuralLimitations.description: Permanent model-level exclusions for the providers present in the resource mix (e.g. IAM, CloudWatch metering, AWS Support). Semantically separate from notObservableCategories: these describe limits of the simulation model, not of this particular topology. Consistent across all decision objects within a session (same providers → same structural exclusions).

billingPolicyCoverage.description: Economic billing-policy dimension, separate from resource behavior and base-rate fidelity. An RDS resource always lists RDS Extended Support as an unpriced exclusion; CWM does not estimate that surcharge.

resourceType.description: Resource type, or "cost_category" for category rows.

costFidelity.description: Coverage fidelity for the cost dimension of this resource. "modeled" = Backed by deterministic CWM pricing rules using public list rates. Modeled does not mean billing-validated — real invoices may differ due to committed-use discounts, support surcharges, marketplace fees, and on-demand price changes since the last benchmark calibration. "estimated" = approximated via ML-blend or extrapolation. "known_gap" = resource exists in the topology but cost is not modeled. "not_observable" = CWM has no visibility into this charge category.

shareOfSimulatedCost.description: Share (0–1) of total simulated cost. May be deliberately 0 when the SKU is unrecognized (see shareExcluded). Does NOT necessarily sum to 1.0 — use modeledCostShareOfTotal as the authoritative denominator.

shareExcluded.description: Present and true when shareOfSimulatedCost is deliberately zeroed because the resource's declared SKU/basis is unrecognized or unsupported. Absent (or false) for resources whose zero share is legitimate (e.g. free-tier or zero-cost resources).

reason.example: CPU, latency, autoscaling, warm-up, and hourly cost follow deterministic provider-calibrated rules.

expiresAt.description:
Present only on x402 (wallet-paying) calls. ISO-8601 timestamp when
ownership (and the simulation itself) expires. Reset to now+90 days on
every successful step-hybrid call.

ownership.description:
Present only on x402 (wallet-paying) calls. Describes the wallet
that owns this simulation and when that ownership expires.

type.description: Ownership type — always "wallet" for x402 callers.

wallet.description: Normalized Ethereum wallet address that owns this simulation.

expiresAt.description:
ISO-8601 timestamp when ownership (and the simulation itself)
expires. Reset to now+90 days on every successful step-hybrid call.

409.description: Simulation already owned by another wallet or API key

message.example: This simulation is owned by a different wallet.

post.summary: Submit a deterministic traffic injection for a simulation
post.description:
Changes the simulation's traffic level in a single call. Supply
`targetRps` or `deltaPercent` for deterministic, reproducible results
(recommended for agents and controlled scenarios):

- **`targetRps`** (absolute, recommended) — sets traffic to exactly this
  value (clamped 1–500 000 RPS). Takes precedence over `deltaPercent`.
  Response `mode: "target_rps"`.
- **`deltaPercent`** (relative, recommended) — new traffic is
  `currentTraffic × (1 + deltaPercent/100)`, rounded (e.g. `75` turns
  400 RPS into 700 RPS). Response `mode: "delta_percent"`.
- **`random: true`** (explicit random spike) — injects a large random
  spike of +30 000–50 000 RPS on top of current traffic
  (`mode: "random_spike"`; if a ramp pattern is active the call instead
  advances it by one increment, `mode: "ramp_increment"`). Not suitable
  for controlled scenarios or reproducible runs — use only when an
  uncontrolled spike is intentional.

When `targetRps` or `deltaPercent` is supplied, any active traffic
patterns are **deactivated** (their names are echoed in
`deactivatedPatterns`) so the injected level persists across subsequent
`step` calls instead of being pulled back toward a pattern target.
If the first simulation step has finalized replay identity, a controlled
traffic override is rejected with `409 Conflict` when an active traffic
pattern would need to be deactivated. Edit traffic patterns before the
first step; replay identity finalization cannot be bypassed.

Every response echoes the applied outcome:
`{ previousRps, appliedRps, mode, requestedTargetRps?, requestedDeltaPercent? }`.

**Unknown fields are rejected before payment settlement** — if the request body
contains any field other than `targetRps`, `deltaPercent`, or `random` (for
example the common agent mistakes `multiplier`, `factor`, or `spike`), the
endpoint returns a structured 400 with a hint naming the likely intended field
and, when the value is numeric, the equivalent `deltaPercent` expression. An
empty body `{}` also returns 400 with a hint naming all three valid patterns.
No USDC charge is settled on a 400 response.

Requires `write` scope and ownership.

targetRps.description: Absolute traffic target in RPS. Takes precedence over deltaPercent. Deactivates any active traffic patterns so the level persists across steps.

deltaPercent.description: Relative traffic change in percent (e.g. 75 = +75% of current traffic). Ignored when targetRps is supplied.

random.description: Set to `true` to explicitly opt into random spike selection. Mutually exclusive with targetRps and deltaPercent.

requestedTargetRps.description: Echo of the targetRps request field (present only when supplied)

requestedDeltaPercent.description: Echo of the deltaPercent request field (present only when supplied)

deactivatedPatterns.description: Names of traffic patterns deactivated by a controlled inject (present only when patterns were active)

400.description: Invalid request body — e.g. `targetRps` out of range (1–500 000), `deltaPercent` ≤ −100, an unknown field, or an empty body `{}` (must supply at least one of `targetRps`, `deltaPercent`, or `random: true`). The response body contains a structured `FieldError` (or array of `FieldError` objects) so agents can programmatically identify the rejected field and self-correct.

409.description:
Replay identity is finalized and an active traffic pattern would
need to be deactivated for this controlled override. The traffic
override is rejected; replay identity finalization cannot be bypassed.

post.summary: Start a rolling ECS Fargate deployment
post.description:
Starts a rolling replacement of all running tasks in an `ecsFargate`
resource. Tasks are replaced in batches of `maxSurge`: each new batch
warms through `taskStartupSeconds` (the resource's configured startup
delay) before the corresponding old tasks begin draining through
`taskScaleDownSeconds`. During the drain window the ready new tasks
serve new connections while the old tasks finish existing ones, so
effective serving capacity is preserved throughout the deploy.

Progress is visible in subsequent `GET /simulations/{simulationId}`
responses under each resource's `metadata.fargateDeployReplacingCount`
and in `normalizedConfig.requestServing[].rollingDeploy` (present only

post.summary: Submit a targeted node failure injection
post.description:
Fails one resource in the simulation (marks it critical) and records an
error event.

Quick `inject-failure` uses the resource's bounded `failureParkSteps`
window (or `criticalSteps` when that field is omitted): the targeted
compute/Kubernetes node is unavailable and receives no routed traffic
during that window, then rejoins the routing pool automatically when
organic cooldown can resume. A targeted database is also unavailable
during its bounded park window. With no serving database and positive
offered traffic, the next step reports 100% errors, zero throughput,
and `errorBreakdown.dbFailure: 100`. If an AWS Aurora writer explicitly
declares a healthy related replica (`replicaOf` the writer) via
`characteristics.auroraStandbyResourceId`, the modeled first step
remains interrupted; on the second step the standby takes over and
`metrics.databases[].auroraFailover` reports the failed and standby
resource IDs, phase, and success. Promotion removes the writer-outage
penalty while the writer remains parked. `multiAz` or a second,
unrelated database alone does not prove a write-capable standby.
Each quick step is one modeled simulation second: the second-step
promotion is one second after injection, not 30 seconds. Chaos
`database_crash` instead samples at 10-second intervals with a default
30-second promotion and a 1800-second sole-writer restart after the
injection duration. Compare equivalent outage/serving phases, not
equal step indices or wall-clock times. These are deterministic
assumptions, not observed AWS failover timing.
Its original connection configuration is
restored after the window, followed by organic cooldown, or earlier
via `recover-resource`. Random selection remains compute/Kubernetes-only.
Network and other non-node resources cannot be quick-failed.
Authenticated callers can instead use `failure.create` with
`database_overload` for a typed database failure; this typed tool is
not available anonymously. This is different from the persistent
reversible `instance_down` failure created through `/failures`, which
remains unavailable until deactivated or recovered with
`recover-resource`; `instance_kill` permanently removes the resource.
Poll the step response or `GET /simulations/{simulationId}` for
`availabilityState`, `isRoutable`, `routedRps`, and `recoveryProgress`.
`failureParkSteps` must be a positive integer; an explicit zero is
rejected rather than treated as an ambiguous no-park mode.

**Targeting (recommended)** — pass `resourceId` or `resourceName`
(human-readable name; exact match preferred, an unambiguous prefix is
accepted) in the request body to fail a specific, named resource (e.g.
`{ "resourceName": "web-server-01" }`). This path is deterministic and
reproducible — use it for controlled scenarios, CI fault-tree runs, and
any case where a predictable outcome matters. If `resourceName` matches
more than one resource, a 400 is returned with a `candidates` list
naming every match so the caller can retry unambiguously. If the
resolved resource is not in a faileable state (already critical/warning),
a 400 describing its current status is returned.

**Random mode (opt-in)** — pass `{"random": true}` to explicitly select
a random healthy node via the simulation's RNG. This path is
**non-deterministic** and not suitable for controlled scenarios or CI
replay. Use it only when intentional random selection is explicitly
desired. An empty body `{}` returns 400 with a hint naming all three
valid patterns.

The response always echoes the applied outcome via
`resolvedResourceId`, `resolvedResourceName`, and `previousHealth` —
on the random path these are populated from whichever resource was
selected.

Returns 400 if no healthy nodes are available to fail.
For fine-grained control over failure type and duration, use
`POST /simulations/{simulationId}/failures` instead.

**Resource name discovery (agents: do this first)** — before calling this
endpoint, call `GET /simulations/{simulationId}` and read the top-level
`resources` array. Each element has an `id` and a `name` field. Use one of
those values as `resourceId` or `resourceName` in your request body. The
response also returns a `healthyNodes` array `[{id, name}, ...]` listing
every currently healthy resource, so you can update your inventory on each
call without a separate lookup.

**Unknown fields are rejected before payment settlement** — if the request body
contains any field other than `resourceId`, `resourceName`, or `random` (for
example the common agent mistake `targetResourceId`, `target`, or `resource`),
the endpoint returns a structured 400 with a "Did you mean" hint before any
USDC charge is settled. An empty body `{}` also returns 400 with a hint naming
all three valid patterns.

Requires `write` scope and ownership.

post.summary: Run an RL action and advance one step
post.description:
Executes an agent action, simulates one time step, and returns the next observation,
reward, and episode completion status. This is the core training loop interaction.

**Idle TTL:** Each successful step call resets the environment's 2-hour idle timer.
Environments that receive no `step` or `reset` calls for 2 hours are automatically
deactivated and their linked simulation artifacts removed. Subsequent requests to a
deactivated environment return `404`. Call `step` or `reset` at least once every
2 hours during long training runs to keep the environment alive.

Python – warm-up/training
x-codeSamples.source:
"""
Two-phase training loop: fast warm-up followed by fine-grained training.

Phase 1 – Warm-up (300 s ticks)
  Use large tick_seconds to fast-forward through startup noise before the
  agent starts making meaningful autoscaling decisions. Each step advances
  the simulation clock by 5 minutes, so 20 warm-up steps cover ~1.7 hours
  of simulated time in seconds of wall time.

Phase 2 – Training (60 s ticks)
  Switch to 1-minute ticks for precise autoscaling control. The agent now
  observes and reacts to traffic on a per-minute basis, matching the
  granularity of real autoscaling cooldown windows (e.g. AWS default: 300 s).
"""
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api"
API_KEY = "your-api-key"
ENV_ID = "env-aws-001"

session = requests.Session()
session.headers.update({"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"})

def step(action: dict, tick_seconds: int) -> dict:
    resp = session.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/rl/environments/{ENV_ID}/step",
        json={"action": action, "tick_seconds": tick_seconds},
    )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()

NO_OP = {"type": "no_op", "parameters": {}}

# --- Phase 1: Warm-up (300 s / 5-minute ticks) ---
WARMUP_STEPS = 20
print("=== Warm-up phase (300 s ticks) ===")
for i in range(WARMUP_STEPS):
    data = step(NO_OP, tick_seconds=300)
    print(
        f"  warmup {i+1:2d}/{WARMUP_STEPS}  "
        f"sim={data['sim_time_human']:>8s}  "
        f"cpu={data['obs']['cpu_util']:.1%}  "
        f"instances={data['obs']['instances']}"
    )
    if data["done"]:
        print("  Episode ended during warm-up — reset and retry.")
        break

# --- Phase 2: Training (60 s / 1-minute ticks) ---
print("\n=== Training phase (60 s ticks) ===")
done = False
while not done:
    cpu = data["obs"]["cpu_util"]
    if cpu > 0.75:
        action = {"type": "scale_out", "parameters": {"instanceCount": 1}}
    elif cpu < 0.30 and data["obs"]["instances"] > 1:
        action = {"type": "scale_in", "parameters": {"instanceCount": 1}}
    else:
        action = NO_OP

    data = step(action, tick_seconds=60)
    done = data["done"]
    obs = data["obs"]
    # Per-node routed load — optional field, so guard against its absence
    # (absent on reset observations and compute-free simulations):
    rps_per_node = obs.get("routedRps_per_node", obs["rps"] / max(obs["instances"], 1))
    print(
        f"  t={data['t']:4d}  sim={data['sim_time_human']:>8s}  "
        f"reward={data['reward']:+.3f}  "
        f"cpu={data['obs']['cpu_util']:.1%}  "
        f"rps/node={rps_per_node:.1f}  "
        f"p95={data['metrics']['latency_p95']} ms  "
        f"cost=${data['metrics']['cost_usd_hr']:.2f}/hr  "
        f"done={done}"
    )

Python – mid-episode cold instance (warmup_factor)
x-codeSamples.source:
"""
Mid-episode warmup_factor safe-access pattern.

obs.warmup_factor is an optional field — it is ABSENT from the observation
vector until the first cold compute instance exists in the episode. This happens
in two cases:
  1. An `add_resource` action provisions a new compute resource mid-episode.
  2. Canvas autoscaling adds a compute replica in response to high CPU/traffic.

Because the field appears dynamically, agents building a fixed-width
observation vector must default to 1.0 (fully warmed) when the field is absent:

  wf = obs.get("warmup_factor", 1.0)

A value < 1.0 means at least one compute instance is still warming up and is
not yet at full throughput. Use wf directly as a feature — do not re-derive it
from step counters or metrics.compute[].warmup_steps_remaining.

The pattern below shows a typical episode loop that handles both the pre-warmup
phase (field absent) and the post-add_resource warm-up window (field in (0, 1]).
"""
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api"
API_KEY = "your-api-key"
ENV_ID = "env-aws-001"

session = requests.Session()
session.headers.update({"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"})

def step(action: dict) -> dict:
    resp = session.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/rl/environments/{ENV_ID}/step",
        json={"action": action},
    )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()

done = False
while not done:
    # --- build observation vector (always safe to call even if field absent) ---
    obs = step({"type": "no_op", "parameters": {}})["obs"]
    wf = obs.get("warmup_factor", 1.0)   # 1.0 = fully warmed / no cold instance

    cpu = obs["cpu_util"]

    # penalise decisions made while a cold instance is still warming up
    effective_cpu = cpu / wf if wf > 0 else cpu

    if effective_cpu > 0.75:
        action = {"type": "scale_out", "parameters": {"instanceCount": 1}}
    elif effective_cpu < 0.30 and obs["instances"] > 1:
        action = {"type": "scale_in", "parameters": {"instanceCount": 1}}
    else:
        action = {"type": "no_op", "parameters": {}}

    data = step(action)
    done = data["done"]
    print(
        f"  t={data['t']:4d}  wf={wf:.2f}  "
        f"cpu={cpu:.1%}  effective_cpu={effective_cpu:.1%}  "
        f"reward={data['reward']:+.3f}  done={done}"
    )

tick_seconds.description:
Per-step override for the simulation clock advancement. When provided,
this value overrides the episode-level `tick_seconds` set in `episodeConfig`
for this step only. Useful for agents that want to fast-forward through
warm-up phases (e.g. 300 s ticks) and then switch to finer-grained steps
(e.g. 60 s ticks) for precise autoscaling decisions. The actual value
used is reflected in `observation.tick_seconds` in the response.

doAdjustThreshold.description:
Lower the CPU scale-out trigger from the default 70 % to 65 % so the
DigitalOcean autoscaler scales out earlier, reducing latency during wave
traffic peaks. Also tightens the throughput threshold to 70 %.

doScaleOut.summary: DO: proactively add a Droplet replica
doScaleOut.description:
Force-provision one additional s-2vcpu-4gb Droplet replica ahead of a
predicted traffic spike. The first observation after this action will
reflect the ~30 s cold-start latency overhead modelled for DigitalOcean.

doScaleIn.summary: DO: remove an idle Droplet replica
doScaleIn.description:
Remove one Droplet replica when traffic has subsided. The 180 s cooldown
in the DigitalOcean autoscaling profile prevents thrashing between
scale-in and scale-out actions.

digitaloceanAMDNVMeScaleOut.summary: DO AMD NVMe: add an s-2vcpu-4gb-amd Droplet replica
digitaloceanAMDNVMeScaleOut.description:
Force-provision one additional AMD NVMe Droplet (s-2vcpu-4gb-amd,
$0.038/hr per instance) ahead of a predicted traffic spike. The AMD
EPYC variant's NVMe-backed local storage delivers higher I/O throughput
than the standard Intel Droplet at the same price point. After the ~30 s
cold-start overhead the cluster moves from 2 to 3 instances, bringing
CPU utilisation down from ~71 % to ~56 % and P95 latency from ~148 ms
to ~118 ms. This action triggers the `digitaloceanAMDNVMeStep` response
shape, where resources are named "Droplet s-2vcpu-4gb-amd" to
distinguish AMD NVMe Droplets from standard Intel Droplets.

t.description: Current simulation time step (incremented after each action)

resources.description: Full resource list with per-resource `recoveryPolicy`. Resources that have never had `set_recovery_policy` applied carry the global defaults (criticalCpuThreshold: 80, criticalSteps: 4, warningCpuThreshold: 70, warningSteps: 3). Use this to confirm a `set_recovery_policy` action took effect or to compare healing configurations across resources.

reward.description: Scalar total reward for this step (weighted sum of reward_components)

performance.description: Performance score (0–1, based on latency and errors)

cost.description: Cost efficiency score (0–1, based on budget)

stability.description: Stability score (−1 to 1, penalizes excessive changes)

sla.description: SLA compliance score (−1 to 0, penalizes violations)

connection_pressure.description: DB connection-pool saturation penalty. Only present when the simulation contains database resources. 0 when pool pressure ≤ 1.0 (healthy); decreases with slope −1 per unit of pressure from 1.0 to 1.5 (reaching −0.5), then drops with slope −2 per unit above 1.5 — twice as steep — flooring at −1.0 at pressure ≥ 1.75. Added directly to the weighted sum of the other four components so agents are penalised for driving pools into exhaustion even before latency rises. NOTE: This component is absent until the episode first contains a database resource. When a DB is added mid-episode (via add_resource), the penalty is ramped in linearly over 5 steps (starting at 1/5 of its full magnitude on the first step it appears, reaching full strength after 5 steps) so its introduction does not cause a sudden step-to-step reward discontinuity. Agents may still treat the first appearance as a near-zero baseline.

unmodeled_cost.description: Penalty applied when one or more cost dimensions are active but not modeled in the reward function (e.g. egress charges, cross-AZ traffic). Absent when no unmodeled dimensions are detected. Magnitude equals -(count × unmodeled_cost_penalty_per_dimension). Agents should treat this as a persistent blind-spot signal rather than a transient cost spike.

sim_time_human.description:
Human-readable representation of the elapsed simulated time.
Format is `Xh Ym` when at least one hour has elapsed,
`Xm Ys` when at least one minute (but less than one hour)
has elapsed, and `Xs` for less than one minute.
Mirrors the value inside `info.sim_time_human` for convenient
top-level access without unpacking the info object.

eventsGenerated.description: Number of events generated this step

sim_time_human.description:
Human-readable representation of the elapsed simulated time.
Format is `Xh Ym` when at least one hour has elapsed,
`Xm Ys` when at least one minute (but less than one hour)
has elapsed, and `Xs` for less than one minute.

scale_clamped.description: Present and `true` when a `scale_out` or `scale_in` action was trimmed to honour the effective per-resource instance bounds (`characteristics.maxInstances` / `characteristics.minInstances` vs `autoscalingConfig.maxInstances` / `autoscalingConfig.minInstances`, whichever is tighter). Absent when no clamping occurred.

requested.description: Present when `scale_clamped` is `true`. The number of instances the action *requested* to add (scale_out) or remove (scale_in) — i.e. the `instanceCount` action parameter.

actual.description: Present when `scale_clamped` is `true`. The number of instances that were *actually* added (scale_out) or removed (scale_in) after applying the effective bound. `0` when the action was fully blocked (fleet is already at the hard limit).

limit.description: Present when `scale_clamped` is `true`. The effective bound that triggered clamping (`effectiveMax` for scale_out or `effectiveMin` for scale_in).

unmodeled_cost_warning.description: List of cost dimension identifiers that are active this step but not modeled in the reward function. Present (and non-empty) only when at least one unmodeled dimension is detected. Omitted when all detected dimensions are modeled. Known values: `egress` (network egress charges are incurred whenever traffic > 0), `cross_az_traffic` (cross-AZ data transfer charges apply when resources with different availability zones are connected).

unmodeled_cost_penalty.description: Total reward penalty applied this step due to unmodeled cost dimensions. Equals -(count of active unmodeled dimensions × episodeConfig.unmodeled_cost_penalty_per_dimension). Present only when `unmodeled_cost_warning` is non-empty.

post.summary: Run multiple RL actions in a single request
post.description:
Executes up to 30 actions sequentially in a single HTTP round-trip, advancing the
simulation by one step per action. Stops early and returns partial results if the
episode ends (`done: true`) before all actions are processed.

**Rate limiting:** Each action in the batch counts as one call against the
5 000 req/hr RL training quota. A batch of 30 actions consumes 30 quota units.
If the quota is exhausted mid-batch, the endpoint returns 429 with a `Retry-After`
header indicating how many seconds remain until the window resets.

**Idle TTL:** The last successful batch-step call resets the environment's 2-hour
idle timer, the same as a single `step` call.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
Python
x-codeSamples.source:
import time, requests

BASE_URL = "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api"
API_KEY = "your-api-key"
ENV_ID = "env-aws-001"

session = requests.Session()
session.headers.update({"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"})

def batch_step(steps: list[dict], max_retries: int = 5) -> dict:
    for attempt in range(max_retries):
        resp = session.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/rl/environments/{ENV_ID}/batch-step",
            json={"steps": steps},
        )
        if resp.status_code == 429:
            retry_after = int(resp.headers.get("Retry-After", 60))
            print(f"Rate limited — waiting {retry_after}s")
            time.sleep(retry_after)
            continue
        resp.raise_for_status()
        return resp.json()
    raise RuntimeError("Exceeded max retries")

NO_OP = {"action": {"type": "no_op", "parameters": {}}}
SCALE_OUT = {"action": {"type": "scale_out", "parameters": {"instanceCount": 1}}}

# Warm-up: 30 no-ops at 300 s each (covers ~2.5 hours sim time)
warmup = batch_step([{**NO_OP, "tick_seconds": 300}] * 30)
print(f"Warm-up complete: {len(warmup['results'])} steps")

# Training loop
total_reward = 0.0
while True:
    result = batch_step([SCALE_OUT] + [NO_OP] * 9)
    for step_result in result["results"]:
        total_reward += step_result["reward"]
        if step_result["done"]:
            print(f"Episode complete — total reward: {total_reward:.2f}")
            break
    else:
        continue
    break

post.summary: Submit an eval-episode job for asynchronous execution
post.description:
Replays one or more ordered action sequences through a fresh episode reset and returns
per-episode cumulative rewards computed with `evalCostOverrides` applied. Use this to
detect **reward blind spots**: policies trained without egress or cross-AZ cost pricing
will show a significant reward drop (reward_collapse) when those dimensions are priced.

The endpoint does **not** mutate any stored environment or simulation state — all
episode rollouts are in-memory and ephemeral.

**Async mode (default):** Returns `202 Accepted` immediately with a `jobId`. Poll
`GET /rl/environments/{environmentId}/eval-episodes/{jobId}` until `status` is
`completed` or `failed`.

**Sync mode (`?sync=true`):** Runs the rollout in-process and returns the full result
inline with `200 OK`. Suitable for small workloads (≤ 3 episodes, ≤ 20 steps each).

**reward_collapse logic:** `reward_collapse` is `true` when
`meanEvalReward < trainingTotalReward − collapseThreshold × |trainingTotalReward|`.
With the default threshold of 0.20, any policy whose eval reward is more than 20 %
below its training reward is flagged as collapsing.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
Python
x-codeSamples.source:
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api"
API_KEY = "your-api-key"
ENV_ID = "env-aws-001"

resp = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/rl/environments/{ENV_ID}/eval-episodes",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"},
    json={
        "actions": [
            [{"type": "no_op", "parameters": {}}] * 10
        ],
        "evalCostOverrides": {"egress": 0.5, "cross_az_traffic": 0.3},
        "collapseThreshold": 0.20,
    },
)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()
print(f"reward_collapse={data['reward_collapse']}  mean_eval={data['meanEvalReward']:.3f}  training={data['trainingTotalReward']:.3f}")

parameters.description: ID of the RL environment whose training reward is used as the baseline

actions.description: Array of episodes. Each episode is an ordered array of actions to replay from a fresh reset. All episodes use the same `evalCostOverrides`. Maximum 10 episodes.

items.description: Ordered sequence of actions for one eval episode

Supported keys: `egress` (any simulation with traffic > 0) and `cross_az_traffic` (simulations with resources in distinct Availability Zones). post.summary: Run a chaos engineering test
post.description:
Execute a chaos engineering test by injecting failures into a simulation.
Can use pre-built scenarios or custom failure injections.

This endpoint works with simulations built on **any supported provider**,
including AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and **DigitalOcean**. When targeting a
DigitalOcean-based simulation, failure types such as `kill_instance`
affect Droplets, `zone_failure` targets DigitalOcean datacenter regions,
and `database_crash` targets Managed Database clusters.

**Failure naming surfaces** — three zone-related names, three different contexts:
- `zone_outage` — custom injection type in `customInjections[].failureType` (this endpoint)
- `az_outage` — failure type in the synchronous `POST /simulations/{id}/failures` API
- `zone_failure` — pre-built scenario ID used in `scenarioId`

**Multi-fault cascade example** — inject a zone outage and a database slowdown simultaneously
via `customInjections` to test correlated failure handling:

```json
{
  "simulationId": "sim-abc123",
  "customInjections": [
    { "failureType": "zone_outage", "targetZone": "us-east-1a", "duration": 120 },
    { "failureType": "database_slowdown", "targetResourceId": "db-primary", "intensity": 80, "duration": 120 }
  ]
}
```

For `database_crash` custom injections, `promotionDelaySeconds` (default 30)
and `restartDelaySeconds` (default 1800) are bounded integer simulation-clock
assumptions, not measured provider behavior or SLAs. A healthy database
explicitly linked by `replicaOf` promotes after the first delay; without
one, the writer restarts after the injection duration plus the second delay.
Crashes scheduled for the same simulation instant are considered together:
a simultaneously crashed replica is not eligible. In that case the writer
uses sole_writer_restart, with promotionUnavailableReason set to
related_replica_unavailable_at_injection; a replica lost after promotion
was announced instead produces an Explicit replica promotion failed event.
`multiAz` and `instanceCount` do not imply an eligible replica. The chosen
effective values are returned per target in
`resilienceScore.metrics.databaseCrashAssumptions`.
While no database serves, positive offered work has 100% errors and zero
goodput; promotion restores service without a residual writer-outage
penalty. Chaos samples every 10 simulation seconds (default promotion
at 30 seconds). Quick `inject-failure` instead advances one simulation
second per step, promotes on the second step (one second after injection),
and rejoins after its bounded park window. Compare equivalent
unavailable/serving phases, not equal step indices or wall-clock times.

The prebuilt `scenarioId: "database_crash"` also accepts these two fields
at the top level of this request (not inside `customInjections`). They
override only this job, not the saved scenario. Other scenario IDs and
custom injections cannot use the top-level fields.

 **Resilience grade** — the `grade` in the result is derived from the
 live weighted `overall` score, including recovery, availability, data
 integrity, and graceful degradation. Vulnerability findings remain
 architectural evidence and may be similar across fault combinations,
 but the grade is not a static SPOF label. To inspect both, pair
 `POST /chaos/run` (vulnerability report) with the synchronous
 `POST /simulations/{id}/failures` + step-loop pattern (live metrics).

post.summary: Search multi-cloud deployment strategies
post.description:
Analyze a workload profile and generate optimized multi-cloud deployment strategies.
The system evaluates different provider combinations across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and DigitalOcean
based on cost, latency, and vendor lock-in considerations.

**DigitalOcean as a candidate provider:** DigitalOcean is a first-class candidate in every
exploration run. It is particularly well-suited for cost-optimized workloads — Droplets and
Managed Databases typically produce the lowest monthly spend in the comparison report. Set a
high `cost` weight (e.g. 0.7+) and a moderate budget to see DigitalOcean-primary strategies
appear at the top of `topStrategies` in the results.

**Request body fields:** The request body has two top-level fields that are independent of
each other. `workloadProfile` describes the workload being evaluated (compute/database
instances, traffic, latency requirements, and primary region). `optimizationWeights` is a
separate top-level object — **not** nested inside `workloadProfile` — that controls how
strategies are ranked: `cost` (default 0.4), `latency` (default 0.4), and `vendorLockIn`
(default 0.2). Weights need not sum to 1.0; the engine normalises them during scoring. A
cost-heavy weight (e.g. `cost: 0.9`) surfaces the cheapest strategies at the top of
`topStrategies`; a latency-heavy weight (e.g. `latency: 0.9`) surfaces the lowest-latency
strategies instead.

get.summary: Fetch multi-cloud exploration results
get.description:
Retrieve the **final** results from a multi-cloud exploration job.

**Only returns data once the job has finished.** This endpoint returns
results exclusively when the job `status` is `completed`. While the job
is still `pending` or `running` it returns `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; a
`failed` job returns `500`.

**Polling pattern:**
- Poll `GET /multi-cloud/jobs/{jobId}` (or subscribe to `/stream`) until `status` is `completed`, then call this endpoint once for the final ranked strategies and comparison report.
- To read strategies as they accumulate while the job is still running, use `GET /multi-cloud/jobs/{jobId}/partial-results` instead — that endpoint returns `isComplete: false` until the job reaches a terminal state.
- For real-time streaming of progress, use the `/stream` endpoint.

**Response field names:**
The successful `200` response contains `topStrategies` (the highest-scoring strategies,
sorted by `metrics.compositeScore` descending) and `allStrategies` (every strategy
evaluated, also sorted). Do **not** use the field names `variants`, `strategies`, or
`ranked` — those do not exist in the response.
