# Poll status until the job is completed, then fetch the final results.
# /results returns 400 while the job is still pending or running.
until curl -sf "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api/multi-cloud/jobs/job_abc123" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" | grep -q '"status":"completed"'; do
  sleep 2
done

curl "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api/multi-cloud/jobs/job_abc123/results" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY"

# Filter results to DigitalOcean and AWS strategies only
curl "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api/multi-cloud/jobs/job_abc123/results?providers=digitalocean,aws" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY"

x-codeSamples.label: Python
x-codeSamples.source:
import time
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api"
API_KEY = "your-api-key"
JOB_ID = "job_abc123"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"}

# Poll status until the job is finished. /results returns 400 while
# the job is still pending or running; use /partial-results to read
# strategies as they accumulate during a run.
while True:
    status = requests.get(
        f"{BASE_URL}/multi-cloud/jobs/{JOB_ID}", headers=HEADERS,
    ).json()
    if status["status"] in ("completed", "failed", "cancelled"):
        break
    time.sleep(2)

resp = requests.get(
    f"{BASE_URL}/multi-cloud/jobs/{JOB_ID}/results",
    headers=HEADERS,
)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()
print(f"Job {JOB_ID}  status={data['status']}  "
      f"complete={data['isComplete']}  strategies={data['strategiesGenerated']}")
for strategy in data.get("topStrategies", []):
    cost = strategy["metrics"]["monthlyCost"]
    latency = strategy["metrics"]["avgLatencyMs"]
    print(f"  {strategy['name']}  cost=${cost}/mo  latency={latency}ms")

parameters.name: providers
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of cloud provider names to filter results by preferred primary provider.
A strategy is included if any of the specified providers holds ≥ 50 % of the traffic allocation.
Supported values: `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`, `digitalocean`, `oci`.
If omitted, all strategies are returned.

200.description: Job results (partial or complete based on job status)

isComplete.description: True if job is finished, false if still running or pending

strategiesGenerated.description: Number of strategies generated so far

allStrategies.description: All raw strategies generated so far (available during and after generation)

topStrategies.description: Top 10 optimized strategies (only available when status is completed)

comparisonReport.description: Markdown comparison report (only available when complete)

providerTrustLevels.description: Per-provider rate trust level — the worst rateProvenance.basis across the pricing constants behind that provider's cost figures. "on-demand" means every contributing rate is a verified published list price; "estimated" means at least one contributing rate is a flat estimate, so treat that provider's ranking as approximate.

estimateDisclaimer.description: Reminder that cost and latency figures are baseline planning estimates; validate with materialize + step under production load.

methodology.description: Describes the data origin and validation basis for these results. Agents should read this object before interpreting cross-provider rankings or citing consistency across multiple independent runs as external evidence.

dataSource.description: Origin of the result data. simulation-model means results come from the Cloud World Model deterministic simulation engine, not from live cloud APIs or external benchmark tooling.

validationBasis.description: Characterises how the underlying data has been validated externally. Currently only simulation_only is emitted. Future values (calibrated_public_data, provider_benchmark) can be added without removing or retyping this field.

externallyValidated.description: Convenience boolean for agents that need a simple truth test without pattern-matching validationBasis strings. false whenever validationBasis is simulation_only.

seedCount.description: The number of random seeds used in this job own simulation. Always 1 per job. Running multiple independent jobs and observing consistent rankings reflects model stability, not external performance validation.

note.description: Authoritative plain-English statement suitable for direct use by agents calibrating recommendation language. Static across all runs.

example.note: Results describe Cloud World Model simulation outcomes and should not be interpreted as measured cloud-provider benchmarks. Consistency across multiple independent runs confirms model stability, not external performance validation.

interpretationScope.description: Machine-readable interpretation constraints attached alongside methodology. Agents must consult this object before forming any conclusion about provider performance.

providerPerformanceScope.description: Scope of any provider-performance statement derivable from these results. Currently only simulation-only is emitted; future values (calibrated, empirically-validated) may be added without breaking change.

externalValidation.description: Mirrors methodology.externallyValidated so agents that reach interpretationScope first get an unambiguous false without cross-referencing.

crossSeedConsistencyMeans.description: Agreement across seeds proves the model is deterministic, not that cloud providers behave that way.

untestedLoadExtrapolationAllowed.description: When false, any load level outside testedLoadLevels must be presented as a hypothesis requiring a new simulation, not a derived conclusion.

prohibitedClaimCategories.description: Machine-readable constraint list; agents must check planned conclusions against each entry. Category labels are hyphenated enum tokens, not prose.

permittedUses.description: What these results may legitimately be used for.

testedLoadLevels.description: Derived from job config; only these levels are validated by this simulation run.

untestedScenariosNote.description: Authoritative sentence defining how untested scenarios must be labelled.

permittedUses: compare simulation-model cost and latency trade-offs under the tested scenarios
identify which provider the model favours given the configured resource shapes and traffic levels
use rankings as a structured starting point for further empirical benchmarking
example.untestedScenariosNote: Load levels or failure modes not present in testedLoadLevels are hypotheses requiring a new simulation run, not conclusions derivable from this result.

# Multi-Cloud Strategy Comparison Report

## Winner: DigitalOcean AMD NVMe Primary Strategy

Monthly cost: **$6,200** — 55% lower than the AWS-dominant baseline ($13,800).
Average latency: **52 ms** — within the 150 ms SLA requirement.
Vendor lock-in score: **44/100** — low lock-in, easy to migrate if requirements change.

## Key Resources

- **Compute:** DigitalOcean AMD NVMe Droplets (s-2vcpu-4gb-amd, nyc3) — AMD EPYC processors with NVMe-backed local SSD storage deliver higher disk I/O throughput than standard Intel Droplets at the same hourly rate ($0.036/hr per Droplet). Ideal for workloads with frequent local reads/writes or ephemeral scratch space.
- **Database:** DigitalOcean Managed Databases (PostgreSQL, 2-node HA cluster, nyc3) — automated failover, daily backups, and PgBouncer connection pooling included at no extra charge.
- **Object Storage:** DigitalOcean Spaces — S3-compatible API, 250 GB included, optional CDN edge caching.

## AMD NVMe vs Standard Droplets

The `s-2vcpu-4gb-amd` slug selects the AMD NVMe variant of the standard shared-CPU tier. Compared to the equivalent Intel Droplet (`s-2vcpu-4gb`):
- Same vCPU count and RAM
- Same hourly price
- NVMe local SSD instead of spinning disk — up to 3× higher sequential read throughput
- AMD EPYC "Milan" or "Rome" core depending on host availability

Choose the AMD NVMe variant when your workload is I/O-bound (e.g. log processing, local caching, build pipelines) or when you want deterministic low-latency disk access without paying for a dedicated CPU plan.

## Trade-offs

| Metric | DO AMD NVMe Primary | DO AMD NVMe + GCP | AWS-Dominant |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly cost | $6,200 | $8,100 | $13,800 |
| Avg latency | 52 ms | 49 ms | 41 ms |
| Lock-in score | 44 | 38 | 74 |

## Recommendation

For cost-sensitive workloads with moderate I/O requirements, the DigitalOcean AMD NVMe Primary strategy delivers the best value. The 11 ms latency gap versus the AWS baseline is unlikely to affect end-user experience for the given SLA. If burst capacity beyond current Droplet limits is anticipated, consider the DO AMD NVMe + GCP Balanced strategy, which adds only $1,900/month for a 3 ms latency improvement and lower vendor lock-in.

get.summary: Fetch partial multi-cloud results from a running job
get.description:
Retrieve strategies accumulated so far for a multi-cloud exploration job, even while the job is still running.

This endpoint is the dedicated channel for polling partial results during job execution.
The `/results` endpoint requires the job to be completed; use this endpoint instead when you want
to start analyzing strategies before the full exploration finishes.

**Polling pattern:**
```
while true:
  data = GET /api/multi-cloud/jobs/{jobId}/partial-results
  show data.allStrategies to user
  if data.isComplete: break
  sleep(2s)
# Fetch ranked results and comparison report from /results once complete
full = GET /api/multi-cloud/jobs/{jobId}/results
```

**isComplete flag:**
- `false` — job is still `pending` or `running`; more strategies may arrive
- `true` — job has reached a terminal state (`completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled`)

**When `isComplete` is true and `status` is `completed`**, fetch the ranked
`topStrategies` and `comparisonReport` from `GET /api/multi-cloud/jobs/{jobId}/results`.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
# Poll partial results until the job is complete
while true; do
  DATA=$(curl -s "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api/multi-cloud/jobs/job_abc123/partial-results" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY")
  echo "$DATA" | jq '{strategies: (.allStrategies | length), isComplete: .isComplete}'
  [ "$(echo "$DATA" | jq -r '.isComplete')" = "true" ] && break
  sleep 2
done

x-codeSamples.label: Node.js

parameters.name: providers
parameters.description:
Comma-separated list of cloud provider names to filter results by preferred primary provider.
A strategy is included if any of the specified providers holds ≥ 50 % of the traffic allocation.
Supported values: `aws`, `gcp`, `azure`, `digitalocean`, `oci`.
If omitted, all strategies are returned.

200.description: Partial or terminal results for the job

isComplete.description: True if job has reached a terminal state, false if still pending or running

strategiesGenerated.description: Number of strategies generated so far

allStrategies.description: All raw strategies generated so far

providerTrustLevels.description: Per-provider rate trust level — the worst rateProvenance.basis across the pricing constants behind that provider's cost figures, derived from strategies accumulated so far. "on-demand" means every contributing rate is a verified published list price; "estimated" means at least one contributing rate is a flat or usage-based floor approximation (e.g. Aurora Serverless v2/DSQL, GPU inference families). Present for every job status; updates as strategies accumulate. Empty object while no strategies exist yet.

preProvisionVerdict.description: Present when status is completed. Summarizes the leading returned strategy's budget, latency, modeled error-rate, resilience-evidence gap, and uncertainty.

methodology.description: Describes the data origin and validation basis for these results. Agents should read this object before interpreting cross-provider rankings or citing consistency across multiple independent runs as external evidence.

dataSource.description: Origin of the result data. simulation-model means results come from the Cloud World Model deterministic simulation engine.

validationBasis.description: Characterises how the underlying data has been validated externally. Currently only simulation_only is emitted.

externallyValidated.description: Convenience boolean — false whenever validationBasis is simulation_only.

seedCount.description: The number of random seeds used in this job own simulation. Always 1 per job.

note.description: Authoritative plain-English statement for agents calibrating recommendation language. Static across all runs.

example.note: Results describe Cloud World Model simulation outcomes and should not be interpreted as measured cloud-provider benchmarks. Consistency across multiple independent runs confirms model stability, not external performance validation.

interpretationScope.description: Machine-readable interpretation constraints attached alongside methodology. Agents must consult this object before forming any conclusion about provider performance.

providerPerformanceScope.description: Scope of any provider-performance statement derivable from these results. Currently only simulation-only is emitted; future values (calibrated, empirically-validated) may be added without breaking change.

externalValidation.description: Mirrors methodology.externallyValidated so agents that reach interpretationScope first get an unambiguous false without cross-referencing.

crossSeedConsistencyMeans.description: Agreement across seeds proves the model is deterministic, not that cloud providers behave that way.

untestedLoadExtrapolationAllowed.description: When false, any load level outside testedLoadLevels must be presented as a hypothesis requiring a new simulation, not a derived conclusion.

prohibitedClaimCategories.description: Machine-readable constraint list; agents must check planned conclusions against each entry. Category labels are hyphenated enum tokens, not prose.

permittedUses.description: What these results may legitimately be used for.

testedLoadLevels.description: Derived from job config; only these levels are validated by this simulation run.

untestedScenariosNote.description: Authoritative sentence defining how untested scenarios must be labelled.

permittedUses: compare simulation-model cost and latency trade-offs under the tested scenarios
identify which provider the model favours given the configured resource shapes and traffic levels
use rankings as a structured starting point for further empirical benchmarking
example.untestedScenariosNote: Load levels or failure modes not present in testedLoadLevels are hypotheses requiring a new simulation run, not conclusions derivable from this result.

error.description: Error message — only present when status is failed

post.summary: Update all compute resources to a new DigitalOcean Droplet size
post.description:
Resizes every `type: "compute"` resource in the simulation to the
specified DigitalOcean Droplet size tier (e.g. `s-2vcpu-4gb`,
`s-4vcpu-8gb`, `s-8vcpu-16gb`). Useful for right-sizing experiments
where you want to evaluate the cost/performance trade-off of a
uniform resize.

**Scope:** Only applies to `type: "compute"` resources. Database
resources (`type: "database"`) are not affected and remain unchanged.

**DigitalOcean-only:** if any compute resource uses a non-DigitalOcean
provider (AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI), the request is rejected with a
`PROVIDER_MISMATCH` 400 naming the providers found, and no resource is
modified. This endpoint never changes a resource's provider. To
recover a failed resource on any provider, use
`POST /simulations/{simulationId}/recover-resource` instead.

The size must be a valid DigitalOcean Droplet slug. Use
`GET /api/description` to discover available sizes.

Requires `write` scope and ownership.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api/simulations/sim-abc123/bulk-resize \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"dropletSize": "s-4vcpu-8gb"}'

x-codeSamples.label: Python
x-codeSamples.source:
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api"
API_KEY = "your-api-key"

resp = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/simulations/sim-abc123/bulk-resize",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"},
    json={"dropletSize": "s-4vcpu-8gb"},
)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()
print(f"Resized {data['resizedCount']} compute resource(s) to s-4vcpu-8gb")

post.summary: Update a resource using a right-sizing hint
post.description:
Applies a right-sizing recommendation from
`GET /simulations/{simulationId}/right-sizing-hint` to the targeted
resource in one call. Pass the `affectedResourceId` and
`recommendedSlug` from the hint response; the server validates the
slug against the resource's available sizes before mutating anything.

**Validation:** Returns `400 UNKNOWN_SIZE` with a list of valid slugs
if `recommendedSlug` is not recognized for the resource's provider and
type — so callers can pass the hint slug directly without a separate
size lookup.

**Supported resource types:** compute, database, storage (any
provider). GPU node-count hints (`gpu-underutilized`, `gpu-saturated`)
and managed-API breakeven hints (`gpu-api-breakeven`) produce
non-slug `recommendedSlug` values and cannot be applied via this
endpoint. SQL Server Express databases are also excluded: their
instance class and CPU-credit billing configuration must remain
consistent. This route returns `400 UNSUPPORTED_RESIZE` without
changing the simulation for those resources.

**Cross-provider alternatives:** DigitalOcean slugs returned as
cross-provider alternatives in right-sizing hints are accepted for
non-DO resources; the resource's cost characteristics are updated to
the DO tier without changing the provider field.

Requires `write` scope and ownership.

x-codeSamples.label: curl
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -X POST https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api/simulations/sim-abc123/apply-right-sizing \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"resourceId": "res-1", "recommendedSlug": "t3.small"}'

x-codeSamples.label: Python
x-codeSamples.source:
import requests

BASE_URL = "https://www.cloudworldmodel.ai/api"
API_KEY = "your-api-key"

# Step 1: get the hint
hint_resp = requests.get(
    f"{BASE_URL}/simulations/sim-abc123/right-sizing-hint",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"},
)
hint = hint_resp.json()["hints"][0]

# Step 2: apply it
resp = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/simulations/sim-abc123/apply-right-sizing",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"},
    json={"resourceId": hint["affectedResourceId"], "recommendedSlug": hint["recommendedSlug"]},
)
resp.raise_for_status()
data = resp.json()
print(f"Applied {data['appliedSlug']} to {data['resourceName']}")

post.summary: Run recovery for a single failed resource
post.description:
Clears a specific failed resource's failure state so the simulation
engine restores it to healthy over subsequent steps. Deactivates any
in-effect **reversible** failure injection targeting the resource
(`instance_down`, `database_overload`), restores snapshotted
characteristics where available, and resets the resource's health
counters to zero so only subsequent qualifying simulation steps count.

Returns 409 `PERMANENT_DATA_LOSS` for destroyed data that has not been
explicitly rebuilt. Generic recovery never clears `dataState`; an empty
rebuilt database can serve again while its original data remains lost.

The quick `inject-failure` endpoint is intentionally different: its
positive `failureParkSteps` window is automatic, so the node may rejoin
routing after the window without this endpoint. Use `recover-resource`
when an explicit recovery is required for a persistent reversible
`instance_down` failure; poll `isRoutable`, `routedRps`, and
`recoveryProgress` after either flow.

**`instance_kill` cannot be recovered** — that failure type
permanently removes the target resource from the simulation. Calling
this endpoint with the killed resource's id returns `400
RESOURCE_KILLED`; re-add the resource via
`PATCH /simulations/{simulationId}`, or prefer `instance_down` when
you want a reversible outage.

**Scoped to the targeted resource only** — other resources that remain
failed are not affected.

The response echoes the applied outcome, including `stepsToHealthy`:
a lower-bound estimate of the `POST /step` (or `step-hybrid`) calls
needed for the engine to demote the resource back to `healthy` under
the current recovery policy (defaults: critical→warning after 4 steps
below 80% CPU, warning→healthy after 3 steps below 70%; the default
lower bound is 7 steps from critical). `stepsToHealthyIsLowerBound` is always true:
explicitly failed resources may require an additional failure-park
transition before cooldown resumes, and a CPU threshold breach resets
the cooldown counter. Callers should take at least `stepsToHealthy`
steps, then poll `GET /simulations/{simulationId}` until the resource
is healthy.

Works for every provider (AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, DigitalOcean) —
unlike `bulk-resize`, which is DigitalOcean-only.

Provide `resourceName` or `resourceId`. Returns 400 when the resource
cannot be found, was permanently removed by `instance_kill`, or is
already healthy.

Requires `write` scope and ownership.

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"resourceName": "app-server-01"}'

get.summary: Validate simulation cost accuracy against provider benchmarks
get.description:
Compares the simulation's cost estimates against known real-world provider
pricing benchmarks. Returns a validation result indicating whether the
simulated cost per hour is within the acceptable tolerance (±10%).

Useful for confirming the simulation is faithfully modelling provider
pricing before using it for cost-optimisation decisions.

**Skip semantics:** Resources without a `serviceFamily` characteristic,
or whose `provider`/`serviceFamily`/`size` combination has no pricing
benchmark entry, are silently skipped. When all resources are skipped,
`validations` is empty, `summary.total` is `0`, and `checked` is `false`.
In that state `valid: true` means "no failures among the zero resources
checked" — it does **not** mean the simulation's cost accuracy was
verified. Always check `checked: true` before acting on `valid`.

Requires `read` scope and ownership.

valid.description: Whether all checked resources are within the ±10% cost tolerance. Only meaningful when `checked` is `true`.

checked.description: `true` when at least one resource had a matching pricing benchmark and was evaluated. `false` means no comparable data was found — the simulation resources may lack `serviceFamily` or have no pricing benchmark entry. When `checked` is `false`, `valid: true` does **not** mean accuracy was verified.

source.description: Source citation for the benchmark value

total.description: Number of resources that had a matching benchmark

avgDeviation.description: Average deviation across all checked resources

skippedCount.description: Number of resources (or resource-metric pairs) that were evaluated but had no matching benchmark entry and were therefore skipped.

skippedReasons.description: Human-readable explanation for each skipped resource. Common reasons: no `serviceFamily` set, or no pricing benchmark found for the provider/serviceFamily/size combination.

get.summary: Validate performance accuracy against provider benchmarks
get.description:
Compares the simulation's throughput and latency estimates against known
real-world provider benchmarks. Returns a validation result indicating
whether the simulated performance metrics are within the acceptable
tolerance (±15%).

**Skip semantics:** Resources without a `serviceFamily` characteristic
are skipped entirely. For resources that do have a `serviceFamily`,
individual metrics (`max_throughput`, `baseline_latency`,
`max_connections`) are skipped when no benchmark entry exists for that
provider/metric combination. When all resource-metric pairs are skipped,
`validations` is empty, `summary.total` is `0`, and `checked` is `false`.
In that state `valid: true` means "no failures among the zero pairs
checked" — it does **not** mean the simulation's performance accuracy
was verified. Always check `checked: true` before acting on `valid`.

Requires `read` scope and ownership.

valid.description: Whether all checked resource-metric pairs are within the ±15% performance tolerance. Only meaningful when `checked` is `true`.

checked.description: `true` when at least one resource-metric pair had a matching performance benchmark and was evaluated. `false` means no comparable data was found — the simulation resources may lack `serviceFamily`, or no performance benchmark exists for the provider/metric combination. When `checked` is `false`, `valid: true` does **not** mean accuracy was verified.

metric.description: The metric that was validated. One of: `max_throughput`, `baseline_latency`, `max_connections`.

total.description: Number of resource-metric pairs that had a matching benchmark

skippedCount.description: Number of resource-metric pairs that were skipped because no benchmark was found.

skippedReasons.description: Human-readable explanation for each skipped resource-metric pair.

get.summary: Validate both cost and performance accuracy
get.description:
Convenience endpoint that runs both cost and performance accuracy
validations in a single call. Returns a combined result with an
`overallValid` flag that is `true` only if both checks pass.

Requires `read` scope and ownership.

cost.description: Full cost accuracy validation result — same shape as `GET /validate-cost-accuracy`. Check `cost.checked` before trusting `cost.valid`.

benchmarkCost.description: Expected hourly cost from provider benchmark (USD)

performance.description: Full performance accuracy validation result — same shape as `GET /validate-performance-accuracy`. Check `performance.checked` before trusting `performance.valid`.

metric.description: The metric that was validated. One of: `max_throughput`, `baseline_latency`, `max_connections`.

checked.description: `true` when at least one of the two sub-validations (cost or performance) found comparable benchmark data and ran a real check. `false` means neither sub-result found matching benchmarks — `overallValid: true` in this state does **not** mean accuracy was verified.

overallValid.description: `true` only when both cost and performance `valid` flags are `true`. Only meaningful when `checked` is `true`.

post.summary: Create a scheduled failure injection
post.description:
Creates a new failure injection that will be applied to the simulation
during the specified time window. The injection is applied immediately
to the resource state (the affected resource's status changes) and an
event is recorded.

**Failure types:**
- `instance_kill` — PERMANENTLY removes a compute instance from the simulation (deleting the failure does not restore it)
- `instance_down` — reversible single-node outage: marks a compute instance critical without removing it; deactivating (`isActive: false`) or deleting the failure restores the node
- `az_outage` — simulates an availability zone outage
- `database_overload` — modeled load-sensitive database CPU, bounded Aurora ACU, latency and failed requests; thresholds are assumptions, not AWS guarantees. Set top-level `severity` (minor/moderate/severe, default moderate) or `intensity` (0–1, mapped into those three bands), not both; the response echoes effective severity. Do not place controls in `parameters`.
- `network_latency` — adds latency to all network resources

**Precondition — already-critical targets:** an `instance_down` or
`instance_kill` element whose `targetResourceId` refers to a resource
that is already in `critical` status is rejected with `400` and error
code `RESOURCE_NOT_FAILEABLE` — the same code and reason semantics as
`POST /simulations/{simulationId}/inject-failure`. Consistent with the
batch contract, one rejected element aborts the whole request
(all-or-nothing) and no failure injection is created or applied. In an
array (batch) body the error pointer is index-prefixed
(`/2/targetResourceId`) and the message is prefixed with `failures[2]: `.

Requires `write` scope and ownership.

HybridAgreement.description:
Model agreement — how closely the ML model and rule engine agree with
each other on a hybrid step (distinct from ML confidence, which is the
model's belief in its own prediction). Derived from the largest
normalised deviation among cost, latency P95, latency P99, and error rate, each
normalised against its safety-bound threshold (maxCostDeviation,
maxLatencyDeviation, maxErrorRateDeviation), so one dimension way off
cannot be washed out by agreement on the others. Sits alongside the
per-field `comparisons` array so component signals can be inspected
directly. Absent on decisions persisted before this field existed.

**Safety-fallback participation:** both latencyP95 and latencyP99
deviations are checked against `maxLatencyDeviation` in
`checkSafetyBounds`. A P99 disagreement that exceeds the threshold
triggers the rule-based fallback in the same way a P95 violation does.
Consumers should therefore treat `largestDisagreement: "latencyP99"`
as a first-class fallback signal, not merely an informational label.

largestDisagreement.description: The dimension with the largest normalised rule/ML deviation.

normalizationBasis.description:
The agreement score is calibrated against the configured safety-bound
thresholds, not against relative sensitivity of each metric. Latency
(P95/P99) and error-rate deviations are absolute differences (ms and
percentage points) divided by maxLatencyDeviation /
maxErrorRateDeviation; cost deviation is relative to the rule-based
cost, divided by maxCostDeviation. A deviation that is large in
relative terms but small against its bound (e.g. error rate
0.1% → 0.5% against a 5 pp bound) can therefore still score as
high agreement.

behaviorMismatch.description: Present when `agreement.level === "low"` AND at least one Kubernetes resource in the simulation carries GPU/inference characteristics (`accelerator`, `tokensPerRequest`, `inputTokensPerRequest`) without `inferenceMode: true`. Indicates that the rule engine is using `generic-kubernetes/load-saturation` for a resource that appears to be a GPU inference workload. This is a factual configuration note, not a claim about the ML predictor's internal model — enabling `inferenceMode` switches the rule engine to the `gpu-inference/ttft-decode` latency path AND activates the ML service's own independently calibrated TTFT/decode estimator (`gpu-inference/ttft-decode-ml`), so both models operate on the same workload class and the agreement score may change. Absent when agreement is not "low", no such misconfiguration is detected, or workload-specific latency evidence is unavailable.

detected.description: True when a rule-engine path mismatch was detected on this step.

cause.description: Human-readable explanation of the detected rule-engine configuration issue. Names the detected GPU characteristics and states what to set to activate the GPU inference latency path in the rule engine.
cause.example: Rule engine used generic-kubernetes/load-saturation for resource(s) that carry GPU/inference characteristics (accelerator, tokensPerRequest, or inputTokensPerRequest) but have inferenceMode: false. If this simulation is intended to model GPU inference workloads, setting characteristics.inferenceMode: true would activate the gpu-inference/ttft-decode latency model in the rule engine, which may change the rule/ML agreement score.

affectedResources.description: IDs of Kubernetes resources that triggered the mismatch.

rulesBehaviorModel.description: Provenance: the latency path the rules engine used for this step's dominant workload class (e.g. `gpu-inference/ttft-decode` for inferenceMode Kubernetes GPU clusters, `generic-kubernetes/load-saturation` otherwise).

mlBehaviorModel.description: Provenance: the path/label the ML service used for this prediction (e.g. `gpu-inference/ttft-decode-ml` when the ML service applied its independently calibrated TTFT/decode token-economics estimator, or `generic/nonlinear-heuristics` for the default heuristic path).

behaviorAlignment.description: `aligned` when the rules engine and ML service operated on the same workload class for this step; `misaligned` when they diverged (e.g. rules used the GPU-inference TTFT model but ML fell back to generic compute saturation). Lets a disagreement be diagnosed as "same model, different numbers" vs "different models entirely".

Absent on non-inference steps.

KubernetesCpuHpaConfig.description: Opt-in bounded CPU-based workload replica model. It changes workload replica counts only; it does not scale Kubernetes node pools, call a live cluster, or claim Kubernetes HPA controller parity. CPU request and demand are labeled ASSUMED unless their corresponding evidence object is supplied. An optional reviewed CPU/RPS measurement series can derive demand through a least-squares fit constrained through zero; its declared demand must match the fit and its source and reference must be retained in cpuDemandEvidence. Omitted CPU requests are never inferred; Utilization targets then return an explicit error. Utilization is measured as a percentage of the declared request; AverageValue is absolute millicores per pod. Each recommendation is ceil(current replicas × current metric ÷ target), then clamped to replica bounds.

The fitted value is aggregate workload CPU millicores divided by offered RPS, using least squares constrained through zero. cpuDemandEvidence must retain the source and reference. Each point is measured at workload level, not inferred by CWM.

RdsSqlServerBillingConfig.description: Bounded caller-provided billing assumptions for AWS RDS SQL Server Express. Attach this object only to an `aws` `database` resource whose `serviceFamily` is `rds-sqlserver-express`. CPU is a constant interval assumption, not inferred from traffic, database load, generic simulated CPU, or a managed-service process. The initial earned-credit and surplus-credit ledgers are separate and cannot both be positive.

engine.description: SQL Server Express, license included. Other engines and editions are outside this bounded model.

region.description: Pricing region supported by this model. It must agree with `resource.location.regionKey` when that field is supplied.

deployment.description: Single-AZ deployment. Multi-AZ pricing is not included.

instanceClass.description: Supported SQL Server Express T3 instance class. If `characteristics.size` or `instanceType` is also present, it must equal this value. Non-burstable classes are intentionally unsupported because this bounded regional Express catalog has no verified non-burstable SKU/rate; they fail validation rather than receiving a fabricated or generic fallback price.

storageType.description: General Purpose SSD storage price to apply. Additional gp3 IOPS and throughput are not modeled.

allocatedStorageGiB.description: Caller-declared allocated database storage in GiB.

durationHours.description: Billing interval in hours. Storage is prorated over a documented 730-hour reference month.

sustainedCpuPercent.description: Caller-provided constant average CPU utilization over the interval. This is neither an application-load attribution nor evidence that RdsAdminService, SQL Server, the OS, or any other process caused it.

creditMode.description: T3 Unlimited credit accounting. Disabling Unlimited is not modeled and would not remove the underlying CPU demand.

initialCreditBalance.description: Earned CPU credits available at interval start, in vCPU-minutes. Bounded by the selected class's 24-hour earning limit.

initialSurplusCreditBalance.description: Uncharged Unlimited surplus-credit debt at interval start, in vCPU-minutes. It is repaid before new credits are banked and is bounded by the selected class's 24-hour earning limit.

settleSurplusAtEnd.description: Whether to charge and clear otherwise uncharged surplus debt at interval end, representing an explicit stop/delete settlement assumption. False keeps debt up to the 24-hour cap in the ending surplus ledger.

RdsSqlServerCreditLedger.description: CPU-credit ledger for the caller-defined interval. One CPU credit is one vCPU-minute. Earned and consumed credits are totals; ending earned and surplus balances remain distinct.

earnedCredits.description: Baseline credits earned during the interval.

consumedCredits.description: Credits consumed by the declared vCPU utilization during the interval.

creditCap.description: Maximum banked earned credits or uncharged surplus debt, equal to 24 hours of baseline earnings.

endingCreditBalance.description: Earned credits remaining after consumption and repayment of any initial surplus.

endingSurplusCreditBalance.description: Uncharged Unlimited surplus debt retained at interval end; zero when end settlement is requested.

chargedCredits.description: Total credits billed as surplus, equal to overflow plus explicit end-settlement credits.

overflowChargedCredits.description: Surplus credits beyond the 24-hour uncharged debt cap.

settlementChargedCredits.description: Surplus debt charged because `settleSurplusAtEnd` was true.

RdsSqlServerBillingResult.description: Deterministic interval estimate for one bounded RDS SQL Server Express configuration. This is not an AWS invoice reconstruction. It excludes free tier, discounts, taxes, backup overage, transfer, additional gp3 IOPS/throughput, and account-specific adjustments; actual CloudWatch sampling and AWS hourly settlement can also differ.

computeCost.description: License-included Single-AZ instance cost over `durationHours`, USD.

licensingCost.description: Separate SQL Server license surcharge over the interval, USD. Zero for this bounded Express license-included catalog because licensing is already included in computeCost.

storageCost.description: Selected gp2/gp3 storage cost over `durationHours`, USD, using a 730-hour reference month.

cpuCreditCost.description: Charged Unlimited surplus-credit cost over the interval, USD.

totalCost.description: Sum of modeled instance, storage, and CPU-credit components, USD.

effectiveHourlyCost.description: Effective interval total divided by durationHours, USD/hr.

workloadVcpus.description: Fixed absolute CPU demand used for size comparisons, equal to class vCPUs times sustained CPU fraction.

assumptions.description: Human-readable pricing, interval, provenance, and exclusion assumptions that qualify this estimate.

RdsSqlServerComparison.description: Cost-only comparison returned by the existing right-sizing-hint route. Alternatives preserve the current result's absolute vCPU demand and billing interval while starting each alternative with zero earned and surplus balances. Fixed vCPU demand is a comparison assumption, not a prediction that managed-service/background CPU remains identical after resizing. Candidates unable to represent that demand without exceeding 100% CPU are omitted rather than clamped. Only verified T3 Express catalog entries are compared; no unsupported non-burstable SKU is synthesized. This does not select an architecture or recommend a migration.

comparisonBasis.description: Exact fixed-workload assumptions used across the alternatives.

recommendation.description: Always null; the bounded comparison deliberately does not choose an option.

SessionAffinity.description: Modeled sticky session cohorts for generic compute or a Kubernetes workload. Compute peers require identical config/fleetId. Existing sessions never migrate on scale-out. Owner loss disconnects them. Omission preserves ordinary routing; min=max is not affinity. These are explicit assumptions, not measured OpenShell metrics.

fleetId.description: Shared identifier grouping compute peers or Kubernetes replicas in the same session-affinity fleet.

initialSessions.description: Number of active sessions present at the start of the simulation.

arrivalsPerStep.description: New sessions arriving during each simulation step.

meanLifetimeSteps.description: Mean session lifetime in simulation steps.

requestsPerSessionPerSecond.description: Request rate generated by each active session.

maxSessionsPerOwner.description: Maximum active sessions assigned to one compute member or Kubernetes replica.

reconnect.description: Whether sessions disconnected by owner loss may reconnect on the next step.

workload.description: Required only on Kubernetes. CPU-only replica HPA independent of node scaling. Assumes scheduling capacity is available. minReplicas <= replicas <= maxReplicas.

replicas.description: Starting number of workload replicas in the Kubernetes fleet.

minReplicas.description: Minimum workload replicas allowed by replica autoscaling.

maxReplicas.description: Maximum workload replicas allowed by replica autoscaling.

capacityRpsPerReplica.description: Modeled request-per-second serving capacity of each workload replica.

SessionAffinityEvidence.description: Expected-value cohorts, explicit owner receipts and goodput ceiling, not measured provider metrics.

dataState.description: Data durability, separate from service health; permanently_lost is irreversible.

databaseRebuilt.description: Explicitly rebuilt empty database; does not restore original lost data.

type.description: Resource type. `kubernetes` models a managed container node pool (EKS / GKE / AKS / OKE / DOKS): its `characteristics.nodeCount` worker nodes autoscale between `characteristics.minNodes` and `characteristics.maxNodes`, growing both serving capacity (`maxThroughput`) and hourly cost proportionally.

location.description: Resource location for create and read. Owned typical requires regionKey us-east-2 on all four nodes; the server stores canonical use2. Do not set region under characteristics.

characteristics.description:
Provider-specific resource characteristics. For AWS RDS resources, lifecycle/support and version inputs such as `extendedSupport`, `engineVersion`, `databaseEngine`, `databaseEngineVersion`, and `dbEngineVersion` are rejected with `INVALID_FIELD`: CWM models base resource rates and behavior but does not price RDS lifecycle/support surcharges. Direct `engine` is also rejected except for literal `engine: "mysql"` as workload-only identity on the exact AWS `db.r5.large` database in the canonical owned CRUD graph; prefer `workloadDatabaseEngine: "mysql"`. This alias does not declare engine version, Extended Support, lifecycle, or billing. The bounded SQL Server Express contract instead uses `rdsSqlServerBilling.engine: "sqlserver-ex"` inside its nested, strict configuration. Arbitrary data remains supported under resource-level `metadata`. For Aurora Serverless, set ACU limits with `config.minCapacity` and `config.maxCapacity` (or flat `minCapacity` and `maxCapacity`). For AWS aurora-serverless databases with size `db.serverless`, flat `minAcu` and `maxAcu` are aliases when the corresponding canonical field is absent. Top-level and nested config aliases are rejected. A modeled two-instance pair cannot change its topology or ACU bounds through PATCH.
Owned AWS CRUD calibration eligibility is an exact predicate: exactly four healthy, routable AWS resources and exactly four edges, one internal ALB → each of two compute apps → one database, with no extra resources or edges. Both apps are `m5.large`; each absent `serviceFamily` is inferred as `ec2` for fit eligibility only, explicit `ec2` is accepted, and any other explicit family fails. The database is `db.r5.large`; absent `serviceFamily` is inferred as `rds` for eligibility only, explicit `rds` is accepted, and any conflicting explicit family fails. MySQL workload identity is required on that database: use `workloadDatabaseEngine: "mysql"` or the narrow literal `engine: "mysql"` alias described above. The alias is accepted on that database shape even in an incomplete graph but does not by itself make the graph fit-eligible. The sole network node must have explicit `serviceFamily: "alb"`, or, only when serviceFamily is absent, an unambiguous name containing `ALB` or `Application Load Balancer`; any explicit size/type discriminator must not identify NLB or another network service. A generic unnamed network/load-balancer node, explicit NLB, or contradictory discriminator is ambiguous and fails eligibility.
Each app may explicitly set `workload: "crud"` or omit the flag only for this completely matched canonical graph with MySQL identity; this is a canonical CRUD modeling assumption, not proof of actual customer workload behavior, and the inference is identified in `calibrationEvidence.note`. Explicit conflicting workload values fail. No CRUD inference applies to similar-but-not-exact graphs, another instance type/provider, or an incomplete graph. Each app must have autoscaling disabled and fixed `minInstances=maxInstances=2`; traffic must be in the inclusive 10–1,000 RPS range. There must be no active failure and no failure, warmup, or snapshot metadata. App `capacityRps`, `requestsPerSecond`, non-default `maxThroughput`, and non-default `baseLatency` overrides disqualify the fit. If supplied, database `maxConnections` must be 500 and `effectiveMaxConnections` must be absent; if supplied, ALB `maxThroughput` must be 50,000. The canonical `us-east-2` / seed `20240601` pair is the parity fixture, not evidence that another region has been measured.
The separate owned typical fit requires appWeight=typical and the same four-node topology, explicit workload="crud-typical", appRuntime="node", appWorkerCount=2 and appDbPoolSize=250 per compute node, workloadDatabaseVersion="8.0" and explicit maxConnections=500 on the MySQL database, and internal loadBalancerScheme on the ALB. Every node must declare location.regionKey="us-east-2" (stored as canonical "use2"), bounds must be fixed 2→2, and load must be 20–300 RPS. Missing identity is never inferred. Only measured 20/100/200 RPS rungs from campaign typical-v1-20260927c are fitted; 300 RPS is a holdout and 500 RPS is saturation context. Generic typical apps and the public lean benchmark do not receive this fit.
For ineligible graphs, `calibrationEvidence.kind` is `modeled` and `calibrationEvidence.note` names every actual failed eligibility check in stable order, with resource identifiers and safe expected / actual values; it must not report only a generic “not applied”. Examples include missing or ambiguous ALB identity, wrong app size or family, non-fixed instance bounds, traffic outside the range, active failure, and conflicting workload identity. For eligible graphs, evidence identifies the owned calibration and states that latency is modeled on the in-VPC ALB path, not end-to-end. No other hardware has been validated. Lean owned evidence requires root appWeight=lean; the separate typical fit requires typical. Known-vCPU serving compute uses the workload model: proportional lean AWS M5 scaling is scaled from measured. At offered application RPS T its full-precision fitted baseline is P50 = max(1.45, 2.4833 - 0.0010466*T) ms and P95 = max(P50, 3.10, 4.3697 - 0.0012973*T) ms. Topology, congestion, storage, memory, routing and failure penalties follow this baseline. There is no generic 5 ms floor on lean scaled latency; 0.05 ms is only a physical/non-finite safety floor. Other providers and generic typical/heavy are reference estimates. An explicitly identified owned typical Node CRUD setup uses its own separate three-rung fit; it does not change the lean benchmark. Unknown-vCPU fallback retains explicitly unverified generic output with no external reference. See PredictionEvidence for assumption intervals.

workload.description: Explicit application workload identity. Set to "crud-typical" only for the owned typical Node CRUD setup (see the required fields below). For lean, set "crud" on each app; each may omit its flag only when the complete exact canonical graph and MySQL database identity match; this is a modeling assumption, not evidence of actual customer workload behavior. Explicit conflicting workload values fail. See the characteristics contract for the complete gate.

appRuntime.description: Explicit runtime identity for owned typical eligibility; must be node. Not inferred from EC2.

appWorkerCount.description: Explicit workers per app host; owned typical requires two on each m5.large.

appDbPoolSize.description: Explicit database connection pool size per app host; owned typical requires 250 on each host.

loadBalancerScheme.description: Explicit ALB scheme; owned typical requires internal.

workloadDatabaseVersion.description: Workload-only MySQL version identity; owned typical requires 8.0. Does not enable RDS lifecycle or support billing inputs.

workloadDatabaseEngine.description: Preferred MySQL workload identity for the exact healthy AWS db.r5.large node in the owned CRUD graph. Literal characteristics.engine="mysql" is a workload-only alias on this exact shape; it does not declare engine version, Extended Support, lifecycle, or billing. Those inputs remain rejected. See the characteristics contract for the complete gate.

engine.description: Narrow AWS RDS workload-only alias: only literal "mysql" is accepted on the exact db.r5.large canonical owned-CRUD database; prefer workloadDatabaseEngine. Does not declare engine version, Extended Support, lifecycle, or billing capability; other engine values and lifecycle/billing inputs remain rejected.

minCapacity.description: Aurora Serverless minimum ACU (flat form; nested config takes precedence). Default 0.5. Explicit reader bounds must match the writer's cluster range; omitted reader bounds inherit it.

maxCapacity.description: Aurora Serverless maximum ACU (flat form; nested config takes precedence). Default 16. Explicit reader bounds must match the writer's cluster range; omitted reader bounds inherit it.

minAcu.description: Exact AWS Aurora Serverless v2 db.serverless shape only; alias for flat minCapacity.

maxAcu.description: Exact AWS Aurora Serverless v2 db.serverless shape only; alias for flat maxCapacity.

auroraReaderScalingMode.description: AWS Aurora Serverless v2 reader scaling: writer-mirror (default, promotion tiers 0/1) follows the writer's capacity; CPU is a modeled mirror, not independently routed load. independent (promotion tiers 2–15) uses only routed work and the ACU floor. Set on an explicit reader or on the two-instance writer to configure its generated reader. Each instance bills its own ACU-hours. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.how-it-works.html (reviewed 2026-09-25).

config.description: Aurora Serverless ACU configuration. Use minCapacity/maxCapacity, not minAcu/maxAcu. The range is cluster-wide for all Serverless v2 instances; explicit reader bounds conflicting with the writer are rejected, while omitted reader bounds inherit the writer range. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.setting-capacity.html#aurora-serverless-v2-examples-setting-capacity-range-for-cluster (reviewed 2026-09-25).

serviceFamily.description:
Provider-specific service family identifier. AWS values include: `ec2`, `ecsFargate`, `rds`, `rds-sqlserver-express`, `aurora-postgresql`, `aurora-dsql`, `aurora-serverless`, `dynamodb`, `s3`, `elb`, `cloudfront`, `lambda`. GCP values include: `gce`, `cloud-sql`, `cloud-spanner`, `bigtable-ssd`, `bigtable-hdd`, `cloudRun`, `cloudFunctions`, `gcs`, `cloud-load-balancing`. Azure values include: `azure_vm`, `azure-sql`, `azureFunctions`, `azureContainerApps`, `blob-storage`, `azure-lb`, `eventhub`. OCI values include: `oci_vm`, `ociFunctions`, `autonomous-db`, `oci-container`, `oci-lb`, `oci-streaming`. DigitalOcean values include: `droplets`, `managed_postgresql`, `spaces`, `load_balancer`.
Only for owned AWS CRUD fit eligibility, absent serviceFamily is inferred as `ec2` for exact AWS compute `m5.large` apps and `rds` for exact AWS database `db.r5.large`; explicit matching values remain valid and conflicting values fail. The sole AWS network node accepts explicit `alb`, or, only when family is absent, a resource name unambiguously containing `ALB` or `Application Load Balancer` and no contradictory size/type discriminator. These inferences are eligibility-only and do not rewrite the caller's persisted input.
Idle / residual-billing families (billed a flat rate regardless of traffic — see `characteristics.billingState`): AWS: `nat-gateway`, `vpc-endpoint`, `eip-detached`, `ebs-snapshot`, `alb-idle`. GCP: `cloud-nat`, `psc-endpoint`, `static-ip`, `pd-snapshot`, `clb-idle`. Azure: `azure-nat-gw`, `private-endpoint`, `azure-static-ip`, `disk-snapshot`, `azure-lb-idle`. OCI: `oci-reserved-ip`, `block-backup`, `oci-lb-idle`. DigitalOcean: `do-reserved-ip`, `do-vol-snapshot`, `do-lb-idle`. Snapshot/backup families bill per GB-month × `capacityGB` ÷ 730.

containerCpu.description: Request-serving compute only — runtime CPU allocation in vCPUs. For ECS/Fargate this must be supplied together with `containerMemoryGiB` and match a supported task allocation. It is canonicalized to the same allocation represented by `size`.

containerMemoryGiB.description: Request-serving compute only — runtime memory allocation in GiB. For ECS/Fargate this must be supplied together with `containerCpu` and match a supported task allocation.

vcpu.description: ECS/Fargate task vCPU allocation; equivalent to containerCpu when both are equal.

memoryGiB.description: ECS/Fargate task memory allocation; equivalent to containerMemoryGiB when both are equal.

cpuArchitecture.description: ECS/Fargate Linux architecture; ARM64 uses the separate Graviton vCPU and memory rates.

runtimeMemoryProfile.description: Optional explicit per-instance application working-set assumption. CWM never infers it from configured memory, CPU, RPS, aggregate memory telemetry, or synthetic latency. It does not alter allocated memory billing.

source.description: Provenance category for the declared working-set profile.

confidence.description: Confidence level assigned to the declared working-set profile.

limitExceededProbability.description: Only calibrated/external profiles may provide a probability.

onLimitExceeded.description: Optional bounded consequences; omitted means CWM reports only the threshold condition.

failedWorkFraction.description: Required when termination is declared; the explicit bounded fraction of work stranded by that termination.

kubernetesMemoryProfile.description: Opt-in per-replica Kubernetes memory-pressure/OOM contract. CWM never infers per-pod memory, OOM likelihood, or working-set demand from the aggregate `memoryUsage` metric, CPU, RPS, or the configured limit alone. Absent by default — kubernetes resources without a profile explicitly report `evaluationStatus: "not_evaluated"` in `metrics.kubernetesMemory`. Single-pool clusters emit one row; a cluster with `nodePools` emits one row per pool and evaluates only pools that provide their own profile. Node/replica billing is unaffected.

burstWorkingSetGiB.description: Declared transient/burst working set applied only while the replica is still warming up. Must be at least `baselineWorkingSetGiB`.

headroomGiB.description: Additional declared safety margin folded into the demand/limit comparison.

loadBreakpoints.description: Declared working-set curve keyed on per-replica RPS, in strictly ascending `perReplicaRps` order. CWM interpolates linearly between breakpoints, and below the first breakpoint ramps linearly from the idle `baselineWorkingSetGiB` anchor up to the first breakpoint's declared value. Above the last breakpoint, behavior is governed by `extrapolation` — it never assumes a linear RPS-to-memory relationship beyond what is declared or implied by that policy.

perReplicaRps.description: Per-replica request rate at which the declared working-set value applies.

workingSetGiB.description: Declared per-replica working-set demand at this load, in GiB.

extrapolation.description: Behavior above the highest declared loadBreakpoint. "linear" (default, preserves pre-existing behavior) extrapolates the final declared segment's slope beyond the last breakpoint. "clamp" holds demand flat at the last breakpoint's `workingSetGiB` value for any RPS beyond it — for curves known to plateau (e.g. a connection-pool- or cache-bounded working set). Only governs the region above the last breakpoint; the below-first-breakpoint ramp is unaffected either way.

source.description: Provenance category for the declared working-set profile.

confidence.description: Confidence level assigned to the declared working-set profile.

restartDelaySteps.description: Bounded restart/readiness delay measured in simulation steps before an OOMKilled replica rejoins serving capacity.

restartDelaySeconds.description: Deprecated compatibility input. This historical spelling is normalized as simulation steps, not wall-clock seconds; use restartDelaySteps.

maxConcurrentRestartFraction.description: Upper bound on the fraction of replicas that may be mid-restart at once, modeling k8s's staggered pod eviction/restart behavior.

memoryAwareAutoscaling.description: Opt-in: when true, the modeled memory-pressure ratio can also trigger HPA scale-out alongside the existing CPU-only default. Leaving this unset/false keeps CPU-only scale-out decisions byte-identical.

memoryScaleOutThresholdRatio.description: Demand/limit ratio at or above which memory-aware scale-out engages. Only consulted when `memoryAwareAutoscaling` is true.

kubernetesMemoryEvidence.description: Observed configuration from a standard Kubernetes Deployment or StatefulSet. These source-labelled request/limit facts are never treated as runtime working-set demand and do not activate OOM, restart, capacity, latency, error, autoscaling, or billing effects.

source.description: Manifest source category for the observed configuration.

sourceFile.description: Repository-relative path of the manifest containing this configuration.

kind.description: Kubernetes workload kind that declares the memory configuration.

workload.description: Name of the Deployment or StatefulSet that supplied the configuration.

replicas.description: Literal replica count declared by the workload, when available.

status.description: Whether the manifest memory configuration was fully and unambiguously extracted.

requestGiB.description: Observed per-replica memory request from the manifest, in GiB.

limitGiB.description: Observed per-replica memory limit from the manifest, in GiB.

reason.description: Specific reason extraction was incomplete or unsupported.

eksSpotInterruption.description: Opt-in deterministic AWS EKS Spot interruption lifecycle. Ordinary Spot pricing and risk behavior is unchanged when this object is absent. `triggerAtStep` is a simulation step; the interruption notice is always a bounded 120 simulated seconds.

healthChecks.description: Opt-in dependency-aware load-balancer and Kubernetes endpoint probes. Omission preserves existing simulation behavior. Dependency resource IDs are explicit graph references; livenessOnly checks do not depend on downstream resources.

desiredTaskCount.description: ECS/Fargate only — initial desired running task count. With ECS CPU target tracking, the declared minimum is used when omitted. Fargate never uses generic compute cloning.

minTaskCount.description: ECS/Fargate only — smallest running task fleet, including zero for scale-to-zero services.

maxTaskCount.description: ECS/Fargate only — hard task-fleet ceiling. Offered traffic above total task capacity queues and can produce latency/errors.

perTaskCapacityRps.description: ECS/Fargate only — modeled serving capacity of one running task in requests per second; it may differ by service/tier and is not a provider performance guarantee.

perTaskCapacityEvidence.description: Caller-supplied evidence. Without a documented/measured basis and supporting source, the rate is labeled an assumption. Guesses must not be called measured.

basis.description: documented/measured are caller assertions and require a supporting source; assumption is unverified.

source.description: Supporting public document URL, report, or measurement reference. Required for documented or measured basis.

applicationAutoscalingPolicy.description: Effective ECS CPU-only target-tracking policy when ecsCpuTargetTracking is enabled on create, or an explicitly supplied ECS policy.

taskStartupSeconds.description: ECS/Fargate only — modeled task startup wait in simulation steps (approximately seconds).

fargateApplicationModel.description: Explicit application assumptions, not native ECS or ALB behavior. The FIFO counts pending requests separately from goodput. Idle/wake requires an explicit timed target-tracking policy and minimum task count zero.

appReadySteps.description: Request-serving compute only — modeled application-readiness ramp after a task or instance becomes active. Zero keeps the default binary-ready behavior.

taskScaleDownSeconds.description: ECS/Fargate only — modeled quiet-period wait before a Fargate task is stopped.

concurrency.description:
Request-serving compute only — maximum simultaneous requests per
 active instance or replica. Capacity is derived from this value
 and requestDurationSeconds; Lambda is constrained to 1.

requestDurationSeconds.description:
Request-serving compute only — modeled request duration in seconds.
 Each provider policy applies its documented billing granularity
 separately from capacity calculations.

requestServingTargetUtilizationPct.description: AWS Lambda only — modeled scale-out target as a percentage of active-environment capacity. A value below 100% reserves request headroom; when omitted, scaling targets full modeled capacity.

provisionedInstances.description: Explicit ready capacity. It raises the warm floor and accrues the provider's warm/provisioned capacity charge.

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: Idle period before a scale-to-zero eligible service releases non-required warm capacity.

requestServingKind.description: Declares whether this request-serving resource follows function or HTTP container lifecycle semantics.

billingState.description: Residual billing state for idle-infrastructure cost simulation. `active` (default) — normal billing. `idle` — resource exists but serves no traffic; idle-family resources bill their flat residual rate. `stopped` — stopped compute/database: instance cost is $0 but any `capacityGB` storage keeps billing. `detached` — unattached IP / orphaned network artifact; bills the unattached rate for its `serviceFamily`. `deleted` — removed via idle-resource remediation; skipped entirely by the cost engine.

size.description: Provider size/SKU label. For `serviceFamily: ecsFargate`, use an exact canonical allocation label such as `0.5 vCPU / 1 GB` or `1 vCPU / 2 GB`. A label and explicit `containerCpu`/`containerMemoryGiB` pair are equivalent; if both are supplied they must match. Unsupported, malformed, incomplete, or conflicting Fargate shapes return `INVALID_FARGATE_TASK_SIZE`. The default `0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GB` is used only when neither sizing form is supplied.

instanceType.description: Compatibility alias for `size`, commonly used for AWS EC2 instance types such as `t3.medium`. When `size` is omitted, this value is canonicalized into `size` and resolved through the provider catalog. If both fields are supplied they must be identical; `size` is the canonical field. Unknown values remain visible as unrecognized SKUs and use the normal estimated fallback coverage.

ocpus.description: OCI flexible compute capacity input, with family-specific documented limits validated against the selected shape. VM.Standard.E4.Flex accepts an explicit positive integer from 1 through 64 for catalog-backed capacity resolution. OCI x86 maps 1 OCPU to 2 vCPUs; this hardware specification does not establish provider-specific performance, throughput, latency, or price. Memory is independently selected and is not inferred as a fixed amount per OCPU. Invalid counts are rejected; omitting the count leaves a flexible shape explicitly generic.

capacityRps.description: Compute only — the literal per-node RPS ceiling: the request rate at which this node reaches ~95% CPU (critical territory). When supplied, the engine converts it to an internal `effectiveMaxThroughput = capacityRps / criticalUtilThreshold` using the provider's calibrated saturation coefficient, so the CPU curve peaks at the stated capacity without changing any accuracy calibration. Agents that know their workload's RPS capacity can set this field instead of tuning `maxThroughput` directly. Simulations that omit `capacityRps` fall back to `maxThroughput` with byte-identical behaviour. Kubernetes create requests containing `capacityRps` are rejected; use `maxThroughput` for the total Kubernetes cluster RPS ceiling, or `nodePools[].maxThroughput` for per-node pool capacity.

maxConnections.description: Database only — the connection-pool capacity (maximum concurrent connections) for a database resource. The simulation models connection-pool pressure as `activeConnections / maxConnections` (surfaced as `metrics.connection_pressure`), so raising this value gives the database more headroom before the pool saturates. Aurora Serverless v2 retains an explicit limit at every ACU; when omitted, the PostgreSQL estimate derives from maximum configured ACU (16 ACU with minimum 2 gives 3360). Other databases retain their existing defaults.

connectionDemand.description: Database only. Omit to retain load-derived connection demand. declaredConnections and idlePoolFloor are ASSUMPTION / plan-time budgets (for example, replicas × per-pod pool size), not observed live DB connections. `declared` ignores instantaneous RPS; `max` takes the greatest of load-derived demand and the declared/floor values. Connection-pressure metrics report both load-derived and selected demand, plus the mode that drove pressure. This setting does not change cost or modeled database CPU/latency. Above the usable limit, declared demand adds a rule-based pool-saturation error signal (up to the existing 5% component cap); below the limit, provider-fit baseline errors remain load-derived unless saturationErrorThreshold is configured. That optional threshold suppresses pool errors below the configured aggregate utilization and applies the provider error curve to utilization beyond it; set the same threshold on every database in a multi-database graph. It does not change capacity, and this thresholded curve is not provider-calibrated.

saturationErrorThreshold.description: Optional utilization threshold for the load-derived pool error curve. Below it, pool saturation adds no errors; above it, the curve uses utilization beyond the threshold. In graphs with multiple databases, set the same value on all databases. This does not change connection capacity.

multiAz.description: For AWS Aurora Serverless v2, true with instanceCount 2 creates a separately billed reader in another AZ. Legacy true without instanceCount has no inferred reader and emits a normalized-config warning.

instanceCount.description: For generic compute, this fixes the number of represented VMs (integer 1–100); capacity is aggregated and CPU is reported per VM. It cannot be combined with autoscaling:true, minInstances or maxInstances. For AWS Aurora Serverless v2, supported values remain 1 with multiAz false or 2 with multiAz true; two instances have separate ACU charges. Conflicting explicit replicas, unknown AZs and unsupported families are rejected. A writer's derived reader has id <writer-id>-reader, characteristics.replicaOf and a distinct location.zoneKey.

replicaOf.description: Database only — explicit ID of the writer this independently modeled healthy database can replace during a chaos database_crash. Promotion defaults to 30 simulation seconds; otherwise the sole writer remains down for the injection duration plus a modeled 1800-second restart delay. Chaos custom injections can override these delays. These are assumptions, not AWS SLAs. A supported Aurora Serverless v2 multiAz:true and instanceCount:2 pair creates this explicit relationship during simulation creation; multiAz alone does not.

auroraStandbyResourceId.description: Opt-in modeled Aurora writer failover. On an AWS Aurora database writer, reference the ID of a distinct healthy AWS Aurora database standby in this simulation. A supported Aurora Serverless v2 multiAz:true and instanceCount:2 pair populates this reference. multiAz alone does not imply standby capacity. Quick inject-failure models a one-step promotion interruption, then reduced DB failure impact while the writer remains parked. No AWS calls or observed failover timing.

capacityGB.description: Storage only — provisioned storage capacity in gigabytes for a storage/volume resource. Used together with `maxIops` to model block-storage throughput and IOPS utilization.

maxIops.description: Storage only — the provisioned maximum IOPS (I/O operations per second) for a block-storage volume. The simulation models storage IOPS utilization against this ceiling (surfaced as `metrics.storageIopsUtilization`). Falls back to the provider's default volume profile IOPS when omitted.

inferenceMode.description: Kubernetes only — marks a GPU/inference cluster. When `true` the engine bills each worker node at the provider's GPU node rate and emits the inference economics metrics (`metrics.gpuUtilization`, `metrics.tokensPerSecond`, `metrics.costPerMillionTokens`). GPU clusters also participate in idle-GPU detection (sustained utilization below 15% fires an idle-candidate event with the monthly waste estimate) and the GPU right-sizing hints (`gpu-underutilized`, `gpu-saturated`, `gpu-api-breakeven`).

accelerator.description: Kubernetes + `inferenceMode` only — the GPU/accelerator type of the node pool. Known values: `a10g` (AWS g5), `t4` (GCP), `a10-fractional` (Azure NC8ads_A10_v4 — 1/3 A10 partition at one-third of full-A10 throughput), `a10` (OCI VM.GPU.A10.1 — full A10), `h100` (DigitalOcean GPU Droplet). Determines the per-node token throughput used to derive `metrics.tokensPerSecond` and `metrics.costPerMillionTokens`.

managedComputePlatform.description: Kubernetes + `inferenceMode` only — managed AI platform overlay running on top of the underlying cloud provider. When set to `nvidia-dgx-cloud`, the resource is an NVIDIA DGX Cloud node (e.g. `dgx-h200`, `dgx-b200`, `gb200-nvl72`) hosted on the provider named in `provider` (azure/gcp/oci) — the provider drives region and base pricing while the platform drives billing semantics (bundled control plane and fabric networking). `nvidia-dgx-cloud-lepton` is reserved for future multi-provider placement.

openshiftOffering.description:
Kubernetes-only distribution overlay. The resource `provider` remains the backing substrate for regions, network behavior, worker-node pricing, and provider latency. `rosa-hcp` and `rosa-classic` require AWS; `aro` requires Azure; `openshift-dedicated` supports AWS or GCP; and `self-managed` supports any existing CWM backing provider. Platform/licensing charges are additive to worker-node charges, and cost breakdowns identify worker, platform, and control-plane rows separately. AWS publishes ROSA's $0.171 per 4-vCPU worker service fee uniformly across supported standard regions and its ROSA HCP $0.25 per-cluster-hour fee. Azure publishes the ARO D4s v3 (4 vCPU) East US OpenShift line at $124.830/month, separate from the $160.60/month Linux VM line ($0.171/hour using 730 hours/month). Verified 2026-08-27 at https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/openshift/. A three-worker, 2-vCPU-per-worker topology derives a valid $0.2565/hour platform total from that unit rate ($0.171 × 6 ÷ 4); it is not an independent published rate. The published ARO platform unit rate is marked `official` only when the resource location is Azure East US; resources in another region, or without a region, retain the East US amount as an estimate/reference assumption. OpenShift
 Dedicated and self-managed subscription allocations remain
 estimated where no comparable universal hourly line is
 published. Omit this field for byte-compatible generic
 Kubernetes.

topology.description:
Kubernetes + `inferenceMode` only — categorical GPU interconnect topology of the node. Two independent fields govern two independent efficiency coefficients.
`intraNode` (inference): bounds tensor-parallel serving efficiency within a single node (PCIe 0.70, NVLink 0.85, NVLink+NVSwitch 0.92, InfiniBand 0.80). Omitting `intraNode` yields exactly 1.0, preserving pre-topology behavior.
`interNode` (distributed training, `trainingMode: true` + more than one node): bounds collective-communication (all-reduce) efficiency across N DGX nodes (InfiniBand 0.90, NVLink+NVSwitch 0.88, NVLink 0.82, PCIe/Ethernet 0.65). Ignored for inference resources and for single-node training (where there is no inter-node all-reduce); absent `interNode` yields exactly 1.0.
Flat-form aliases: `characteristics.intraNode` and `characteristics.interNode` (top-level, same enum) are also accepted and normalized into this nested `topology` object at the API boundary. The nested value wins when both shapes are present; only the nested form is stored and echoed back.

intraNode.description: GPU-to-GPU interconnect within a single node. Applied to inference resources (default); ignored when `trainingMode: true`.

interNode.description: Node-to-node fabric for distributed training. Applied only when `trainingMode: true` and node count > 1; ignored for inference resources and single-node training.

intraNode.description: Flat-form alias for `topology.intraNode`. Normalized into the nested `topology` object at the API boundary before storage; the nested value wins when both are present. Only the nested form is stored and echoed back.

interNode.description: Flat-form alias for `topology.interNode`. Normalized into the nested `topology` object at the API boundary before storage; the nested value wins when both are present. Only the nested form is stored and echoed back.

includesControlPlane.description: Kubernetes only — when `true`, the managed platform's node rate already bundles the Kubernetes control plane, so the per-hour managed-K8s cluster fee is skipped at every billing surface. Set by DGX Cloud resources; absent/false preserves standard provider billing.

bundledNetworking.description: Kubernetes only — when `true`, high-performance fabric networking (e.g. InfiniBand) is bundled into the platform node rate rather than billed separately. Declarative flag set by DGX Cloud resources; informational in Phase 1.

trainingMode.description: Kubernetes + `inferenceMode` only — when `true`, the resource models a distributed-training workload across multiple DGX nodes. The simulation engine applies the inter-node topology coefficient (`topology.interNode`) to bound aggregate throughput by the collective-communication (all-reduce) efficiency of the cross-node fabric: InfiniBand 0.90, NVLink-Switch 0.88, NVLink 0.82, PCIe/Ethernet 0.65. When `false` or absent (default), inference mode is used and `topology.interNode` is ignored — behaviour is byte-identical to resources created before this field existed.

tokensPerRequest.description: Kubernetes + `inferenceMode` only — average output tokens generated per inference request. Bounds token throughput by request demand (`throughputRps × tokensPerRequest`) and drives the decode component of the inference latency model (`latencyP50/P95/P99`). Defaults to 500 when omitted.

inputTokensPerRequest.description: Kubernetes + `inferenceMode` only — average prompt (prefill) tokens per inference request. Drives the time-to-first-token component of the inference latency model. Defaults to `2 × tokensPerRequest` (a typical ⅔-input / ⅓-output chat mix) when omitted.

cacheHitRate.description: Cache / CDN only — the expected cache hit rate as a fraction between 0 and 1 (e.g. `0.85` = 85%). Higher values reduce the load that reaches downstream origin/database resources and lower effective latency. Defaults to 0.8 when omitted for cache resources. Declared request-flow caches must specify it explicitly.

cacheableRequestShare.description: Optional request-flow assumption for an explicitly modeled cache: the fraction of offered requests that are eligible for cache lookup. Cache hits reduce downstream work only within this share; remaining traffic bypasses the cache. This is a scenario assumption, not a measured production request distribution.

asynchronousRequestShare.description: Optional request-flow assumption for an explicitly modeled queue: the fraction of offered requests enqueued for asynchronous processing. Queue consumers pass work downstream at their configured drain rate; queued messages do not reach databases until consumed. Cacheable and asynchronous shares must sum to at most 1.

queueConsumerCount.description: Number of modeled consumers for an explicitly configured queue. Total drain capacity is this count multiplied by `queueDrainRatePerConsumerRps`.

queueDrainRatePerConsumerRps.description: Modeled messages consumed per second by each queue consumer. This is a disclosed scenario assumption, not a provider-measured throughput guarantee.

queueCapacityMessages.description: Explicit queue backlog capacity in messages. Queue fill is backlog divided by this capacity, not offered RPS divided by maximum throughput.

queueSimulationStepSeconds.description: Simulation window in seconds used to convert per-second queue enqueue and drain rates into backlog messages.

autoscaling.description: Compute only — marks a compute resource as the autoscaling primary. When multiple compute resources exist, the engine uses the one flagged `autoscaling: true` as the autoscaling target; otherwise it falls back to the first compute resource.

maxInstances.description: Compute only — hard per-resource ceiling for RL `scale_out`. For request-serving services, this is the maximum active instances, replicas, or Lambda concurrent execution environments; it caps capacity and sheds excess demand rather than creating VM clones. For regular compute, it constrains the effective maximum below the simulation-wide autoscaling limit.

minInstances.description: Compute only — hard per-resource floor for RL `scale_in`. For request-serving services, this is the minimum warm instance or replica floor (raised by `provisionedInstances` when larger). For regular compute, it prevents scale-in below the declared floor.

scaleOutCpuThreshold.description: Compute or Kubernetes — overrides the simulation-wide CPU autoscaling scale-out target (`autoscalingConfig.scaleOutCpuThreshold`, also settable via the top-level `autoscalingTargetCpu` / `scaleOutCpuThreshold` / `scaleOutCpuPercent` / `autoscaleTargetCpuPercent` aliases) for THIS resource's scale decisions only — every other resource in the simulation keeps using the simulation-wide default. Lets, for example, one GKE cluster scale out at 60% while an EC2 fleet in the same simulation scales out at 80%. Absent → this resource follows the simulation-wide default (byte-identical to before this field existed).

scaleInCpuThreshold.description: Compute or Kubernetes — overrides the simulation-wide CPU autoscaling scale-in target (`autoscalingConfig.scaleInCpuThreshold`) for THIS resource's scale decisions only. Absent → this resource follows the simulation-wide default.
