nodeCount.description: Kubernetes only — the current number of worker nodes in the managed node pool. The cluster's `maxThroughput` and hourly cost scale proportionally with this count as autoscaling adds/removes nodes.

workerVcpu.description: Kubernetes OpenShift only — vCPU capacity of each worker node used to prorate published platform or license fees billed per 4 vCPU-hours. Defaults to the canonical 2-vCPU worker when no size is recognized; set explicitly for custom shapes.

minNodes.description: Kubernetes only — the minimum number of worker nodes the node pool will scale in to. Defaults to the provider autoscaling profile minimum when omitted.

maxNodes.description: Kubernetes only — the maximum number of worker nodes the node pool will scale out to. Defaults to the provider autoscaling profile maximum when omitted.

perNodeRate.description: inferenceMode Kubernetes only — caller-supplied GPU node hourly rate (USD/hr per worker node). Use this when the cluster size is not in the CWM GPU catalog (GPU_LARGE_NODE_HOURLY_RATES) to restore cost modeling for the unknown SKU. Must be strictly positive; zero and negative values are rejected (a zero rate looks "free" to any consumer that skips the costFidelity field, which recreates the false-precision problem this field was designed to solve). When absent and the SKU is also unrecognised, the cluster cost is excluded from the aggregate total and costComplete is set to false in the step response.

pricingModel.description: Compute and Kubernetes only — the pricing model for worker instances. `on-demand` (default) uses standard pay-as-you-go rates. `spot` applies the provider's spot/preemptible discount to reduce instance cost significantly (AWS/GCP/Azure: ~60% off on-demand; OCI: exactly 50% off) at the cost of potential interruption when the cloud provider needs capacity back. Non-compute resource types (database, storage, network, etc.) and DigitalOcean resources (which have no spot offering) ignore this field.

eksSpotMigration.description: AWS EKS Kubernetes Spot interruption model. Opt-in only. When enabled, CWM emits a bounded 120-second interruption notice, workload migration/readiness progress, and a separate deadline hit/miss result. Migration evidence is not the same as sustained service-health recovery.

migrationDurationSeconds.description: Optional deterministic scenario override. When omitted, CWM derives migration duration from image pull, scheduling, and startup inputs.

nodePools.description: Kubernetes only — multiple node pools per cluster. When present, each pool scales independently within its own min/max bounds and is billed at its own per-node hourly rate. The legacy single-pool fields (`nodeCount`, `minNodes`, `maxNodes`) are used only when `nodePools` is absent.

nodeCount.description: Current number of worker nodes in this pool. Scales proportionally with the pool's serving capacity and cost as autoscaling adds/removes nodes.

workerVcpu.description: Kubernetes OpenShift only — vCPU capacity of each worker node in this pool for published per-4-vCPU platform or license fee proration. Falls back to the cluster-level workerVcpu, recognized size, or 2 vCPU.

minNodes.description: Minimum number of worker nodes this pool will scale in to. Defaults to the provider autoscaling profile minimum when omitted.

maxNodes.description: Maximum number of worker nodes this pool will scale out to. Defaults to the provider autoscaling profile maximum when omitted.

perNodeRate.description: Hourly cost per node for this pool, USD/hr. Must be strictly positive (zero and negative values are rejected). Falls back to the provider default rate when omitted.

maxThroughput.description: Per-node serving capacity (requests/second) for this pool. When pools carry different instance sizes, the engine uses these values to compute the correct CPU credit on scale events — a pool of large nodes relieves more load per node added or removed than a pool of small nodes. Falls back to a uniform distribution of the cluster's total `maxThroughput` across all nodes when omitted (preserving backwards-compatible behaviour for homogeneous fleets).

streamShardsCount.description: DynamoDB only — number of shards provisioned for the DynamoDB Stream attached to this table. Each shard processes up to 1 000 records/s. When write throughput (see `streamWriteRps`) exceeds the total shard capacity, the simulation engine accumulates iterator age (seconds) and emits a `stream_lag` warning event. The iterator age is drained proportionally when traffic falls back within shard capacity. Ignored on non-DynamoDB resources.

streamWriteRps.description: DynamoDB only — explicit write throughput (records/s) for the DynamoDB Stream. When omitted the engine estimates write load as 10 % of the current simulation traffic. Providing an explicit value is useful when the stream write pattern is decoupled from the simulated request traffic (e.g. bulk imports or batch pipelines that run independently). Ignored when `streamShardsCount` is 0 or absent.

eventNotificationsEnabled.description: Storage event notifications — when true the engine models event notification delivery latency: baseline 1 500 ms, rising by 1 ms per 10 RPS above 5 000 RPS, capped at 30 000 ms. The latency penalty is propagated to downstream serverless compute resources (Lambda for S3, Cloud Functions for GCS, Azure Functions for Azure Blob via Event Grid, OCI Functions for OCI Object Storage). A `notification_delayed` warning event is emitted once when simulation traffic exceeds 20 000 RPS and cleared when traffic drops back below that threshold. Supported providers: `aws` (S3), `gcp` (GCS), `azure` (Blob Storage), `oci` (Object Storage). Ignored on non-storage resources and OCI block-volume resources.

partitionCount.description: Azure Event Hubs only — number of partitions provisioned on the event hub. Each partition processes up to `partitionWriteRps` write records/s (defaults to 1 000 records/s per partition when omitted). When write throughput exceeds total partition capacity the engine accumulates `partitionLag` (seconds) in resource metadata and emits a `partition_lag` warning event when lag exceeds 30 s. Ignored on non-eventhub resources.

streamPartitions.description: OCI Streaming only — number of stream partitions. Uses the same Kafka-style offset lag model as Azure Event Hubs `partitionCount`. When absent the engine falls back to `partitionCount`. A `stream_lag` warning event fires when lag exceeds 30 s. Ignored on non-oci-streaming resources.

partitionWriteRps.description: Azure Event Hubs / OCI Streaming only — total write records/second produced into the event stream by all upstream writers combined. When omitted the engine estimates write load as 10 % of the current simulation traffic. Each partition handles 1 000 records/s; lag accumulates when `partitionWriteRps` exceeds `partitionCount × 1 000` (Event Hubs) or `streamPartitions × 1 000` (OCI Streaming).

warmupSteps.description: Compute and Kubernetes only — length of the JIT/CPU warm-up window in simulation steps. The capacity penalty is steepest on the first step (counter 0) and decays linearly to zero once the counter reaches this value, after which the resource operates at full capacity. Falls back to the engine default of 3 when omitted. A longer window models runtimes that take many steps to reach full throughput (e.g. JVM + JIT compilation, Python ML model loading); a value of 1 produces a single-step burst followed immediately by full capacity (useful for static binaries or pre-warmed containers). Ignored on non-compute resource types.

warmupSeverity.description: Compute and Kubernetes only — peak fraction by which effective capacity is reduced on the first warm-up step. For example, `0.8` reduces capacity to 20 % of its normal value on step 0. The penalty decays linearly to 0 across the `warmupSteps` window. Falls back to the engine default of `0.5` (capacity halved) when omitted. Use higher values (closer to 1) to model cold-start-heavy stacks such as JVM applications or services that load large ML models at start; use lower values to model near-instant start-ups; set to `0` to disable the warm-up capacity penalty entirely. Ignored on non-compute resource types.

routedRps.description:
Compute and Kubernetes only — effective requests per second routed to this resource during the most recent simulation step. Only present on compute and kubernetes resources in step responses (`POST /simulations/{id}/step`); absent on GET and on non-compute, non-kubernetes resource types.
The value is a float (one decimal place) so per-node values sum exactly to the simulation-level traffic without integer rounding error. For an ALB topology with three nodes at 45 RPS total all three nodes report `routedRps: 15.0`; if one node is killed the two surviving nodes each report `routedRps: 22.5` (the killed node's share is redistributed to the survivors). A node that is failed or parked reports `routedRps: 0.0`. Kubernetes clusters in an ALB topology report the per-cluster share of the routed traffic.

availabilityState.description:
Compute, Kubernetes, and Database only — explicit availability classification set by the step pipeline after traffic redistribution is finalised. Absent on resource types where availability is not tracked (network, storage, cache, queue, security).
`"available"` — the resource is healthy and serving traffic normally.
`"degraded"` — the resource is under stress (`status: "critical"` or `"warning"`) but still serving positive traffic. `isRoutable` is `true`. A saturated DB with many open connections that is still handling requests correctly shows `"degraded"`, NOT `"unavailable"` — `status: "critical"` alone does not imply unavailability.
`"unavailable"` — the resource is not serving any traffic: it is parked-critical (cpuUsage=0 and/or maxThroughput=0 while status=critical), downed by an AZ outage, or removed by an instance_kill failure. `isRoutable` is `false`.
`"scaled_to_zero"` — an ECS Fargate service has no running tasks after scale-in. `"cold_start"` — an ECS Fargate service has no task ready to serve while tasks start. Both states have `isRoutable: false`; neither means a failed or parked resource.
The field is optional for backward compatibility with stored snapshots that predate this field; it is always present on resources returned by step endpoints.

isRoutable.description:
Compute, Kubernetes, and Database only — whether this resource is receiving routed traffic during the current simulation step.
`true` for resources with `availabilityState` of `"available"` or `"degraded"`. `false` for resources with `availabilityState` of `"unavailable"`, `"scaled_to_zero"`, or `"cold_start"`.
Absent on resource types where availability is not tracked (network, storage, cache, queue, security), and absent on stored snapshots that predate this field.

recoveryBlockedReason.description:
When the recovery cooldown is not advancing because an engine guard blocked the demotion step, this field names the active guard. Absent when no guard is active and the resource is progressing normally through its cooldown arc.
`"failure_park_window"` — the node was explicitly failed via injectNodeFailure and the minimum park-window has not yet elapsed; cooldownSteps is counting up toward the window boundary, not down toward healthy.
`"idle_cpu_floor"` — the resource is parked-critical but the estimated idle CPU is still above the recovery threshold, so it cannot heal yet.
The field is cleared (absent) on every step where neither guard fires.

failureParkStepsRemaining.description:
Compute and Kubernetes only — number of simulation steps remaining in the forced unavailability window after an `inject-failure` call. Present only on step responses (`POST /simulations/{id}/step`); absent on GET responses, on resources that were not explicitly failed via `inject-failure`, and when the forced window has expired (value would be 0, so the field is omitted instead).
The value counts down from `parkSteps - 1` on the first step after failure injection toward 0 on the last step of the park window, where `parkSteps` is `recoveryPolicy.failureParkSteps` when supplied and otherwise `recoveryPolicy.criticalSteps` (default 4, so the initial value is typically 3). Once the field is absent the node enters its organic cooldown-demotion recovery arc: it transitions critical → warning → healthy over subsequent steps.

recoveryPolicy.description: Per-resource recovery thresholds that control how quickly the simulation transitions a resource from critical → warning → healthy. The four cooldown fields default to the global values (criticalCpuThreshold: 80, criticalSteps: 4, warningCpuThreshold: 70, warningSteps: 3) when omitted. `failureParkSteps`, when supplied, controls only the bounded unavailability window for the quick `inject-failure` flow; after that window the node can rejoin routing and continues through organic critical → warning → healthy cooldown. It must be at least 1. Use the persistent `instance_down` failure plus `recover-resource` when the node must remain unavailable until an explicit recovery action. Stateless microservices can use lower thresholds and fewer steps to heal faster; databases can use higher thresholds and more steps for a stricter recovery window.

criticalCpuThreshold.description: CPU must drop to or below this percentage before the critical → warning cooldown clock starts.

criticalSteps.description: Number of consecutive simulation steps the CPU must stay below criticalCpuThreshold before transitioning from critical to warning.

warningCpuThreshold.description: CPU must drop to or below this percentage before the warning → healthy cooldown clock starts.

warningSteps.description: Number of consecutive simulation steps the CPU must stay below warningCpuThreshold before transitioning from warning to healthy.

failureParkSteps.description: Number of simulation steps that a node failed through the quick inject-failure flow remains unavailable before it may rejoin routing. When omitted, criticalSteps is used. Zero is rejected.

appWeightDefaulted.description: True only when the create request omitted appWeight. Immutable intake provenance.

scenarioAttribution.description: Trusted server-side attribution copied from the live scenario catalog; absent for explicit resource-graph creates.

id.description: Live scenario catalog ID that supplied the simulation graph

scenarioHash.description: Canonical SHA-256 of the persisted scenario graph and attached traffic-pattern order.

effectiveConfigHash.description: Versioned prediction SHA-256 over the replay startup-input hash, engine version, and calibration identity. The original replay-only hash remains at replayIdentity.effectiveConfigHash.

predictionEffectiveConfigHash.description: Engine-versioned prediction identity, separate from the replay-input identity.

engineVersion.description: Simulation engine version used to produce the prediction.

resilienceConfig.description:
Optional retry/cascade resilience model. When present, the step engine
models retry amplification, circuit-breaker state, rate limiting, and
cascading-failure depth across declared dependencies. Absent means the
resilience model is disabled for this simulation (existing simulations are
byte-identical and unaffected).

scenarioHash.description: Canonical SHA-256 of the persisted scenario graph and attached traffic-pattern order.

effectiveConfigHash.description: Canonical SHA-256 of the effective six-control startup configuration.

AppWeight.description:
Immutable root-level simulation.create input. Omission selects typical and
appWeightDefaulted=true; explicit typical has identical numerical predictions.
In the generic fallback at 100 total RPS across two m5.large apps (50 per server), typical targets
20% app-host CPU, P50 18.5 ms and P95 45 ms, not the deliberately lean
benchmark's 1.9% CPU. These are placeholder guidance, not AWS measurements;
the separately eligible owned typical Node CRUD workload uses its measured
20/100/200 RPS fit instead.
Heavy doubles typical load/latency multipliers as an unsupported product assumption.

reason.description: Names the unresolved Fargate shape, missing workload-specific latency calibration, and applicable per-edge timeout boundary.

PredictionEvidence.description:
Versioned provenance of prediction basis, not a claim simulated outputs were
observed. CPU is mean serving app-host CPU (not aggregate cpuUsage); no apps
means appCpu=null and an empty per-resource array. `latencyP99Basis`
independently identifies the P99 basis: owned in-VPC internal-ALB fit,
scaled from that fit (not directly measured), or uncalibrated generic P99.
`predictionEvidence.latencyP99`, when present, carries P99's evidenceLevel
and low/central/high assumption interval; it is prediction provenance, not
observed simulated output, and not a statistical confidence interval.
When `latencyPercentileStatus` is unavailable, public latency percentiles
are null; a serving resource without a modeled latency distribution does not
support P50/P95/P99. Fargate allocation/billing/capacity facts alone do not
establish workload latency. Resilience `timeoutMs` is a per-edge, per-attempt deadline
over local service time, target base latency, injected latency, and queued wait,
not a deadline against aggregate chain percentiles.
Historical evidence may omit or null this optional quantity. `latencyBasis`
names the general modeled latency path; use `latencyP99Basis` for P99.
Ranges are assumption intervals, not confidence intervals. Measured lean
uses 0.65–1.35 times the center; lean proportional AWS M5 scaling uses
CPU 0.40–1.60 and latency 0.50–1.50 times the final reported
P50/P95 centers (after applicable penalties). The lean scaled
baseline uses offered application RPS T: P50 =
max(1.45, 2.4833 - 0.0010466*T) ms, P95 =
max(P50, 3.10, 4.3697 - 0.0012973*T) ms (full-precision fit).
On the exact healthy lean owned ALB → 2× m5.large → MySQL db.r5.large
graph at 10–1,000 offered target RPS, P99 uses
max(final P95, 7.021919127633514 + 0.00027013891327780484*T) ms,
fitted by ordinary least squares on the owned campaign's 10/100/500
RPS P99 measurements. The 1,000-RPS point is a holdout, not a fit point.
The owned fit is a prediction, not a new observed sample or a provider
measurement. Exact eligible P99 uses 0.65–1.35× assumption bounds;
analogous lean M5 sizes use the fit as scaling (0.50–1.50× within
range), not direct measurement. Beyond 1,000 RPS scaling/extrapolation
uses 0.25–2.00×. Generic typical/heavy and ineligible paths retain the generic,
unverified P99 formula, with 0.50–2.00× bounds in-range and 0.25–3.00×
beyond. Active failures disqualify a healthy measured P99 claim. The
exact owned typical Node CRUD path instead fits P99 from 20/100/200
RPS measurements; this is a prediction, not an observed output or a
general typical-app reference. Its 300 RPS holdout is not fitted.
Matching one- and three-app-server topologies are explicitly labeled
owned-scaled and derive app CPU/latency/goodput from equivalent
two-server fit load (2 × total RPS ÷ app-server count); their server
counts were not measured. Database CPU and connection demand still use
total offered traffic. One server at 300 total RPS requires a 600 RPS
equivalent fit extrapolation beyond the holdout, with P50 held at its
300 RPS projection. Pool-capacity comparisons are warnings only and do
not independently imply errors or throughput loss. The
final P99 is floored at final P95; P99 is not scored in Accuracy.
No generic 5 ms floor applies to scaled lean latency; 0.05 ms is
only a physical/non-finite safety floor. Reference estimates use 0.50–2.
Beyond 1000 offered RPS, scaled uses 0.25–2 and reference 0.25–3.
Unknown-vCPU legacy fallback uses the widest reference range and has no
external reference. `legacyGeneric` explicitly labels use of that
unverified generic branch: true at the top level if any reported app CPU
or latency quantity used it, and true on each affected appCpuByResource
item. The evidence note names each affected resource's shape and reason (missing vCPU,
flexible shape without resource.characteristics.ocpus, or unknown/
unrecognized shape). CPU ranges are physically capped at 100%.
Prediction-only capacity metadata covers GCP E2 standard
e2-standard-2/4/8/16/32, N1 standard
n1-standard-1/2/4/8/16/32/64/96, and N2 standard
n2-standard-2/4/8/16/32/48/64/80/96/128. Google-published vCPU and
memory specifications establish hardware dimensions only, not CWM
performance, throughput, or price.
Historical rows missing evidence are returned non-mutating as
unavailable/legacy with null weight/load/quantities and empty IDs; they
are never relabeled measured by today's model.

legacyGeneric.description: True when any reported app CPU or latency quantity used the unverified generic fallback; false for newly produced non-generic evidence; null on explicitly unavailable/legacy historical evidence. Predating saved evidence can omit this field entirely; it is never reconstructed.
True when this resource's app CPU used the unverified generic fallback. Required for newly produced evidence; absent on predating saved evidence.

requestServingCapacity.description: Per-Fargate-service configured task count, per-task modeled rate, aggregate capacity, and explicit evidence basis. Assumptions are not measured throughput.

latencyPercentileStatus.description: Whether percentile evidence is available from a modeled serving-tier distribution.

latencyP99.description: Optional per-percentile P99 evidence, with evidenceLevel and assumption bounds (not confidence intervals). May be null or absent on legacy rows.

GenericShapeInventory.description:
Resolver-derived, read-only inventory of remaining generic prediction
cases. It includes named catalog gaps and conditional categories with
reasons; unknown/custom compute is a wildcard rather than an exhaustive
list of arbitrary SKU strings. Inventory metadata describes capacity
resolution only, not performance benchmarks or prices.

namedCatalogGaps.description: Named catalog-backed shape gaps, with their reasons.

conditionalCategories.description: Conditional fallback classes, including their resolution condition and reason.

kind.description: Whether the applicable workload calibration is owned, explicitly scaled from an owned fit (not measured at that topology), or remains modeled output. The owned CRUD fit uses calibrationId aws-crud/v1:473f1339-f712-4096-96d6-3d4fc07cb427:7416cb63ace3a7ab2e3486bb6f132a2dcb574c34.

latencyBasis.description: General modeled latency path/boundary; use latencyP99Basis for percentile-specific P99 provenance.

latencyP99Basis.description: P99-specific basis: owned in-VPC internal-ALB fit, scaled from that fit (not directly measured), or uncalibrated generic model. Optional on older persisted calibration evidence.

calibrationId.description: Versioned identifier of the owned calibration, present only when it applies.

note.description: Human-readable calibration scope and limitations. For eligible canonical CRUD graphs, identify omitted workload inference as a modeling assumption when used. For modeled fallbacks, name all actual failed eligibility checks in stable order with resource IDs and safe expected/actual values; do not return only a generic "not applied" message. The owned-scaled typical fit identifies its two-server source, equivalent-load derivation, unmeasured server count, pool-to-database ceiling warnings, and any extrapolation.

RequestFlowMetrics.description: Per-step flow for explicitly configured cacheable and asynchronous request shares. Rates are requests or messages per second; queueDepth and capacityMessages are messages. These are model assumptions, not production measurements, and do not model partition lag or generic error absorption.

cache.description: Present only when a cacheable request share is explicitly configured.

cacheableShare.description: Declared fraction of offered requests sent to the cache.

hitRatePct.description: Actual modeled hit rate as a percentage

missRps.description: Cache misses forwarded to synchronous downstream work.

bypassRps.description: Offered requests that bypass the cache and queue and reach synchronous work.

synchronousDatabaseRps.description: Cache misses plus bypass requests routed to relational databases.

queues.description: Per-queue enqueue, consumer drain, and retained backlog for the step.

drainRps.description: Messages consumed and routed to database work during this step.

queueDepth.description: Backlog in messages after this step.

queueFillPct.description: Queue depth divided by its explicit message capacity.

databases.description: Per-database offered work after cache misses, bypass, and queue drain are applied.

NormalizedConfig.description:
Read-only introspection of what CWM actually modelled from the creation
payload. Returned on `POST /api/simulations` (201) and
`GET /api/simulations/{simulationId}` so a consumer can verify the
resolved billing and capacity values per resource — e.g. why two
payloads that look identical produce different costs (different
resolved `size`, GPU SKU, or cost multiplier). Every value is derived
with the same resolution functions the billing/autoscale engine uses.

requestFlow.description: Graph-level assumptions for the explicitly configured cache and queue flow. Values remain assumptions; this summary does not claim measured production behavior, partition lag, or error absorption.

NormalizationReceipt.description:
Immutable, versioned receipt stored at creation and returned unchanged by
create, get, and step responses. It records each material assumption's
source: human/API input, MCP/agent input, platform default, catalog
resolution, engine inference, or unsupported fallback. It makes
normalized Kubernetes inputs comparable without requiring equivalent
natural-language prompts.

modelingScope.description: Explicit generic-Kubernetes limitations. CWM models worker-node capacity, CPU/utilization, autoscaling, and recovery only. The control-plane management fee is cost-only; CWM does not simulate or report control-plane CPU, master/API throttling, or control-plane cooldown. memoryUsage is synthetic aggregate utilization and cannot establish per-pod GiB, working-set demand, OOM timing, cgroup limits, eviction, or OOMKill behavior.

capacity.description: Resolved Kubernetes worker serving capacity. For a multi-pool cluster, sum `pools[].capacityRps` to reconstruct `clusterMaxThroughputRps`; each `pools[].capacityShare` is the pool's share of that cluster ceiling and sums to approximately 1.0.

perNodeRps.description: Uniform-equivalent per-node capacity in requests per second. For pool-aware capacity, use the pool-level `perNodeRps` values instead.

clusterMaxThroughputRps.description: Immutable pre-effect Kubernetes cluster serving ceiling in requests per second. This is the reconstruction target for the sum of `pools[].capacityRps`.

representation.description: Whether the capacity is broken down using heterogeneous node-pool weights or represented as a uniform per-node equivalent.

source.description: How the cluster ceiling was resolved.

pools.description: Per-pool capacity contributions. Present only for multi-pool Kubernetes resources. `capacityWeight` is the pool's node-count-weighted capacity, `capacityShare` is `capacityWeight` divided by the sum of all pool weights, and `capacityRps` is `clusterMaxThroughputRps × capacityShare`.

poolId.description: Stable unique identifier for this node pool.

nodeCount.description: Resolved current worker-node count for this pool.

capacityWeight.description: Capacity weight used to calculate this pool's share. It is `nodeCount × per-node maxThroughput` when declared, otherwise the node count for the uniform fallback.

capacityShare.description: Fraction of the cluster ceiling assigned to this pool.

capacityRps.description: This pool's serving-capacity contribution in requests per second; sum this field across pools to reconstruct the cluster ceiling.

perNodeRps.description: This pool's capacity contribution divided by its node count.

NormalizedResourceConfig.description: Resolved billing and capacity values for one resource.

requestFlowAssumptions.description: Per-resource opt-in cache or queue configuration. Drain rates, request shares, hit rate, and queue capacity are declared model assumptions rather than production observations.

resolvedSku.description: Effective resource SKU after applying the size/instanceType compatibility alias. When both are supplied they must match; an unknown explicit SKU remains visible and is reported through the normal estimated/unsupported coverage path.

openshiftOffering.description: Resolved OpenShift distribution overlay, when present.

openshiftPlatformFeePerHour.description: Additive OpenShift platform or license fee in USD/hr. For per-4-vCPU offerings this is prorated across the resolved worker vCPU capacity.

openshiftPricingStatus.description: Provenance of the resolved OpenShift platform/license amount. ARO is official only for a resource explicitly located in Azure East US; other or missing regions are estimated reference use of the East US published line.

openshiftControlPlanePricingStatus.description: Provenance of the backing-provider or OpenShift-specific control-plane charge. For ARO this is estimated because the control-plane charge is modeled from Azure Kubernetes pricing and is included in the aggregate rather than represented as an excluded aro/managed resource.

resolvedCostMultiplier.description: Effective cost multiplier the engine applies (explicit characteristics.costMultiplier, size-tier backfill, or pricing benchmark backfill — whichever the billing path resolves).

resolvedHourlyRate.description: Resolved generic instance hourly rate (base rate × multiplier), USD/hr. Applies to compute and fixed-rate relational database resources; request-priced DynamoDB is described by dynamoDbBilling instead.

rateProvenance.description: Provenance of the resolved rate — present whenever `resolvedHourlyRate` or `resolvedGpuRatePerNode` is emitted. Tells consumers what pricing basis the constant reflects, which lookup path resolved it, and when it was last cross-checked against the provider's published pricing page (static metadata from the pricing constants, not fetched live). AWS M7, M8, and M9 entries such as `m7g.large`, `m8g.large`, and `m9g.large` use `basis: on-demand` and `resolution: exact-catalog` when their resolved hourly value matches the canonical AWS EC2 Price List catalog. This certifies price provenance only; EC2 performance characteristics remain CWM-modeled unless separately marked by a performance source.

basis.description: Pricing basis — `on-demand` for published list-price constants, `estimated` for fallback/approximation constants.

resolution.description: Lookup path taken — exact first-party catalog SKU (for example AWS M7, M8, or M9), exact premium GPU SKU, provider entry-level GPU fallback, or the general base-rate × multiplier path.

lastVerified.description: ISO-8601 date the constant was last verified against the provider's public pricing page; null when unknown.

region.description: Region the verified rate applies to, from the constant's pricing source (e.g. `us-east-1`, `us-central1`, `eastus`, `us-ashburn-1`); null only for genuinely region-uniform pricing (e.g. DigitalOcean).

sku.description: Exact provider catalog SKU when resolution is exact-catalog (for example `m7g.large`); absent for generic and GPU fallback paths.

architecture.description: Fargate Linux task architecture (X86_64 or ARM64).

source.description: Official pricing source URL for verified billing-unit rates, or price-list source for an exact catalog rate; absent for generic and fallback paths.
source.example: AWS EC2 Price List API (Linux, shared tenancy, on-demand)

resolvedMaxThroughputRps.description: Effective aggregate throughput (RPS) for this resource. For fixed compute fleets, per-VM resolved throughput is multiplied by effectiveVmInstanceCount; independently materialized autoscaling members each count as one VM. When compute capacity is not declared, the resolved CPU/capacity model default is reported rather than an enforced serving ceiling. For Kubernetes, this is the enforced cluster serving ceiling; 0 means no serving ceiling is configured (the autoscaler's separate 10,000-RPS heuristic is not a ceiling).

effectiveVmInstanceCount.description: Effective physical VM count represented by this compute resource during simulation. A fixed logical fleet can represent multiple VMs; materialized autoscaling members each represent one. Absent for non-compute resources.

effectiveCpuCapacityRps.description: Aggregate CPU-model capacity denominator (RPS) for this compute resource, calculated as the resolved per-VM CPU denominator times effectiveVmInstanceCount. This model denominator can differ from the declared serving capacity and is not itself a throughput ceiling.

minNodes.description: Effective autoscale floor (explicit minNodes or the provider autoscaling profile default the engine applies). Single-pool kubernetes.

maxNodes.description: Effective autoscale ceiling (explicit maxNodes or the provider profile default, floored to the current node count). Single-pool kubernetes.

perNodeRatePerHour.description: Per-worker-node hourly rate the cluster bills at, USD/hr (single-pool kubernetes).

controlPlaneFeePerHour.description: Cost-only cluster control-plane management fee, USD/hr. It is not control-plane CPU, API-throttling, or cooldown telemetry.

spotFactor.description: Spot-pricing discount factor applied to node billing (present only when pricingModel is spot).

currentNodesCostPerHour.description: Hourly cost at the CURRENT node count — controlPlaneFee + Σ(rate × nodes), spot factor applied, USD/hr.

nodePools.description: Per-pool resolved billing/bounds for multi-pool clusters. When present, nodeCount/billingFloor values aggregate across pools and the pool entries carry the authoritative per-pool rates.

minNodes.description: Effective per-pool scale-in floor (explicit or profile default).

maxNodes.description: Effective per-pool scale-out ceiling (explicit or profile default).

perNodeRatePerHour.description: The rate this pool bills each node at (explicit perNodeRate or the cluster default), USD/hr.

perNodeMaxThroughputRps.description: Per-node serving capacity for this pool, when explicitly configured.

autoscaleThreshold.description: Effective CPU autoscale thresholds (provider profile merged with any simulation-level override; GPU inference clusters include the provider GPU overlay).

resolvedGpuRatePerNode.description: Resolved GPU node hourly rate (inference-mode kubernetes clusters), USD/hr.

resolvedSkuLabel.description: The exact GPU SKU (`size`) that matched the premium GPU catalogue, or a fallback indicator naming the provider-level default GPU rate used instead.

perNodeTokensPerSec.description: Per-node token serving capacity (tokens/s) resolved from the accelerator type.

billingFloorNodes.description: Smallest node count autoscaling can ever shrink the cluster to — min(nodeCount, effective minNodes), summed across pools for multi-pool clusters.

billingFloorCostPerHour.description: Minimum billable hourly cost — controlPlaneFee + rate × billingFloorNodes (per-pool rates for multi-pool clusters), spot factor applied, USD/hr.

resolvedConnectionLimit.description: Effective connection limit — the exact value the engine's connection-pressure model uses (serverless ACU-based limit, else maxConnections, connections, or the engine default of 100).

acuBilling.description: Aurora Standard Serverless v2 billing units. Hourly compute is currentAcu multiplied by ratePerAcuHour per billable DB instance; not a flat instance-hour rate.

dynamoDbBilling.description: DynamoDB's modeled cost is request-volume based, not a fixed instance-hour price. For each DynamoDB resource, the CWM modeled hourly cost is referenceModeledCostPerHour multiplied by that resource's allocated request rate divided by referenceRequestRateRps. Simulation traffic is split evenly across DynamoDB resources. The reference cost is derived from CWM's generic database base-rate anchor and effective cost multiplier; it is not AWS-published DynamoDB pricing or a provider quote.

billingModel.description: DynamoDB's modeled hourly cost scales linearly with allocated request rate.

referenceRequestRateRps.description: Per-resource request-rate reference at which the CWM modeled hourly cost anchor applies.

referenceModeledCostPerHour.description: CWM-modeled USD/hour anchor at referenceRequestRateRps; not an AWS DynamoDB price.

referenceCostBasis.description: Identifies the reference cost as an internal CWM model estimate rather than provider-published pricing.

providerPublishedPrice.description: Always false; the CWM reference anchor is not a provider-published price or quote.

requestServing.description:
Provider request-serving configuration (Cloud Run, functions, Azure Container Apps, or ECS/Fargate) derived from the same characteristics used by
 capacity and billing. Usage-based cost excludes provider free tiers,
 networking, logging, and discounts unless noted by the service policy.

perTaskCapacityEvidence.description: Resolved trust label. CWM size heuristics and unverified caller values are assumptions, never measured throughput or provider catalog facts.

aggregateCapacityRps.description: Desired task count multiplied by this service's resolved per-task rate.

maxAggregateCapacityRps.description: Maximum task count multiplied by this service's resolved per-task rate.

taskVcpuHourRate.description: ECS/Fargate Linux on-demand us-east-1 vCPU-hour rate.

taskMemoryGibHourRate.description: ECS/Fargate Linux on-demand us-east-1 GB-hour rate.

minimumBillableSeconds.description: ECS/Fargate minimum billable task start duration.

behaviorModel.description: Machine-readable identification of the latency simulation path applied to this resource at step time. Present on all resource types. Use `latencyPath` to programmatically determine which model will run — e.g. to verify a GPU inference cluster is using `gpu-inference/ttft-decode` rather than the generic K8s path.

latencyPath.description: Canonical latency-path identifier. One of: `gpu-inference/ttft-decode` (K8s cluster with inferenceMode: true — token-economics TTFT+decode model), `generic-kubernetes/load-saturation` (K8s cluster without inferenceMode — generic saturation model), `generic-compute/load-saturation` (compute/VM resources), `database/connection-saturation` (database resources — connection-pool pressure model), `database/request-capacity` (DynamoDB — request/capacity model), `storage/iops-saturation` (OCI Block Volume only — IOPS ceiling tracked; penalties propagated to co-located DBs), `generic/flat-rate` (all other storage, network, cache, queue, security — cost-only, no latency simulation).

description.description: Human-readable description of the latency model.
description.example: Token-economics model: TTFT + decode, weighted by throughput and batch pressure.

modelingNote.description: Optional provenance note. Present on GPU inference resources (`latencyPath: gpu-inference/ttft-decode`) to remind API consumers that TTFT and decode-throughput figures are produced by the CWM simulation model, not by externally measured hardware benchmarks. When topology is omitted, includes an explicit legacy-baseline note stating that factor 1.0 reflects the pre-topology assumption, not a measurement of a specific interconnect fabric. Absent on non-inference resources.
modelingNote.example: TTFT and decode-throughput figures are CWM simulation-model estimates, not externally measured hardware benchmarks.

topologyThroughputFactor.description: The exact throughput scaling coefficient that `resolveTopologyScalingFactor` applied to this resource's token capacity (`nodes × perNodeTokens × topoFactor × gpuUtil/100`). 1.0 when `topology.intraNode` is absent or unrecognised (legacy baseline). Present only on inferenceMode Kubernetes resources. Entirely separate from `topologyTtftFactor` and `topologyDecodeFactor`, which describe the TTFT+decode latency model.

topologyThroughputCalibrationStatus.description: Calibration status of the throughput scaling factor (`resolveTopologyScalingFactor`) that bounds effective token capacity — entirely separate from the TTFT and decode latency factors (`resolveTopologyLatencyFactors`) described by `topologyCalibrationStatus`. "estimated" for all current inference-mode intraNode coefficients (0.70 pcie / 0.85 nvlink / 0.92 nvlink-nvswitch), which are engineering assumptions based on bandwidth arithmetic with no directly measured controlled per-request token-throughput ratio attributable to intraNode fabric type alone. "not_applicable" on non-inferenceMode resources. Reserve "calibrated" for when a directly measured source is added.

topologyIsLegacyBaseline.description: `true` when `topology.intraNode` was absent or unrecognised, meaning `topologyThroughputFactor: 1.0` reflects the pre-topology legacy baseline — not a measurement of a specific interconnect fabric. `false` when an explicit, known `intraNode` value was supplied and the throughput factor is topology-modeled. Present only on inferenceMode Kubernetes resources. Agents should check this field before interpreting a factor of 1.0 as a best-fabric result.

ibNetworkingCostPerNodePerHour.description: Per-node InfiniBand networking cost premium (USD/hr) added on top of the base GPU node rate when `topologyInterNode === "infiniband"` and `topologyNodeCount > 1`. Sourced from `IB_NETWORKING_COST_PER_NODE_PER_HOUR` in `shared/provider-pricing.ts` (calibration status: estimated — derived from the Azure NC24rs_v3 vs NC24s_v3 IB delta lower bound and NVIDIA DGX Cloud networking pricing upper bound; will be updated to on-demand status when a provider publishes a discrete IB fabric line-item at this granularity). Total cluster IB cost = `ibNetworkingCostPerNodePerHour × nodeCount`, surfaced as a separate `"infiniband_networking"` entry in the simulation-level `costBreakdown`. Absent when IB networking is not active (no `interNode` topology, single-node cluster, or non-IB fabric type).

inferenceWarnings.description: Non-fatal configuration warnings. Populated when a Kubernetes resource carries inference/GPU characteristics (`accelerator`, `tokensPerRequest`, `inputTokensPerRequest`) but `inferenceMode` is absent or false — meaning the `generic-kubernetes/load-saturation` model will be used instead of the GPU inference model. Empty or absent when no warnings apply. To silence these warnings and activate the GPU inference path, set `characteristics.inferenceMode: true` on the resource.
example: Resource has inference/GPU characteristics (accelerator: h100, tokensPerRequest: 512) but inferenceMode is not enabled. The generic-kubernetes/load-saturation latency model will be used. Set characteristics.inferenceMode: true to activate gpu-inference/ttft-decode.

auroraTopologyWarnings.description: Non-fatal warning on a legacy AWS Aurora database with multiAz:true but no instanceCount and no explicit standby. No reader is inferred from that flag alone; specify instanceCount:2 on Aurora Serverless v2 to create a separately billed reader in another AZ.

targetSLA.description: Service-level objectives used to calculate the episode reward.

tick_seconds.description:
Number of simulated seconds each step advances the simulation clock.
Default is 60 (one simulated minute per step). Set higher values to
model longer time horizons (e.g. 300 for 5-minute ticks, 3600 for
hourly ticks). The value is fixed for the lifetime of the episode.

unmodeled_cost_penalty_per_dimension.description: Reward penalty applied per active unmodeled cost dimension per step. The total penalty is -(count × this value) and is reported in `reward_components.unmodeled_cost` and `unmodeled_cost_penalty` in the step response. Default is 0.1.

evalCostOverrides.description: Per-dimension cost override rates in USD per 1 000 RPS per hour. Supported keys: `egress` (outbound data-transfer fee charged whenever traffic > 0) and `cross_az_traffic` (inter-AZ data-transfer fee charged when resources in different Availability Zones are connected). When present, these rates are added to the simulated cost before computing the reward cost score, making previously unpriced dimensions visible in the reward signal. Primarily used by the `eval-episodes` endpoint to stress-test trained policies against real-world cost blind spots.

RLTradeoffSummary.description:
Per-metric deltas between the episode-start config and the episode-end config.
Returned only on the final step response (`done: true`). Use this to evaluate
whether the agent's actions improved cost, latency, and resilience over the course
of the episode.

costDeltaPercent.description: Cost change as a percentage of the episode-start cost. Negative = cheaper.

costDirection.description: improved = lower cost, degraded = higher cost. Unchanged when |delta| < 0.5%.

latencyP95DeltaMs.description: P95 latency change in milliseconds relative to episode start. Negative = faster.

latencyP95Direction.description: improved = lower latency, degraded = higher latency. Unchanged when |delta| < 1 ms.

resilienceDeltaScore.description: Change in resilience score (uptime = 1 − error_rate) between episode start and end. Range −1 to 1. Positive = more resilient (fewer errors).

resilienceDirection.description: improved = higher uptime, degraded = lower uptime. Unchanged when |delta| < 0.001.

jobId.description: Unique identifier for the eval job. Use this to poll the GET endpoint.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the job was created

episodes.description: Per-episode results in the same order as the request `actions` array

episodeIndex.description: Zero-based index of this episode in the request array

stepsExecuted.description: Number of actions executed (may be less than the action array length if the episode ended early)

totalReward.description: Cumulative reward across all steps in this eval episode

steps.description: Per-step error evidence from the replay; database pressure details omit zero-contribution databases.

step.description: One-based step number within this evaluation episode

meanEvalReward.description: Mean of `totalReward` across all eval episodes

trainingTotalReward.description: Stored cumulative training reward from the environment (the baseline being compared against)

collapseThreshold.description: The collapse threshold used for this evaluation (echoed from request)

reward_collapse.description: `true` when `meanEvalReward` falls more than `collapseThreshold × |trainingTotalReward|` below `trainingTotalReward`. Indicates the policy exploits cost dimensions unpriced during training.

error.description: Error message describing why the job failed
error.example: Environment or simulation no longer exists

lastSimTimeHuman.description: Human-readable simulated elapsed time as of the last step or reset (e.g. "1h 30m"). Absent before the first step.

webhookDeliveryAttempts.description: Number of webhook delivery attempts made

webhookDeliveryError.description: Error message if webhook delivery failed

webhookDeliveredAt.description: Timestamp when webhook was successfully delivered

idleExpiresAt.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp at which this environment will be automatically expired
due to inactivity. Computed as `lastActivityAt` (or `createdAt` if no step
or reset has been called yet) plus the 2-hour idle TTL. Agents can use
this value to schedule keep-alive calls (`POST /rl/environments/{environmentId}/step`
or `POST /rl/environments/{environmentId}/reset`) before expiry.

RewardWeights.description:
User-defined weights controlling how cost, resilience, latency, performance,
and stability each contribute to the scalar reward returned on each RL step.

Valid create-time keys: `cost`, `resilience`, `latency`, `performance`, `stability`.
These are the weights you set when creating or resetting an environment — they
are distinct from the step-response `reward_components` fields
(`connection_pressure`, `unmodeled_cost`, `sla`) which are computed automatically.

All values must be non-negative. They are automatically normalized to sum to 1.0
on the server side, so you may supply raw priority scores
(e.g. `{ cost: 3, resilience: 1, latency: 1 }`) or pre-normalized fractions
(e.g. `{ cost: 0.6, resilience: 0.2, latency: 0.2 }`).

When omitted (the default), the agent uses the built-in weighting of
latency: 0.35 / cost: 0.25 / resilience: 0.40 — optimized for
balanced cloud workloads.

cost.description: Weight assigned to cost optimization (staying within cost budget).

resilience.description: Weight assigned to resilience (low error rates, stable resources, no SLA violations).

latency.description: Weight assigned to latency performance (p95 latency relative to SLA target).

performance.description: Weight assigned to throughput and capacity performance.

stability.description: Weight assigned to autoscaling stability (penalizes thrashing and rapid oscillation).

Action.description: Action selected by the RL agent for one simulation step.

parameters.description: Type-specific values for the selected action; pass an empty object when the action has no parameters.

ScaleParams.description: Parameters for scaling the compute fleet in or out.

instanceCount.description: Number of instances to add (`scale_out`) or remove (`scale_in`) — a delta, not a target count. The effective change is clamped to the per-resource instance bounds: the ceiling is `min(autoscalingConfig.maxInstances, characteristics.maxInstances)` for `scale_out`, and the floor is `max(autoscalingConfig.minInstances, characteristics.minInstances)` for `scale_in`. When clamping occurs the step response `info` object contains the flat keys `scale_clamped: true`, `requested` (this parameter's value), `actual` (delta applied, 0 if blocked), and `limit` (effective bound).

ResourceParams.description: Resource details for adding a resource, or its identifier when removing one.

resourceId.description: For remove_resource action, ID of resource to remove

resourceType.description: For add_resource action, type of resource to add

provider.description: For add_resource action, cloud provider for the new resource

targetSize.description: For add_resource action, size label for the new resource (e.g. "t3.micro" for aws)

regionKey.description: For add_resource action, region key to assign to the new resource (e.g. "us-east-1" for aws). Must be a valid region for the specified provider. Returns UNKNOWN_REGION if invalid.

SetRecoveryPolicyParams.description:
Parameters for set_recovery_policy action. Supports two call forms:

**Per-resource form** — provide `resourceId` and the nested `recoveryPolicy`
object to override healing thresholds on one specific resource.

**Global flat form** — omit `resourceId` and pass the four threshold fields
(`criticalCpuThreshold`, `criticalSteps`, `warningCpuThreshold`, `warningSteps`)
directly at the top level to apply the same policy to every resource in the
simulation at once. The nested `recoveryPolicy` object takes precedence over the
flat fields if both are supplied.

resourceId.description: ID of the resource to update. Omit to apply the policy globally to all resources (global flat form).

recoveryPolicy.description: Recovery policy thresholds to apply (per-resource form). Takes precedence over flat threshold fields when both are provided.

criticalCpuThreshold.description: CPU % above which a resource is considered critical

criticalSteps.description: Steps the resource must stay at critical CPU before recovery triggers

warningCpuThreshold.description: CPU % above which a resource is considered in warning state

warningSteps.description: Steps the resource must stay at warning CPU before recovery triggers

criticalCpuThreshold.description: CPU % above which a resource is considered critical (global flat form — applies to all resources when resourceId is omitted)

criticalSteps.description: Steps a resource must stay at critical CPU before recovery triggers (global flat form)

warningCpuThreshold.description: CPU % above which a resource is considered in warning state (global flat form)

warningSteps.description: Steps a resource must stay at warning CPU before recovery triggers (global flat form)

latencyPercentileStatus.description: Whether P50/P95/P99 are supported by a modeled serving-tier latency distribution.

connectionPressure.description: Database connection-pool pressure — the ratio of estimated active connections to total pool capacity (capped at 3.0). Only present when the simulation contains a database resource; absent otherwise.

currentTime.description: Current simulation time (total elapsed simulated seconds)

sim_time_seconds.description:
Total elapsed simulated seconds since the episode started.
Equals `currentTime` (which is now expressed in seconds).
Included so agents can compute real-world time durations without
re-reading the environment config.

tick_seconds.description:
Number of simulated seconds this step advanced the clock.
Reflects the per-step `tick_seconds` override if one was supplied in
the step request body; otherwise matches the `tick_seconds` value set
in `episodeConfig` at environment creation time.

total.description: Total reward for this step (weighted sum of components)

performance.description: Performance score (0-1, based on latency and errors)

cost.description: Cost efficiency score (0-1, based on budget)

stability.description: Stability score (-1 to 1, penalizes excessive changes)

sla.description: SLA compliance score (-1 to 0, penalizes violations)

metrics.description: Raw metrics used for reward calculation

RLObs.description: Agent-facing decision state returned by the step and observation endpoints. Contains only the signals an RL agent needs to choose its next action. Fractions (cpu_util, error_rate, uptime) are in the range [0, 1].

instances.description: Total number of active compute instances

tick_seconds.description:
Number of simulated seconds this step advanced the clock.
Reflects the per-step `tick_seconds` override supplied in the step
request body, or the episode-level `episodeConfig.tick_seconds` when
no per-step override was given.

unmodeled_dimensions_active.description: True when at least one cost dimension is active but not modeled in the reward function (e.g. egress or cross-AZ traffic). See `unmodeled_cost_warning` at the step-response top level for the list of active dimensions. Absent (falsy) when all dimensions are modeled or no unmodeled dimensions are detected.

warmup_factor.description:
Minimum warmup capacity factor across all compute/Kubernetes resources that carry a warm-up counter, in (0, 1]. Value is 1.0 when all instances are fully warmed; less than 1.0 while any instance is still in its warm-up window.

**Mid-episode transition:** This field is absent at episode start when no compute resource carries a warm-up counter. It appears dynamically once a cold compute instance is provisioned — either via an `add_resource` action or via canvas autoscaling triggered by high CPU or traffic. After the warm-up window completes (typically 3 steps), the field returns to 1.0 and may become absent again if no further cold instances exist.

**Safe access pattern:** Agents building a fixed-width observation vector must guard against its absence by defaulting to 1.0 when the field is not present. In Python: `wf = obs.get("warmup_factor", 1.0)`. In JavaScript/TypeScript: `const wf = obs.warmup_factor ?? 1.0`. Never assume the field is present across all steps of an episode.

Use this as a direct observation feature in your reward function — low values indicate recently-provisioned instances are not yet at full throughput. For per-resource detail see metrics.compute[].warmup_factor.

routedRps_per_node.description:
Average requests per second routed to each active compute node this step. Computed as the instance-count-weighted mean of per-node `routedRps` across all compute resources: `sum(perNodeRps × instances) / totalInstances`.

Unlike `rps` (the simulation-wide throughput total), this field expresses per-node load directly so agents can make scaling decisions without dividing by instance count themselves. When nodes fail their share of traffic is redistributed to surviving nodes — `routedRps_per_node` captures this redistribution effect accurately, eliminating the approximation error that arises when computing `rps / instances` after a partial failure.

**Availability:** Present on step responses whenever at least one compute resource exists and the simulation engine has produced a routedRps map for the step. Absent on reset observations (which are pre-step snapshots) and on simulations that contain no compute resources.

**Safe access pattern:** Default to `obs.get("rps", 0) / max(obs.get("instances", 1), 1)` when the field is absent for backward compatibility.

unavailable_node_count.description:
Number of compute, Kubernetes, and database resources whose `availabilityState` is `"unavailable"` at this step. A value of zero means every tracked resource is serving traffic normally.

Use this as a compact policy signal — when greater than zero, at least one node has failed (parked-critical, AZ-outage, or instance_kill) and surviving nodes are absorbing its redirected traffic share. Pair with `observation.resources[].availabilityState` for per-node detail when you need to identify which specific resources are unavailable.

**Zero on reset observations** (all resources default to `"available"` before the first step, so this value is always 0 on fresh episode start).

**Safe access pattern:** `unavailable = obs.get("unavailable_node_count", 0)` — treat absence as zero.

RLMetrics.description: Evaluation-oriented metrics returned alongside obs by the step and observation endpoints. These are the outputs your reward function and monitoring dashboards should read. Fractions (error_rate, uptime) are in the range [0, 1]. The `connection_pressure` field is optional — it is only present when the simulation contains at least one database resource (e.g. RDS, Cloud SQL, Azure SQL, Autonomous DB, Managed PostgreSQL). Agents should guard against its absence when no database resource is configured.

sla_violations.description: Number of SLA dimension violations at this step (0 = fully compliant)

connection_pressure.description: DB connection-pool pressure ratio (activeConnections / maxConnections), capped at 3.0. Only present when the simulation contains database resources. Values > 1.0 indicate pool exhaustion; values > 1.5 indicate severe saturation. Use this field to build reward functions that penalise connection-pool exhaustion independently of the aggregate error_rate signal.

compute.description:
Per-resource warm-up state for compute and Kubernetes resources that carry a warm-up counter. Only present when at least one such resource exists in the simulation. Absent when no resources have a warm-up counter.

**Mid-episode transition:** Like `obs.warmup_factor`, this array is absent at episode start when no compute resource carries a warm-up counter. It appears dynamically once a cold compute instance is provisioned mid-episode (via `add_resource` or canvas autoscaling) and disappears again once all warm-up windows complete. Guard against its absence with `metrics.compute ?? []` or `metrics.get("compute", [])`.

Agents should read `obs.warmup_factor` as the primary scalar observation feature — do not re-derive it from step counters or this array.

resource_id.description: Resource id of this compute or Kubernetes resource

warmup_factor.description: Normalized capacity factor in (0, 1]. Value is 1.0 when fully warmed; less than 1.0 while warming (steepest at step 0). Use this directly as an RL observation feature instead of inferring it from step counters.

warming.description: True while the resource is still in its warm-up window

warmup_steps_remaining.description: Steps remaining until the resource is fully warmed (0 when warmed)

error_breakdown.description: Per-contributor breakdown of the error rate. Each field is the pre-clamp additive contribution in percentage-point units (same scale as `error_rate × 100`). `queue_absorption` is the amount removed by queue buffering (positive value = reduction). `dependency_failure` is the client-level contribution from failed downstream dependency paths. Only present when the simulation engine produces an errorBreakdown for the step. Absent on early steps or simulations without failure sources. Use these fields to build reward functions that penalise specific failure modes — for example, penalise `pool_saturation > 0` for modeled connection demand beyond a usable database limit, or reward reducing `capacity_overload` after a scale-out. `database_pressure` reports the generic contribution once a database's connection or CPU utilization exceeds its effective threshold (80% by default); benchmark-compatibility runs retain their provider reference fit. It shares a combined 5 percentage-point database-error cap with `pool_saturation`. The accompanying details name the database and whether connection use, CPU, or both drove the pressure. Pool-saturation details identify databases whose modeled demand exceeds their own usable connection limits. `cpu_overload` is serving-CPU telemetry, not a compute-failure signal. Only active, request-serving compute and Kubernetes resources that are actually serving traffic contribute; parked or unavailable nodes are excluded from the numerator and denominator. Database and network resource CPU is separate and never contributes to `cpu_overload`. For each eligible serving resource, the engine computes `max(0, (cpuUsagePercent - 80) / 20)`, averages those per-resource excesses, and multiplies by the provider slope. Ordinary/custom AWS uses a 10 percentage-point slope: one eligible AWS node at 100% CPU contributes 10 points, while eligible nodes at 100% and 70% contribute 5 points. Adding a parked 100% node, a database at 100%, or a network resource at 100% leaves that value unchanged. Other providers currently use slope 0. The owned AWS CRUD benchmark may intentionally report zero here as an internal calibration policy; that is not a generic API rule and should not be applied to ordinary AWS responses.

database_pressure.description: Generic database pressure contribution after per-database connection utilization or CPU utilization exceeds its effective threshold (80% by default); benchmark-compatibility runs retain their provider reference fit.

database_pressure_details.description: Per-database attribution for the under-limit pressure contribution.

pool_saturation.description: Error contribution from connection-pool exhaustion (percentage points)

pool_saturation_details.description: Databases whose modeled connection demand exceeds their own usable pool limits.

enum: modeled connection demand; not observed live sessions

db_failure.description: Error contribution from failed or overloaded database resources (percentage points)

compute_failure.description: Error contribution from failed compute nodes (percentage points)

capacity_overload.description: Error contribution from traffic exceeding compute capacity (percentage points)

cpu_overload.description: Serving CPU overload contribution in percentage points. Uses the mean per-resource CPU excess above 80% among active serving compute/Kubernetes resources, excluding parked or unavailable nodes and excluding database/network CPU. Ordinary/custom AWS uses a 10-point slope, so 100% on one eligible node contributes 10 points.

oci_storage.description: Error contribution from OCI storage I/O issues (percentage points)

queue_absorption.description: Amount of error rate absorbed (buffered) by queue resources (percentage points, positive = reduction in effective error rate). Subtract this from the sum of the other contributors to get the net error rate before clamping.

dependency_failure.description: Client-level error contribution from unavailable or failing downstream dependency paths (percentage points)

ttft_p50_ms.description: Weighted-average time-to-first-token (TTFT) in milliseconds across all `inferenceMode` GPU Kubernetes clusters in the simulation. Accounts for the accelerator catalog TTFT base, the prompt-token count (`inputTokensPerRequest`), the topology TTFT factor, and batch pressure at the current GPU utilization. Only present when the simulation contains at least one active `inferenceMode` cluster with positive throughput weight. Absent on non-inference simulations. Use this field to reward inference-serving agents that minimize time-to-first-token.

decode_tokens_per_sec.description: Weighted-average effective decode throughput (tokens/second) across all `inferenceMode` GPU Kubernetes clusters. Derived from the accelerator catalog decode rate, the topology decode factor, and batch pressure at the current GPU utilization. Higher values indicate the cluster is decoding tokens faster. Only present when at least one active `inferenceMode` cluster exists with positive throughput weight. Absent on non-inference simulations. Convert to per-request decode latency: `decodeMs = (outputTokensPerRequest / decode_tokens_per_sec) * 1000`.

cooldownSeconds.description: Simulated seconds between ordinary scale-out decisions (ordinary simulation steps advance one simulated second each). Creation warm-up sizing with declared compute capacityRps does not arm this cooldown; a later offered load exceeding the entire declared serving fleet can override an active scale-out cooldown.

ecsCpuTargetTracking.description: When true, the ECS Fargate fleet uses CPU-only target tracking; latency/throughput triggers in this config do not apply to ECS.

description.example: Reduces costs by 38% while maintaining performance

example: Changed web-server-1 from m5.large to t3.medium

costSavingsPercent.description: Cost savings vs baseline. `null` when `coverageState` is `insufficient_cost_coverage` — the baseline aggregate cost excluded at least one unknown-rate resource, so no real savings percentage can be computed.

coverageState.description: Cost-coverage trust signal. `cost_complete` — the baseline cost covered every resource and costSavingsPercent is a real figure. `insufficient_cost_coverage` — at least one resource with an unknown rate (e.g. an inferenceMode Kubernetes cluster with an uncatalogued GPU SKU and no characteristics.perNodeRate) was excluded from the baseline aggregate; costSavingsPercent is null. Behavioral and latency metrics remain valid. Absent on jobs completed before this field existed (treat as cost_complete).

excludedRateResources.description: Names of the resources excluded from the baseline cost aggregate because their rate is unknown. Empty when coverage is complete.

reversibility.description: Rule-based classification of how hard this recommendation is to reverse. Derived deterministically from the changes array (never from real cloud APIs or an LLM — basis is always rule_based). The least-reversible change sets the tier. Absent on jobs completed before this field existed.

ResilienceScore.description: Composite resilience result. For canonical outcome-backed results, `overall` is reproducible from the displayed breakdown components using weights recovery 0.25, availability 0.30, dataIntegrity 0.25, and gracefulDegradation 0.20 (rounded displayed components are used). A critical no-failover/no-redundancy/single-point finding on the crashed resource sets the recovery component to zero, even if a later restart succeeds. The batch applies this rule if any child has the target-specific risk. `scoringReason` explains the policy. Legacy payloads may omit newer breakdown components and metrics. `grade` is derived from the live weighted score when canonical evidence is present, not from static vulnerability labels. It is not a deadline verdict or a statement that an unrecovered run is production-ready; inspect `metrics.outcome` for authoritative evidence and final health state when present.

scoringReason.description: Explanation of a target-specific recovery score adjustment.

breakdown.description: Score components on a 0-100 scale. The composite uses `recovery * 0.25 + availability * 0.30 + dataIntegrity * 0.25 + gracefulDegradation * 0.20`, rounded to the reported overall score. Canonical outcome-backed scores provide all four components. Legacy payloads may retain historical breakdown keys or omit newer components; treat those payloads as compatibility data.

livenessOnly.description: If true, dependencyResourceIds must be empty and downstream outages do not fail this check.

scheduledReadyAtSeconds.description: Estimated minimum cold-start completion; readyAtSeconds is set only when readiness is observed.

readyAtSeconds.description: First simulation-clock sample at which readiness is actually observed.

ResilienceMetrics.description:
Resilience measurements over the same simulation-time request window. `availabilityPercent` is successful service over offered requests (goodput divided by offered load), not the percentage of samples below the 5% recovery-health threshold. When offered-load evidence is absent, the authoritative basis and explicit estimate are in `outcome`; no request totals are invented. `recoveryTimeSeconds` and `meanTimeToRecovery` are null when no sustained recovery was observed; older stored reports may contain 0 as a legacy sentinel, not proof of immediate recovery. Use recovery milestones and `sustainPeriodCompleted` in `outcome` to distinguish
 unrecovered, recovered, and recovered-then-regressed runs. A 15%
 error rate with zero goodput and no offered load is unavailable, not
 85% availability. A healthy history with no detected incident has
 baseline evidence only and no recovery milestone. In a batch, mixing
 request-backed children with a rate-only `estimated_from_error_rate`
 child makes the offered denominator unavailable; independent goodput,
 request-window duration, and duration-weighted error-rate evidence remain
 reported. Graceful degradation is the percentage of offered requests
 successfully served in the same window; without a complete positive
 denominator its score is 0, not evidence of successful service. Batch
 recovery duration is null if any child incident did not recover.

healthCheckLifecycle.description: Per-resource unhealthy, deregistration, replacement/restart, readiness, and ALB fail-open evidence.

databaseCrashAssumptions.description: Effective simulation-clock assumptions for each database_crash target, including defaults, in injection order. Absent on older reports and on runs with no database crash. Both delays are reported even though only the delay selected by recoveryMode applies to a given target. Neither value is a provider SLA. Available on single-job results and on each childJobs[].resilienceScore in batch results.

promotionUnavailableReason.description: Present only when an explicitly related replica exists but is unavailable at injection time (including a simultaneous crash). The writer uses sole_writer_restart; promotionDelaySeconds is reported but does not apply.

latencyP95Ms.description: Maximum sampled per-interval p95 latency in milliseconds; null when no serving interval has latency evidence. Not a pooled request percentile.

chaosIntervals.description: Bounded ten-second [startSeconds,endSeconds) simulation-clock intervals (last interval clipped at job duration). Rates integrate by interval duration into outcome request totals. Null means unavailable, not zero; targetStatus remains critical during the crash. Connected writers are hard dependencies: any required writer without its own serving replacement causes 100% errors and zero goodput, including when another independent writer is healthy or crashes concurrently. Without connection edges each writer is considered required; crashing a non-serving reader does not cause this outage. servingResourceId identifies only the first crash target (or its explicitly related promoted replica) when aggregate service is available, otherwise null; it never identifies an unrelated writer. Database crashes honor startTime on the ten-second sampling clock. No task, ACU, or connection-usage values are inferred. databaseTargets reports each distinct crashed database separately; rates and request totals remain aggregate interval values, never duplicated per target. Absent on older persisted reports.

servingMaxConnections.description: Configured connection limit, not measured live connections.

databaseTargets.description: One entry per distinct database crash target, in injection order. A null targetStatus means the target was removed after explicit replica promotion. Replacement is null while promotion/restart is pending; for sole-writer restart the replacement is the original target. Connection limits are configured capacity, not observed usage. No per-target request counts are implied.

servingReplacementMaxConnections.description: Configured connection limit, not measured live connections.

recoveryTimeSeconds.description: Observed sustained recovery duration in simulation seconds, null when unobserved. Older reports may contain a legacy zero sentinel; consult outcome recovery milestones for authoritative status.

availabilityPercent.description: Successful service percentage over the measured request window, clamped to 0-100. With observed offered load this is successfulRequests / observedOfferedRequests × 100 (equivalently duration-weighted goodput / offered RPS); 15% error with valid offered load is approximately 85%, even when no sample is below the recovery threshold.

dataLossIncidents.description: Count of data-loss or corruption incidents observed during the run.

gracefulDegradationScore.description: Successful requests divided by offered requests over the bounded chaos window (0-100). Zero when no complete positive denominator establishes partial service; scoringReason explains the basis.

meanTimeToRecovery.description: Observed sustained recovery duration in simulation seconds; null if unobserved. Legacy stored zero is not proof of recovery.

errorRateDuringChaos.description: Error rate during chaos in percentage points.

eksSpotMigrations.description: Per-resource EKS Spot migration evidence for concurrent active migrations.

eksSpotMigrationEvents.description: EKS Spot interruption lifecycle events; intentionally separate from sustained recovery evidence.

errorRateDuringFailure.description: Legacy alias for the error rate during failures (percentage points).

outcome.description:
Optional authoritative outcome evidence. The object is omitted for legacy results that predate this contract; when present, all fields below describe one common simulation-time request window. RPS fields are rates and request fields are totals over that window. A positive modeled shedding value means offered work exceeded modeled serving
  capacity; it is not silently counted as an application error and is
  never fabricated from goodput or error rate. For batch results,
  request-backed evidence mixed with a rate-only
  `estimated_from_error_rate` child yields
  `availabilityBasis: "unavailable"` rather than combining an
  observed subset into a denominator; goodput, duration, and error-rate
  evidence remain independent.

availabilityBasis.description: Evidence basis for availability and offered-load values. `mixed_observed_and_estimated` combines observed offered load with goodput-and-error-rate modeled demand only. A batch that mixes request-backed evidence with a rate-only `estimated_from_error_rate` child is `unavailable`, because no relative request weight exists for that child.

requestWindowSeconds.description: Exact duration of the normalized simulation-time request window, including the final sample duration. The analyzer's optional windowEndSeconds input clips the final interval to an exact exclusive boundary; this public field reports the resulting duration.

observedOfferedRequests.description: Observed original-client offered request total over the window.

estimatedOfferedRequests.description: Deprecated compatibility alias for modeledOfferedRequests. This value is an estimate, never an observed request count.

modeledOfferedRequests.description: Offered request total modeled from goodput and error rate when no aggregate original-client denominator exists. This is an estimate, not an observed request count.

successfulRequests.description: Successful request total (goodput × duration) over the window.

modeledShedRequests.description: Requests explicitly shed by modeled capacity limits over the window; null when not evidenced.

observedOfferedLoadRps.description: Observed original-client offered load rate for the window.

estimatedOfferedLoadRps.description: Deprecated compatibility alias for modeledOfferedLoadRps. This value is an estimate, never observed offered load.

modeledOfferedLoadRps.description: Offered load rate modeled from goodput and error rate when no aggregate original-client denominator exists.

successfulThroughputRps.description: Duration-weighted successful throughput/goodput rate over the window.

modeledSheddingRps.description: Duration-weighted request rate explicitly shed by modeled capacity limits.

errorRatePercent.description: Error rate in percentage points over the same request window.

recovery.description: Sustained service-health recovery evidence. Health requires positive successful service and error rate below 5% for 30 simulation seconds. A healthy blip shorter than the sustain period does not complete recovery. A later regression keeps the first recovery milestone but clears the current healthy-streak milestone until another sustained recovery; finalState becomes unhealthy and regressedAfterRecovery is true. If no incident is detected, healthy samples are baseline evidence and do not create recovery milestones.

healthErrorRateThresholdPercent.description: Strict healthy-state error-rate threshold in percent.

sustainPeriodSeconds.description: Simulation-time duration below the health threshold required to complete recovery.

incidentStartSeconds.description: Simulation-time start of the detected incident.

firstHealthyStartSeconds.description: First simulation-time instant at which the run entered the healthy threshold.

firstRecoveryCompletedSeconds.description: First sustained-recovery completion time, or null when not completed.

finalSustainedRecoveryCompletedSeconds.description: Most recent completed sustain milestone for the current healthy streak; null after a relapse until another sustain period completes.

sustainPeriodCompleted.description: Whether the 30-second healthy sustain period completed.

regressedAfterRecovery.description: Whether the run became unhealthy after a sustained recovery milestone.

finalState.description: Final observed health state at the end of the common request window.

recoveryTimeLowerBoundSeconds.description: When recovery is unobserved, at least this many simulation seconds have elapsed since the incident without sustained recovery.

estimatedServiceRestoreSeconds.description: Modeled earliest return of serving capacity (not a successful recovery or provider SLA).

assumption.description: Explains the clock and restart/promotion assumptions, not a universal cloud-provider guarantee.

EksSpotMigrationState.description: Current bounded EKS Spot interruption migration state. This evidence describes migration completion against the 120-second deadline and is separate from sustained service-health recovery.
