skuClass.description:
Primary product-class label for this allocation. Derived from the two per-dimension fields below (`computeSkuClass`, `databaseSkuClass`) using the following precedence: if `computeSkuClass` is non-default (i.e. `do-droplet`, `bare-metal-compute`, or `free-tier-compute`), that compute class is used even when a `databaseSkuClass` is also present. Otherwise the `databaseSkuClass` is used when present; the final fallback is `general-compute`.
Allocations that share the same `skuClass` are cost-comparable at the class level; allocations with different values are not directly comparable — see the parent Strategy's `crossClassNote` when present.

computeSkuClass.description:
Compute-dimension SKU class for this allocation.
`general-compute` — standard dedicated-vCPU VMs (EC2, Compute Engine, Azure VMs, OCI VM.Standard/Flex; the default when no specific compute family is set), `do-droplet` — DigitalOcean Droplets (shared-vCPU cloud VMs; different resource model and performance guarantees from dedicated-vCPU instances), `free-tier-compute` — always-free / zero-cost compute (OCI Always Free AMD micro VMs; costs excluded from estimate totals), `bare-metal-compute` — dedicated bare-metal servers (OCI BM.Standard3.64, BM.Optimized3.36; no hypervisor overhead, full core isolation).
Always present after annotation; defaults to `general-compute`.

databaseSkuClass.description:
Database-dimension SKU class for this allocation. Absent when no database service family is set (allocation carries no bespoke database tier).
`managed-rdbms` — provisioned relational databases (RDS, Cloud SQL, Azure SQL, …), `oci-heatwave` — OCI MySQL HeatWave DB System and HeatWave Analytics Cluster (in-memory analytics accelerator; distinct billing model and capability profile from standard managed-rdbms — not directly cost-comparable), `serverless-db` — pay-per-use / auto-scaling databases (Aurora Serverless, Cloud Spanner, Autonomous DB, …), `managed-nosql` — wide-column or key-value NoSQL (Bigtable SSD/HDD, …).

provider.description: Cloud provider for this allocation slice

computeCostPerHour.description: Hourly compute cost for this provider slice (USD)

databaseCostPerHour.description: Hourly database cost for this provider slice (USD)

storageCostPerHour.description: Hourly storage cost for this provider slice (USD)

egressCostPerHour.description: Hourly internet egress cost attributed to this provider slice (USD), after deducting the provider's free monthly egress allowance (converted to an hourly GB budget — ÷ 730). Free allowances: OCI 10,000 GB/month (Always Free, flat), DigitalOcean 1,000 GB/instance/month (scales with computeInstances), AWS 100 GB/month, GCP 200 GB/month (Americas), Azure 5 GB/month. Volume within the free tier produces zero. Zero also when trafficRPS is 0.

totalCostPerHour.description: Sum of compute + database + storage + egress costs for this slice (USD)

computeInstances.description: Number of compute instances in this provider slice

databaseInstances.description: Number of database instances in this provider slice

storageGB.description: Total storage provisioned in this provider slice (GB)

computeUnitRate.description: Per-instance hourly compute rate used for this slice (USD/hr)

databaseUnitRate.description: Per-instance hourly database rate used for this slice (USD/hr)

storageUnitRate.description: Per-GB storage rate used (USD/GB/hr, on a per-1000-GB basis)

egressFreeTierExhaustedAtRPS.description: The requests-per-second (RPS) threshold at which this provider's hourly egress free-tier allowance is fully consumed, given the current traffic share and instance count. Below this value egressCostPerHour is $0; above it the overage rate applies. Computed as Math.round(freeHourlyGB / (RPS_TO_GB_PER_HOUR × share)), where RPS_TO_GB_PER_HOUR = 0.0072 and freeHourlyGB = monthlyFreeGB / 730 (DigitalOcean scales by computeInstances). Omitted when trafficPercentage is 0 or when the provider has no free egress allowance.

databaseServiceFamily.description: Database product sub-family override applied to this slice (e.g. "cloud-sql", "aurora-serverless", "autonomous-db"). Absent when the provider's default managed database rate is used.

totalCostPerHour.description: Total hourly cost across all providers

vendorLockInScore.description: Vendor lock-in score (0-100, higher = more locked in / harder to migrate away). Single-provider strategies score 55-84 depending on service proprietary-ness (Aurora Serverless scores higher than standard RDS); multi-provider strategies score 20-50 depending on traffic distribution and provider count.

dataPortabilityScore.description: Data portability score (0-100, higher = more portable)

migrationEgressCost.description: One-time data-migration egress cost estimate (USD) — the cost of moving the workload's stored data out of the source provider. Computed as `EGRESS_PER_GB_RATES[sourceProvider] × storageGB`. Always present; zero-valued strategies have zero storage in the workload profile.

egressCostPerHour.description: Estimated ongoing internet egress cost per hour (USD) — the recurring cost of serving outbound responses to external users. Derived from `trafficRPS` using a 2 KB average response payload (RPS × 3600 s/hr × 0.000002 GB/request) and each provider's `INTERNET_EGRESS_RATES` overage rate (USD/GB), after deducting each provider's free monthly egress allowance (converted to an hourly GB budget): OCI 10,000 GB/month (Always Free, flat), DigitalOcean 1,000 GB/instance/month (scales with computeInstances), AWS 100 GB/month, GCP 200 GB/month (Americas), Azure 5 GB/month. For multi-provider strategies the cost is traffic-share-weighted across all allocations. This estimate is added into `totalCostPerHour` so rankings reflect the full ongoing cost including egress. Absent only on strategies with zero traffic. Volume within a provider's free tier produces `egressCostPerHour: 0`.

latencyHeadroomPct.description: How far below the user's latency SLO this strategy sits, expressed as a percentage of the SLO limit. Computed as max(0, (SLO − p95LatencyMs) / SLO × 100). A value of 13.75 means p95 latency is 13.75% below the SLO limit — the strategy has that much buffer before it would breach the target. 0 means the strategy is at or above the SLO limit. Absent for strategies that exceed the SLO.

Strategy.description: A flight-simulator-style planning estimate for a specific multi-cloud deployment configuration. Cost and latency figures reflect baseline on-demand rates under typical load and are **not actual billing data**. Internet egress is estimated and included in `totalCostPerHour` via the `egressCostPerHour` field in each `costBreakdown` entry, after deducting each provider's free monthly egress allowance (OCI 10,000 GB/month, DigitalOcean 1,000 GB/instance/month, AWS 100 GB/month, GCP 200 GB/month, Azure 5 GB/month). Still excluded: monitoring/support surcharges, non-egress free-tier credits, reserved-instance discounts, and spot/preemptible pricing. Allocations with different `skuClass` values are not directly cost-comparable; the `crossClassNote` field explains any such mix. Validate top candidates by materialising them as owned simulations before making infrastructure commitments.

suggestedResources.description: Materializable SKU objects for each resource type in this strategy. Each entry identifies the canonical instance size, unit count, and per-unit hourly rate so consumers can pre-populate infrastructure manifests or compare costs directly.

crossClassNote.description: Present only when this strategy's allocations span more than one class in either the compute dimension (comparing `computeSkuClass` values) or the database dimension (comparing `databaseSkuClass` values). Each dimension is evaluated independently so a compute-tier mismatch is never masked by a shared database tier, and vice-versa. The note names the mismatched dimension(s) and warns that cost and latency figures across those allocations may not be directly comparable because they model different product tiers. Absent when all allocations share the same class in both dimensions.
crossClassNote.example: This strategy mixes non-equivalent compute product tiers (bare-metal-compute, general-compute). Cost and latency estimates may not be directly comparable across allocations; validate each provider's tier independently before committing.

costBreakdown.description: Per-provider cost breakdown for this strategy. One entry per provider allocation, each showing compute, database, storage, and egress costs attributed to that provider's slice of the workload. `egressCostPerHour` in each entry reflects the overage cost after deducting the provider's free monthly egress allowance (see `ProviderCostBreakdown`). `totalCostPerHour` in each entry is the sum of all four line items for that slice.

CompletedResilienceEvidence.description: Caller-attested completed test report for the exact candidateFingerprint. Recorded means observations recorded during the test, not externally verified production evidence. Estimated reports remain unevaluated for deployment gating.

errorBudgetPct.description: Optional explicit error budget percentage, replacing the exploration error-budget check for this evaluation only.

PreProvisionVerdict.description: Conservative machine-readable verdict for the highest-ranked returned strategy. Exploration alone cannot return ship. The verdict endpoint can return ship when cost, latency, error-budget and recorded caller-attested resilience checks all pass. This is a planning decision, not independent verification or a production guarantee.

decision.description: hold means a known supplied budget or latency requirement failed, or no candidate is available. ship_with_changes means the visible checks have no known failure but evidence or explicit budgets are missing. ship requires every required check to pass.

candidateFingerprint.description: SHA-256 identity of the candidate ID, allocations, suggested resources and workload. Retain with test inputs; null when no candidate exists.

awsThresholdOptimizationWebhook.summary: AWS — EC2 Auto Scaling threshold optimization completed (Black Friday)

recommendations.title: Lower CPU scale-out threshold to 70%
recommendations.description: Triggering scale-out at 70% CPU instead of 80% gives 60–90 seconds of lead time before saturation under the Black Friday ramp
recommendations.action: Set scaleOutCpuThreshold to 70 in the EC2 Auto Scaling policy
recommendations.expectedImpact: Reduces peak CPU from 81% to ~68%, drops error rate from 0.4% to <0.1%

recommendations.title: Keep scale-in threshold at 30% to avoid flapping
recommendations.description: A conservative scale-in threshold prevents the Auto Scaling group from terminating instances too quickly after the Black Friday peak, avoiding a secondary spike during wind-down
recommendations.action: Set scaleInCpuThreshold to 30 in the EC2 Auto Scaling policy
recommendations.expectedImpact: Eliminates post-peak scale-in flap; saves one unnecessary scale-out cycle during wind-down

gcpThresholdOptimizationWebhook.summary: GCP — Cloud Run threshold optimization completed (Holiday seasonal burst)

recommendations.title: Set CPU scale-out threshold to 60% to prevent concurrency saturation
recommendations.description: Cloud Run saturates when per-instance concurrency fills before CPU-based scale-out fires. Triggering at 60% CPU ensures new instances are warm before the holiday ramp overwhelms the active pool
recommendations.action: Configure Cloud Run --cpu-throttling and set Knative autoscaling target annotation to 60
recommendations.expectedImpact: Peak error rate drops from 12.1% to <0.5%; p95 latency drops from 310 ms to ~58 ms

recommendations.title: Set minimum instances to 3 to eliminate cold-start lag
recommendations.description: Keeping 3 instances warm prevents the 45-second scale-out delay at ramp start that causes early-stage errors before the optimizer thresholds can take effect
recommendations.action: Set --min-instances=3 on the Cloud Run service revision
recommendations.expectedImpact: Removes cold-start lag; threshold optimizer can respond within 5 s instead of 45 s

azureThresholdOptimizationWebhook.summary: Azure — AKS HPA threshold optimization completed (product launch spike)

recommendations.title: Lower HPA CPU target to 60%
recommendations.description: Scaling out at 60% CPU instead of 75% gives the AKS node pool an extra 45 seconds of lead time for the product launch spike, eliminating the brief 110 ms latency overshoot at step 21
recommendations.expectedImpact: Eliminates p95 latency spike at launch; steady-state p95 drops from 62 ms to 48 ms

recommendations.title: Set cooldown to 120 s to prevent HPA thrashing during sustained load
recommendations.description: The product launch pattern holds elevated traffic for 50 steps — a 120-second cooldown prevents the HPA from scale-in oscillations during the sustained period
recommendations.expectedImpact: Eliminates 3 unnecessary scale-in/scale-out cycles during the sustained traffic window

ociThresholdOptimizationWebhook.summary: OCI — VM.Standard.E4.Flex threshold optimization completed (month-end batch)

recommendations.title: Set scale-out CPU threshold to 65% for the batch window
recommendations.description: Month-end batch load ramps gradually over 35 steps — triggering at 65% CPU provides a 2-instance buffer before peak query load hits, keeping ATP connection pool below 60%
recommendations.action: Update OCI Autoscaling policy CPU threshold to 65% for the VM.Standard.E4.Flex instance pool
recommendations.expectedImpact: Peak CPU drops from 72% to ~63%; ATP connection pool pressure drops from 74% to ~58%

recommendations.title: Use a 300-second cooldown to prevent premature scale-in mid-batch

MultiCloudWebhookPayload.description: Webhook payload sent when a multi-cloud exploration job completes

error.description: Error message if status is failed

RLEpisodeWebhookPayload.description: Webhook payload sent when an RL training episode completes

sim_time_human.description: Human-readable simulated elapsed time at episode completion (e.g. "1h 0m")

ResilienceRetryPolicy.description:
Per-dependency retry policy. Controls how many times a failed request is
retried, the back-off shape, jitter, and per-call timeout. Retry budgets
(`retryBudgetRatio` / `retryBudgetRps`) cap the total retry RPS produced
by this dependency so cascading retry storms are bounded.

maxRetries.description: Maximum retry attempts per original request (0 = no retries).

backoffMs.description: Initial back-off delay in milliseconds before the first retry.

backoffMultiplier.description: Exponential multiplier applied to backoffMs on each retry attempt.

jitterRatio.description: Fraction of the computed delay added as random jitter (0 = no jitter, 1 = full jitter).

timeoutMs.description: Per-request timeout in milliseconds. Requests that exceed this are counted as failures.

retryBudgetRatio.description: Retry budget as a multiple of the original RPS. Retry RPS is capped at `retryBudgetRatio × originalRps`. Set to 0 to disable retries entirely even when maxRetries > 0.

retryBudgetRps.description: Absolute retry RPS cap (takes precedence over retryBudgetRatio when both are set and the ratio-derived cap would be higher). Use to impose a hard ceiling on retry amplification regardless of traffic scale.

retryActorId.description: Optional stable identifier for the actor producing this edge's retries (for example, a gateway or client).

ResilienceCircuitBreaker.description: Circuit-breaker configuration for one dependency edge.

enabled.description: Whether the circuit breaker is active for this dependency.

failureRateThreshold.description: Fraction of requests that must fail before the breaker opens (0.5 = 50%).

minimumRequests.description: Minimum requests in the measurement window before the failure rate is evaluated.

openSteps.description: Number of simulation steps the breaker stays open before transitioning to half-open.

halfOpenMaxRequests.description: Max probe requests allowed through while the breaker is half-open.

ResilienceProtection.description: Load-protection mechanisms for a dependency edge.

rateLimitRps.description: Hard RPS ceiling applied to this dependency. Requests above the limit are shed immediately (counted in `shedRps`). Absent means no rate limit.

loadShedding.description: When true, requests beyond the dependency's capacity are shed rather than queued. Enables graceful degradation under overload.

ResilienceCapacityConstraint.description: Capacity model for a dependency's target resource endpoint.

maxRps.description: Peak RPS the target can sustain before requests overflow.

maxConcurrent.description: Maximum concurrent in-flight requests the target can hold.

meanServiceTimeMs.description: Average time (ms) the target takes to process one request. Drives Little's Law concurrency pressure.

ResilienceScalingPolicy.description:
Generic capacity/autoscaling policy for a dependency. `constrainedMetric`
describes the resource that can saturate while `observationMetric` describes
what the policy actually watches; they may intentionally differ to model an
autoscaling blind spot.

observedResourceId.description: Optional resource supplying source_cpu; defaults to the dependency source.

Scenario.description:
Reproducible, pre-built simulation template. Pass resources, connections,
seed, resilienceConfig, and the initial traffic preset to simulation creation.
When protectedResilienceConfig is present, use it as the mitigated policy in
a deterministic resilience comparison.

title.description: Short display title for the reusable simulation scenario.

description.description: Summary of the scenario setup and the behavior it is intended to demonstrate.

difficulty.description: Relative experience level recommended for running and interpreting the scenario.

resources.description: Resource graph instantiated when the scenario is loaded.

connections.description: Directed links between the scenario resources.

duration.description: Approximate time needed to run the scenario.

tags.description: Search and categorization labels for the scenario.

category.description: Broad scenario category used for filtering and organization.

primaryPurpose.description:
Optional explicit primary purpose. Educational means a guided concept,
chaos means an injected failure, predictive means a capacity simulation,
and optimization means a configuration comparison. Legacy rows may omit it.

seed.description: Deterministic simulation seed for repeatable scenario replays.

protectedResilienceConfig.description: Source-aligned protective policy for deterministic A/B replay.

name.description: Name for the scenario's default traffic pattern.

startTime.description: Simulation step when the pattern begins.

parameters.description: Pattern-specific traffic values such as start, end, or peak RPS.

duration.description: Duration in simulation steps, independent of startTime.

defaultLifecycleEvents.description: Deterministic lifecycle events that are part of the scenario's pre-run plan.

providerApiLimitScenario.description:
Optional preset for the separate synchronous provider API-limit simulator.
The preset is loaded into the Workspace panel, but it is not executed
automatically and does not change the simulation's /step state.

question.description: Learning question shown above the provider-limit controls.

policyId.description: Expected provider policy identifier used for provenance checks.

scopeDescription.description: Human-readable scope of the expected provider quota.

date.description: Incident date as published by the cited source.

ResilienceDependency.description:
A directed dependency edge between two resources. The engine models retry
amplification, circuit-breaker state, rate-limiting, and load-shedding across
this edge on every simulation step. Caller-set retry settings belong in this
edge's `retryPolicy` object; omitted retry-policy fields are materialized with
the documented defaults and returned as the effective configuration.

id.description: Unique identifier for this dependency within the simulation.

sourceId.description: Resource ID of the upstream (calling) service.

targetId.description: Resource ID of the downstream (called) service.

requestRatio.description: Requests sent to the target per original client request (fan-out multiplier).

authRequestsPerAttempt.description: Auth/token requests added per attempt to an auth service. Models token-refresh overhead.

authDependencyId.description:
Optional dependency edge that receives the auth/token traffic generated
by this edge. Use it to model gateway retry amplification causally
saturating a downstream token service. The referenced dependency must
exist and cannot be this dependency itself.

retryPolicy.description: Per-edge retry timeout, retry count, backoff, jitter, retry budget, and retry actor settings.

ResilienceScheduledFault.description:
A fault injected at a specific simulation step range. Must target either a
resource (`targetResourceId`) or a dependency (`dependencyId`). `endStep` must
be greater than `startStep` when provided. Duplicate `id` values within a
config are rejected.

id.description: Unique fault identifier within the resilience config.

type.description:
Fault category:
- `capacity_limit` — reduce the target's RPS ceiling to `capacityPercent`% of normal.
- `concurrency_limit` — cap concurrent in-flight requests at `maxConcurrent`.
- `latency` — add `addedLatencyMs` to every request on this path.
- `error_rate` — inject synthetic failures at `errorRate` fraction (0–1).
- `traffic_surge` — multiply original client demand on the targeted root dependency.

targetResourceId.description: Resource to fault (mutually exclusive with dependencyId; one is required).

dependencyId.description: Dependency edge to fault (mutually exclusive with targetResourceId; one is required).

startStep.description: Simulation step at which the fault activates (inclusive).

endStep.description: Simulation step at which the fault deactivates (exclusive). Omit for a permanent fault.

capacityPercent.description: Used with type=capacity_limit — target capacity reduced to this percentage of normal.

maxConcurrent.description: Used with type=concurrency_limit — max concurrent requests while the fault is active.

addedLatencyMs.description: Used with type=latency — milliseconds added to every request.

errorRate.description: Used with type=error_rate — fraction of requests that fail synthetically.

trafficMultiplier.description: Used with type=traffic_surge — multiplier applied to original client demand.

ExternalMetricsConfig.description:
Opt-in deterministic external-metric recommendation model, not KEDA controller parity.
No network calls, fallback algorithm, cooldowns, provisioning, billing changes, or
provider autoscaler changes. Capacity is a separate modeled recommendation track.
Each trigger recommends ceil(value / targetValue), clamped to the capacity bounds.
Successful triggers combine by maximum, so zero cannot cancel demand.
Samples start at step 0, have strictly increasing steps, and hold until replaced.
Evaluation uses simulation.currentTime before step advancement. Normal creation
warms up five steps; read returned currentTime before choosing sample steps.
A supplied positive currentTime restores that clock and skips creation warm-up.
The entire declared timeline is replayable: PATCH replaces the timeline and resets
its derived history; reset/clone require no hidden controller state.
drop_failed_trigger excludes errors but blocks scale-in whenever any trigger errors;
all errors produce no recommendation and retain current modeled capacity.
freeze_combined_decision retains the last all-success combined recommendation on any
error, or returns null/frozen_without_prior if none exists. initialCapacity is not
a successful recommendation. Only no_ready_endpoints may opt into a successful zero.

initialCapacity.description: Must lie between minCapacity and maxCapacity.

triggers.description: Independently identified triggers; IDs must be unique.

noReadyEndpointsAsZero.description: Converts only no_ready_endpoints to successful zero, never discovery_error or fetch_error.

currentCapacity.description: Modeled capacity before this decision; not a measured resource count.

lastSuccessfulRecommendation.description: Last combined recommendation with all triggers successful, including this step.

ResilienceConfig.description:
Dependency-resilience model for a simulation. When attached (via
`simulation.resilienceConfig`), the step engine traverses declared dependency
edges, applies retry policies and circuit-breaker state, and emits
`retryAmplificationFactor` + full `resilience` telemetry in every step response.

**Limits** (shared with the engine to prevent unbounded work):
- `dependencies`: max 64 edges
- `scheduledFaults`: max 32 faults
- `maxRetries` per dependency: max 8
- `maxCascadeDepth`: max 8
- `maxGeneratedRps`: max 500,000 RPS
- `maxStepWork`: max 2,048 work units per step

**Version:** only `version: 1` is accepted.

enabled.description: Master switch — set false to disable the resilience model without removing the config.

dependencies.description: Directed dependency edges to model. Duplicate ids are rejected.

scheduledFaults.description: Step-ranged faults to inject during the run. Duplicate ids are rejected.

scalingPolicies.description: Capacity/autoscaling policies, including intentionally mismatched observed and constrained metrics.

maxCascadeDepth.description: Maximum dependency depth the engine traverses per step (prevents O(n) blow-up on deep graphs).

maxGeneratedRps.description: Hard ceiling on combined retry-generated and auth/token RPS across all dependency edges per step.

maxStepWork.description: Maximum work-unit budget consumed per step across all dependency paths.

retryGeneratedTrafficAffectsCost.description: When true, retry-amplified RPS contributes to the cost model (more compute utilization = higher cost).

ResiliencePathMetrics.description: Per-dependency-edge metrics for one simulation step.

originalRps.description: Original (pre-retry) RPS arriving at this edge.

servedRps.description: RPS successfully served by the target.

shedRps.description: RPS dropped by rate-limiting or load-shedding.

failedRps.description: Attempt RPS that failed from capacity/queue pressure, timeout, or an application error. Excludes shed requests.

timedOutRps.description: RPS that timed out (counted against the retry budget).

authTokenRps.description: Auth/token-refresh RPS generated by this edge.

authTokenFailedRps.description: Auth/token-refresh RPS that failed on this edge.

retryAmplificationFactor.description: Per-edge retry amplification (attemptedRps / originalRps). 1.0 = no amplification.

queueDepth.description: Estimated in-flight queue depth at the target.

connectionPressure.description: Connection pressure ratio at the target (analogous to DB connection-pool pressure).

availability.description: Fraction of requests successfully served (0 = fully unavailable, 1 = fully available).

circuitState.description: Current circuit-breaker state for this edge.

saturated.description: True when the target is operating above its capacity ceiling.

activeFaultIds.description: IDs of scheduled faults currently active on this edge or its target.

ResilienceTelemetry.description:
Aggregated resilience telemetry for one simulation step — produced by the
engine when `simulation.resilienceConfig.enabled` is true. Contains both
simulation-level totals and the per-dependency `paths` array.

originalClientRps.description: Total original client RPS entering the dependency graph this step.

totalAttemptedRps.description: Original client RPS plus all retry-generated RPS. Normal service hops are not counted again.

servedRps.description: Total RPS successfully served across all edges.

shedRps.description: Total RPS shed by rate-limiting or load-shedding across all edges.

authTokenRps.description: Total auth/token-refresh RPS generated across all edges.

authTokenFailedRps.description: Total auth/token-refresh RPS that failed across all edges.

retryAmplificationFactor.description: Simulation-level retry amplification factor (totalAttemptedRps / originalClientRps). null when originalClientRps is zero (no traffic). Values > 1.0 indicate net amplification.

queueDepth.description: Peak queue depth across all dependency edges this step.

connectionPressure.description: Peak connection pressure across all dependency edges this step.

incidentOutcome.description:
Aggregate incident outcome for this step:
- `stable` — all dependencies within normal bounds; no amplification.
- `degraded` — one or more edges are saturated or failing but traffic still flows.
- `cascading` — retry amplification is propagating failures across multiple edges.
- `protected` — circuit breakers or rate limiters absorbed the failure; end-user impact limited.
- `recovered` — previously failing edges have returned to normal; circuit breakers reset.

bounded.description: True when a generated-traffic, traversal-work, or cascade-depth bound truncated model work.

truncatedWorkItems.description: Number of dependency-path work items skipped due to the maxStepWork budget ceiling.

paths.description: Per-dependency-edge metrics for this step. Bounded by maxStepWork.

capacityByResource.description:
Bounded aggregate capacity attribution, with one entry per logical dependency
resource. When values are finite, nominalCapacityRps minus
warmupCapacityLossRps (capacity reduced while members are warming) and
healthCapacityLossRps (capacity reduced by unavailable or degraded members)
equals routableCapacityRps, within rounding. Null values mean no finite
capacity ceiling is known.

retryActors.description: Retry RPS grouped by independently identified retry actor.

ResilienceCapacityAttribution.description: Aggregate capacity details for one logical resilience resource; never a per-member list.

resourceId.description: Logical resource ID used by one or more resilience dependency paths.

role.description: Whether this resource is a dependency source, target, or both.

routableCapacityRps.description: Aggregate capacity available after modeled warm-up and member health; null when no finite capacity ceiling is known.

nominalCapacityRps.description: Aggregate capacity before warm-up and member-health reductions; null when no finite capacity ceiling is known.

warmupCapacityLossRps.description: Aggregate capacity lost because fleet members are still warming up; zero means no modeled warm-up loss.

healthCapacityLossRps.description: Aggregate capacity lost because members are unavailable or degraded; zero means no modeled member-health loss.

ResilienceIncidentOutcome.description:
Stable, generic incident result for one bounded replay. It is suitable for
automated diagnosis and deterministic A/B comparisons without interpreting
browser-only copy.

retryAmplificationFactor.description: Peak attempted/original retry amplification observed during the run.

peakErrorRate.description: Peak failed-attempt percentage across modeled dependency paths.

timeToRecoverySteps.description: Steps from first active fault to recovery; null when recovery was not observed in the replay window.

cascadeContained.description: True when no step in the replay was classified as cascading.

ResilienceRunSummary.description: Aggregate statistics for one resilience replay run (baseline or mitigated).

config.description: The resilience config used for this run.

peakRetryAmplificationFactor.description: Highest per-step retryAmplificationFactor observed across the replay window. null when no steps produced traffic (zero originalClientRps throughout).

peakErrorRate.description: Peak simulation error rate (%) across all replayed steps.

peakLatencyP95.description: Peak P95 latency (ms) across all replayed steps.

totalServedRequests.description: Cumulative successfully-served requests across all replayed steps.

totalShedRequests.description: Cumulative shed (rate-limited / load-shed) requests across all replayed steps.

finalOutcome.description: Incident outcome at the last replayed step.

ResilienceComparisonRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /simulations/{simulationId}/resilience/compare`.
The baseline defaults to the simulation's current `resilienceConfig`; an
explicit `baselineConfig` overrides it. Returns 400 when neither is set.

steps.description: Number of simulation steps to replay for both runs.

baselineConfig.description: Explicit baseline resilience config. When omitted, the simulation's current `resilienceConfig` is used. Returns 400 when both are absent.

mitigatedConfig.description: The mitigated resilience config to evaluate against the baseline.

mitigatedResources.description: Alternative resource array for the mitigated run. Uses the simulation's resources when omitted.

mitigatedAutoscalingConfig.description: Optional autoscaling config override for the mitigated run.

ResilienceComparison.description:
Side-by-side comparison of baseline vs. mitigated resilience runs.
Use `delta.retryAmplificationFactor` as the headline: a negative value means
the mitigated config amplifies retries less (better). `delta.errorRate < 0`
means fewer errors. Both `baseline` and `mitigated` carry peak and cumulative
metrics plus the final incident outcome.

seed.description: RNG seed used for both replay runs (deterministic; derived from the simulation's seed and current step).

startStep.description: Simulation step at which both replay runs began.

traffic.description: Traffic level (RPS) at the start of the replay window.

delta.description:
Difference (mitigated − baseline) for key metrics. Negative values indicate
improvement (less amplification, fewer errors, lower latency). All fields
are nullable when the corresponding baseline metric is null.

retryAmplificationFactor.description: Change in peak retry amplification factor (mitigated − baseline). Negative means the mitigated config produces less retry amplification.

errorRate.description: Change in peak error rate in percentage points (mitigated − baseline). Negative = fewer errors.

latencyP95.description: Change in peak P95 latency in ms (mitigated − baseline). Negative = lower latency.

shedRequests.description: Change in total shed requests (mitigated − baseline). Negative = fewer shed requests.

ProviderApiLimitSimulationRequest.description: Caller-defined workload and client behavior for a deterministic provider API-quota simulation.

provider.description: Cloud provider whose modeled API quota policy will be applied.

region.description: Provider region used to resolve regional quota policies.

service.description: Provider service whose API operations will be simulated.

operations.description: Ordered or dependency-linked groups of provider API operations to schedule.

workerCount.description: Number of simulated workers issuing the planned operations.

maxConcurrency.description: Maximum simultaneous in-flight operations scheduled across workers.

quotaOverrides.description: Optional caller-supplied provider quota policies for this workload.

seed.description: Seed used to make randomized scheduler outcomes reproducible.

concurrency.description: Fixed simulated concurrency when a concurrency sweep is not used.

failureProbability.description: Probability that an operation encounters a modeled transient failure.

maxThrottleRate.description: Upper bound on the fraction of planned operations the scheduler may throttle.

maxEvents.description: Maximum scheduler events permitted for this request.

ProviderApiOperation.description: One provider operation group included in the simulated workload.

id.description: Unique identifier for this group and any groups that depend on it.

operation.description: Provider operation class or operation name used to select quota policies.

category.description: Service category used to resolve provider API-limit policies.

plannedCount.description: Number of operations in this group to schedule.

dependsOn.description: IDs of operation groups that must complete before this group is scheduled.

items.description: Identifier of a prerequisite operation group.

resource.description: Optional opaque resource label used to match resource-scoped quota policies.

ProviderApiConcurrencySweep.description: Optional set of concurrency levels at which to repeat the modeled workload.

items.description: A number of simultaneous in-flight operations to evaluate.

ProviderApiLatency.description:
Required modeled client-side latency inputs. These values represent
caller assumptions for the Cloud World Model scheduler, not AWS
service defaults or a live provider latency claim. When measurements
are unavailable, use the canonical baseline meanMs 40, p95Ms 80, and
timeoutMs 5000 from the provider-limit operation example.

meanMs.description: Caller-supplied mean operation latency in milliseconds.

p95Ms.description: Caller-supplied P95 operation latency in milliseconds.

jitterMs.description: Maximum modeled latency variation in milliseconds.

ProviderApiRetry.description:
Modeled caller/client retry settings, not AWS SDK or service defaults.
When omitted, the scheduler uses one attempt with no backoff and no
retryable outcomes: maxAttempts 1, baseBackoffMs 0,
maxBackoffMs 0, backoffMultiplier 2, jitterRatio 0.

concurrencyOverflow.description: Optional concurrency-ceiling overflow behavior. Absent retains the existing reject behavior; queue waits for an in-process request to finish.

operations.description:
Per-unit outcomes. Empty when the workload has more than 1,000
planned operations; use the accounting and timing summaries in
that case.

outputDetail.description:
Optional detail marker. `summary_only` is returned when more than
1,000 planned operations cause `operations` to be empty. `full`
denotes itemized operation output when explicitly present;
omission also means full itemized output.

recommendedConcurrency.description:
Deterministic recommended candidate. Null when no candidate is
supported, fully completes, and stays within maxThrottleRate.

retryable.description: Execution-protection failures must not be automatically retried.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request data — structured field-level error

Unauthorized.description: Authentication required or invalid API key

Forbidden.description: Insufficient permissions — the API key lacks the required scope

WalletAuthUnauthorized.description:
No credentials provided to a wallet-session-protected endpoint. The
response body includes a machine-readable `walletAuth` block with the
endpoints and ordered steps needed to complete EIP-191 wallet
authentication and obtain a JWT.

ApiKeyUnauthorized.description:
No credentials provided to an API-key-protected endpoint. The response
body includes a machine-readable `apiKeyAuth` block pointing to the key
creation endpoint so agents can self-serve an API key without consulting
the spec.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit exceeded — slow down requests or upgrade your API key's rate limit

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the rate-limit window resets

X402PaymentRequired.description:
Payment required — the endpoint is metered and no API key was provided.

The response body follows the [x402 v2 protocol](https://x402.org) and describes
one or more USDC payment options that the caller can select before retrying the request.
Base is always the first option and uses `X-PAYMENT`. When an `accepts` entry for Solana
is present, it is an additional USDC-SPL option that uses `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` and its
`extra.feePayer` value. The server verifies either payment through the PayAI facilitator
at `https://facilitator.payai.network`.

The `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` response header carries this entire JSON body as a
base64-encoded string for protocol-aware clients.

Call `GET /api/billing/x402/config` to retrieve the current price table and wallet
address and `paymentOptions` before constructing a payment.

error.example: Payment required. Send an X-PAYMENT header containing a signed USDC payment on Base (x402 protocol).

url.description: Full URL of the endpoint being paid for.

description.description: Human-readable description of the metered call.

amount.description: Payment amount in USDC atomic units (6-decimal integer string).

payTo.description: Recipient wallet address on the selected network.

asset.description: USDC contract or mint address on the selected network.

extra.description:
Network-specific x402 details. Solana options include
`feePayer`, the PayAI wallet that sponsors the transaction fee.

extensions.description: Optional protocol extensions (empty object in standard use).

BearerAuth.bearerFormat: API Key or Wallet Session JWT
BearerAuth.description:
API key or wallet-session JWT authentication using Bearer tokens in the Authorization header.

**How to authenticate:**
1. Create an API key using POST /api/keys
2. Include the key in the Authorization header: `Bearer cwm_live_<your_key>`
3. All RL environment endpoints require authentication

**Rate Limits:**
- Default: 1000 requests/hour per key
- Configurable per key
- Returns 429 when exceeded

UiSessionCookie.name: cwm_ui_session
UiSessionCookie.description:
HttpOnly browser-workspace session cookie issued by
`POST /api/ui/simulations`. It authorizes UI mutations for simulations
owned by that browser workspace.

x402.name: X-PAYMENT
x402.description:
x402 v2 Base micropayment option. Select the Base entry from
`GET /api/billing/x402/config` `paymentOptions`, then send its signed USDC
micro-payment in the `X-PAYMENT` header to get full access to the metered
endpoint in a single round-trip — no account, no API key, no sign-up required.

**402 → pay → retry loop:**
1. Call the endpoint without an `X-PAYMENT` header.
2. Receive a `402 Payment Required` response. The body is a
   standard JSON `PaymentRequired` object. The same payload is also
   echoed as a base64-encoded string in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`
   response header for clients that cannot access the body.
3. Decode the `PaymentRequired` body (or the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED`
   header) to read the exact `payTo` wallet,
   USDC amount, network, and facilitator URL.
4. Construct and sign the payment with your x402 client library.
5. Retry the Base request with the `X-PAYMENT` header — the server
   verifies via `https://facilitator.payai.network` and responds `200`.

**Optional Solana:** When `paymentOptions` advertises a Solana entry, callers
may instead select it and use `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`. Solana is an additional
option; use `X-PAYMENT` for the Base option shown by this security scheme.

**Discovery:** `GET /api/billing/x402/config` returns the live `payTo`
address, canonical `paymentOptions`, per-call-type USDC amounts, facilitator
URL, and the credits-per-USDC conversion rate. Always fetch this before
hardcoding any amounts or a payment header.

**Price range:** $0.0030 per 3-credit call — $0.0050 per 5-credit
call (see `x-x402-price-usdc` on each
operation for the exact amount).

**Facilitator:** `https://facilitator.payai.network` (PayAI-operated,
verifies the advertised Base and optional Solana options).

x402Solana.name: PAYMENT-SIGNATURE
x402Solana.description:
Optional x402 v2 Solana payment alternative. Use this security option only
when `GET /api/billing/x402/config` `paymentOptions` advertises a Solana
network, then send its signed Solana USDC payment payload in the
`PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` header. Include the option's `feePayer` detail when
constructing the transaction.

For the primary Base payment option, select the `x402` security option
instead and send its signed payment payload in the `X-PAYMENT` header.
